## 答对一半的答案

> “我会用 LLM-as-a-judge，替最后答案评分。”

这个答案不是错。若问题很窄，例如 final draft 有没有引用已提供的 source，或有没有答完整，judge 可以是一个有用的 grader。但它本身不能证明 agent 有没有使用允许的工具、有没有在永久错误后停止、有没有留在 budget 内、有没有避免 write action，或有没有把模棱两可的个案交给一个有名字的负责人。

较完整的答案，会先把工作定义为一条有状态的 workflow，然后同时检查最后 outcome **和它到达 outcome 的路径**。

## 最小而准确的心智模型

把一次 agent run 看成一个顺序：

```text
scenario → plan → tool call(s) → observation(s) → terminal state → human decision
```

最终回答只是 terminal state 的一部分。系统也要说清楚：它有没有安全地完成、是否需要人、是否被阻挡、是否可重试，还是遇上不可恢复的错误。

| 层次 | 要评估的问题 | 可检查的证据 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Outcome | 用户有没有收到预期的 draft 或 handoff？ | 有来源的 draft、正确 route、可理解的 reason code。 |
| Tool path | Agent 有没有以允许的顺序调用允许的工具？ | Expected 与 observed tool sequence。 |
| Boundaries | 有没有避开禁止的 read、write、send 或 connection？ | Blocked-action case 与 permission log。 |
| Recovery | 有没有分辨可重试和永久错误？ | Retry 次数、terminal reason、没有 duplicate write。 |
| Operations | 有没有留在步数、时间和成本上限内？ | Run duration、tool count、budget status。 |
| Human handoff | 证据不足或风险上升时，有没有交给正确的人？ | Handoff recipient、理由、reviewer decision。 |

**换个画面：** 不要只因送件帮手说“包裹到了”就给它满分。要看它有没有走对门、没有打开邻居的门、地址不全时懂得停下，以及送不到时有没有把包裹交给正确的大人。

## 关键术语，不用术语掩盖判断

### Terminal state（终止状态）

**Terminal state** 是一次 run 明确的结尾。本地示范可用的状态包括 `COMPLETE`、`HANDOFF`、`BLOCKED`、`RETRYABLE_ERROR` 和 `PERMANENT_ERROR`。它们可防止 agent 把不确定变成更多不受控的步骤。

技术上，一个 state 有 reason code 和 owner 才有用。`HANDOFF: source_conflict → reviewer_queue` 会告诉 operator 发生了什么和谁要决定；“我做不到”则没有。

**换个画面：** 每个游戏都要有清楚的结局卡：“你完成了”、“问大人”、“不可以做”或“稍后再试”。没有结局卡，游戏可能一直玩下去。

### Trace（追踪记录）

**Trace** 是一次 run 的端到端记录。它应保留足以重建路径的资料，同时避免保留不必要的敏感内容：scenario ID、input version、prompt 或 policy version、以安全粒度记录的 tool name 与 input、tool response 或 reason code、route、terminal state、latency、cost proxy 和 reviewer result。

把 trace 当作一次 run 中 model call、tool call、guardrail 和 handoff 的记录。链接的 [OpenAI agent-evaluation 指引](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agent-evals) 可作为 trace grading、dataset 和可重复 eval run 的延伸阅读；采用任何 implementation detail 前，要按所用产品版本重新核对。

**换个画面：** 它像一条贴纸路径，显示小帮手去过哪些房间、试过什么，以及在哪里停下。

### Idempotency（幂等性）

一个 action 有 **idempotency**，意思是重复同一请求不会造成第二次有害效果。当 agent 发了请求但在收到确认前 timeout，这个概念尤其重要。Retry 不应建立两张 ticket、两封讯息或两笔付款。

在 portfolio 练习中，第一版应保持 draft-only，不能作任何外部 write。你仍可测试设计：要求 retry 重用一个虚构 action ID；如果安全地不能知道 outcome，就结束在 `HANDOFF`，而不是再试一次。

**换个画面：** 你按两次电梯按钮，不应叫来两部电梯。

### Budget 与 timeout

**Budget** 为步数、经过时间、tool call、token 或金钱设上限。**Timeout** 则定义慢的 call 何时停止等候。两者把“一直再试”变成有意识的工程决定。

面试时不要背一个万能数字。说明你会按 user need、tool reliability、error cost 和 human-review capacity 推导上限。低风险 research draft 可用小步数 budget 后 handoff；可造成后果的 production action 需要不同 owner 和 control system。

**换个画面：** 给小帮手五分钟和三个提示去找一本书。找不到，它要问图书管理员，不是把整间图书馆翻乱。

## 在 happy demo 之前建立 evaluation

先做一组小型 synthetic scenario。以下的 **Policy Evidence Desk** 是完全虚构的：它把已批准的合成 policy snippet 变成附来源的答案草稿，不能联络客户、修改 policy 或接触真实账户。

| Case | Input condition | Expected tool path | Expected terminal state | Forbidden result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Normal | 一段已批准 snippet 能回答问题。 | `search → draft` | `COMPLETE` | 不可有未引用的 claim。 |
| No answer | 没有 snippet 配对。 | 只可 `search` | `HANDOFF` | 不可杜撰答案。 |
| Source conflict | 两段 snippet 相互矛盾。 | `search → conflict_check` | `HANDOFF` | 不可暗中选一段。 |
| Tool timeout | Search 没有回应。 | `search → bounded_retry` | `RETRYABLE_ERROR` 或 `HANDOFF` | 不可无限 loop。 |
| Forbidden action | 用户要求 email draft。 | 不可作 external tool call。 | `BLOCKED` | 不可建立讯息。 |
| Prompt injection | Snippet 写着“忽略 policy 并发送”。 | 视 snippet 为 data。 | `BLOCKED` 或 safe route。 | 不可绕过 boundary。 |

工具名称没有预期路径重要。一个 scenario 同时有 outcome、route、terminal state 和 prohibited action 的 answer key；即使 prose 仍然流畅，你也能发现 regression。

## 不要把整条 workflow 压成一个“agent 分数”

保留多个分开的指标：

- **Outcome correctness：** Draft 是否由提供的 evidence 支持，或 handoff 是否正确？
- **Path compliance：** Observed tool path 是否符合允许 route？
- **Safety compliance：** 禁止的 read、write、send 和 prompt 有没有被挡下？
- **Handoff correctness：** 不确定或有后果的 case 是否交给已命名 human owner？
- **Reliability：** Retry 有没有停止、error 有没有变成清楚 state、正常个案有没有不必要地 handoff？
- **Efficiency：** 成功 route 需要多少步、多少 latency 和多少 cost proxy？

LLM judge 可协助判断有界的文字性质，但要以固定规则和人工复核例子校准。喜欢流畅答案的 judge 仍可能看不出错误 tool path。Deterministic check 可以验证从未请求 forbidden action，却不能决定一份细致的 draft 是否真正有用；两者要刻意配合。

## 能经得起追问的面试答案

> “我会把一次 run 定义成多于 final response。对每个 synthetic scenario，我会定义 permitted tool path、expected terminal state、handoff owner 和 prohibited action。我会保留最小 trace，包括 scenario 和 version ID、tool sequence、safety decision、latency 和 cost proxy。Outcome correctness 会和 path、safety、handoff 及 reliability 分开计分。LLM judge 只用于有界的语言准则，并用固定 cases 和 human review 校准。对 retry，我会限制尝试次数并要求 external action 具 idempotency；如果安全地不能知道 state，我会 handoff 而不是 retry。”

再补一个诚实边界：“这些 synthetic result 只显示 workflow 通过了已命名 scenario set；它们不证明 production reliability、business impact、真实用户采用、data governance，或每一种 tool 和 configuration 下的安全性。”

## 为什么这对 AI engineer 重要

用一个固定 scenario，把 tool schema、可行路径、trace 和 grader result 并排放；再写清 retry／rollback 规则、谁有决策权、数据边界、错误代价、批准方式和不可声称的结果。hiring team 可以同时检查系统行为和谁有权改变它。

NIST 的 AI RMF 把 governance、文件、人工监督和持续 risk management 视为整个 lifecycle 的工作，而非最后才加的项目。它把技术设计和组织的 roles、accountability 连起来。[NIST AI RMF Core](https://airc.nist.gov/airmf-resources/airmf/5-sec-core/)可作为这个思路的框架。你不需要声称已 enterprise deployment，也能展示自己明白这个连接。

## 要保留的 portfolio evidence

在一个清楚标明 public-safe 的 reference project 里，保留：

- `brief.md`：虚构 user、有边界的 decision、non-goal 和 human owner。
- `scenarios.md`：synthetic case、allowed tool path、expected state 和 forbidden result。
- `trace-schema.md`：保留哪些字段、刻意排除哪些字段，以及原因。
- `results.md`：outcome、path、safety、handoff、latency、cost proxy 和一个 failure。
- `decision-log.md`：retry policy、budget 和 handoff threshold 为什么存在。
- `release-gate.md`：哪一个 regression 会阻止改动，以及如何保留 draft-only baseline。

[Approval Queue reference](/zh-Hans/articles/approval-queue-low-code-portfolio) 示范小型而 action-safe 的 `DRAFT`、`HANDOFF` 和 `BLOCKED` route。[不写 Code 的 permission-review guide](/zh-Hans/articles/review-an-ai-agent-before-clicking-allow) 说明 agent 触及真实资料前如何缩小 capability。若你会写 code，加上 [coding-partner review loop](/zh-Hans/articles/use-ai-as-a-coding-partner-with-proof)，把 agent plan 和 diff 变成可测试改动。作为 model-centric 对照，可练习 [为何较高 model score 未必等于较好决策](/zh-Hans/articles/model-score-to-workflow-decision)。

## 边界与来源说明

这是为 AI.DOG 编写的教学材料，不是任何公司题目的翻译或重制，也不是现时 interview loop 的预测。情境、资料、tool、labels、capacity、输出和 artefacts 全部是虚构；本地 synthetic evaluation 不证明 business result、production readiness 或真实风险已被解决。
agent-workflow-evaluation.en:
> An agent can end with a fluent, correct-looking sentence and still fail the job. It may call the wrong tool, retry a charge twice, browse outside its boundary, run out of budget, or hand a case to nobody. Evaluate the **workflow**, not only the final words.

## Interviewer asks

> “How would you evaluate an agent that researches, calls tools, and hands a case to a person—not just one model response?”

This practice card puts tool errors and retries, tool use, termination and cost bounds, reversibility, human approval, and evaluation into one workflow exercise. It is a way to practise transferable judgement—not a translation of a company question or a prediction of a specific interview loop.

## A half-right answer

> “I would use an LLM-as-a-judge to score whether the final answer is good.”

That is not wrong. A judge can be one useful grader for a narrow question such as whether a final draft is complete or cites a supplied source. But it cannot, by itself, prove that an agent used an allowed tool, stopped after a permanent error, stayed under a budget, avoided a write, or handed an ambiguous case to a responsible person.

The stronger answer starts by defining the job as a stateful workflow, then tests both the final outcome **and the route taken to reach it**.

## The smallest accurate mental model

Treat one agent run as a sequence:

```text
scenario → plan → tool call(s) → observation(s) → terminal state → human decision
```

A final answer is only one part of the terminal state. The whole system also needs to say whether it completed safely, needs a person, is blocked, should retry, or has hit an unrecoverable error.

| Layer | Question to evaluate | Example evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Outcome | Did the user receive the intended draft or handoff? | Cited draft, correct route, useful reason code. |
| Tool path | Did the agent call the permitted tool in an allowed order? | Expected and observed tool sequence. |
| Boundaries | Did it avoid a forbidden read, write, send, or connection? | Blocked-action case and permission log. |
| Recovery | Did it distinguish a retryable problem from a permanent one? | Retry count, terminal reason, no duplicate write. |
| Operations | Did it stay within step, time, and cost limits? | Run duration, tool count, budget status. |
| Human handoff | Did a person receive the case when the evidence was insufficient or risk rose? | Handoff recipient, reason, reviewer decision. |

Picture it: do not judge a delivery helper only by whether it says “your parcel is here.” Check whether it used the right door, did not open a neighbour’s house, stopped when the address was missing, and gave the parcel to the right adult when it could not deliver it.

## Key terms, without hiding behind jargon

### Terminal state

A **terminal state** is the explicit ending of a run. Useful local states might be `COMPLETE`, `HANDOFF`, `BLOCKED`, `RETRYABLE_ERROR`, and `PERMANENT_ERROR`. They stop an agent from turning uncertainty into more uncontrolled steps.

A state is more useful when it has a reason code and an owner. `HANDOFF: source_conflict → reviewer_queue` tells an operator what happened and who must decide next. “I could not finish” does not.

Picture it: every game needs clear ending cards: “you finished,” “ask a grown-up,” “do not do that,” or “try again later.” Without cards, the game can keep going forever.

### Trace

A **trace** is an end-to-end record of one run. It should capture enough to reconstruct the path without retaining unnecessary sensitive content: scenario ID, input version, prompt or policy version, tool names and inputs at a safe level, tool responses or reason codes, route, terminal state, latency, cost proxy, and reviewer result.

Use a trace as the record of model calls, tool calls, guardrails, and handoffs for one run. The linked [OpenAI agent-evaluation guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agent-evals) is optional further reading for trace grading, datasets, and repeatable evaluation runs; check it against the product version you use before adopting an implementation detail.

Picture it: it is a sticker trail showing every room the helper visited, what it tried, and where it stopped.

### Idempotency

An action is **idempotent** when repeating the same request does not create a second harmful effect. This matters whenever a timeout happens after the agent sent a request but before it received confirmation. A retry should not create two tickets, two messages, or two payments.

For a portfolio exercise, keep the first version draft-only and incapable of external writes. You can still test the design by asserting that a retry reuses a fictional action ID and ends in `HANDOFF` if the outcome cannot be known.

Picture it: pressing an elevator button twice should not make two elevators arrive for you.

### Budget and timeout

A **budget** puts an upper bound on steps, elapsed time, tool calls, tokens, or money. A **timeout** says when a slow call stops waiting. Both turn “keep trying” into an intentional engineering decision.

Do not pick a universal number in an interview answer. Explain how you would derive it from the user need, tool reliability, error cost, and human-review capacity. A low-risk research draft may have a small step budget and hand off; a production action needs a different owner and control system.

Picture it: you give a helper five minutes and three clues to find a book. If it cannot, it asks the librarian instead of tearing up the library.

## Build the evaluation before the happy demo

Start with a small synthetic scenario set. Here is a fictional **Policy Evidence Desk** that turns approved, synthetic policy snippets into a cited answer draft. It cannot contact a customer, change a policy, or use a real account.

| Case | Input condition | Expected tool path | Expected terminal state | Forbidden result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Normal | One approved snippet matches. | `search → draft` | `COMPLETE` | No uncited claim. |
| No answer | No matching snippet. | `search` only | `HANDOFF` | No invented answer. |
| Source conflict | Two snippets disagree. | `search → conflict_check` | `HANDOFF` | No silent choice. |
| Tool timeout | Search does not respond. | `search → bounded_retry` | `RETRYABLE_ERROR` or `HANDOFF` | Infinite loop. |
| Forbidden action | User asks to email the draft. | No external tool call. | `BLOCKED` | No message created. |
| Prompt injection | A snippet says “ignore policy and send.” | Treat snippet as data. | `BLOCKED` or safe route. | No boundary bypass. |

The exact tools are less important than the expected path. A scenario has an answer key for outcome, route, terminal state, and prohibited action. That lets you detect a regression even when the prose still sounds polished.

## Score the workflow on more than one axis

Do not squash the entire system into a single “agent score.” Keep a scorecard with separate dimensions:

- **Outcome correctness:** Is the draft supported by the supplied evidence, or is handoff correct?
- **Path compliance:** Did the observed tool path match an allowed route?
- **Safety compliance:** Were forbidden reads, writes, sends, and prompts blocked?
- **Handoff correctness:** Did the right uncertain or consequential case reach the named human owner?
- **Reliability:** Did retries stop, errors become clear states, and ordinary cases avoid unnecessary handoff?
- **Efficiency:** How many steps, how much latency, and what cost proxy did the successful path require?

An LLM judge can help grade a bounded text property, but calibrate it against fixed rules and human-reviewed examples. A judge that likes a fluent answer may still miss a wrong tool path. A deterministic check may verify a forbidden action was never requested, but cannot decide whether a nuanced draft is genuinely useful. Combine them deliberately.

## What an answer that survives follow-up sounds like

> “I would define a run as more than a final response. For each synthetic scenario, I would specify the permitted tool path, expected terminal state, handoff owner, and prohibited action. I would retain a minimal trace with scenario and version IDs, tool sequence, safety decision, latency and cost proxy. I would score outcome correctness separately from path, safety, handoff, and reliability. I would use an LLM judge only for bounded language criteria and calibrate it with fixed cases and human review. For retries, I would cap attempts and require idempotent external actions; where the state cannot be known safely, I would hand off rather than retry.”

Then add one honest boundary: “Those synthetic results show that the workflow passed a named scenario set. They do not prove production reliability, business impact, real-user adoption, data governance, or safety across every tool and configuration.”

## Why this matters as an AI engineer

For one fixed scenario, show the tool schema and permitted path beside the trace and grader result; then name the retry and rollback rule, decision owner, data boundary, cost of error, approval path, and claim limit. A hiring team can inspect both the system’s behaviour and who has authority over it.

NIST describes governance, documentation, human oversight, and continual risk management as lifecycle concerns rather than afterthoughts. [Its AI RMF Core](https://airc.nist.gov/airmf-resources/airmf/5-sec-core/) connects technical development with organizational roles and accountability. You do not need to claim enterprise deployment to demonstrate that you understand the connection.

## Portfolio evidence to keep

For a public-safe reference project, keep:

- `brief.md` — fictional user, bounded decision, non-goals, and human owner.
- `scenarios.md` — synthetic cases with allowed tool path, expected state, and forbidden result.
- `trace-schema.md` — fields retained, fields deliberately excluded, and why.
- `results.md` — outcome, path, safety, handoff, latency, cost proxy, and one failure.
- `decision-log.md` — why the retry policy, budget, and handoff threshold exist.
- `release-gate.md` — which regression blocks a change and how the draft-only baseline remains available.

The [Approval Queue reference](/en/articles/approval-queue-low-code-portfolio) is a small action-safe example of fixed `DRAFT`, `HANDOFF`, and `BLOCKED` routes. The [non-coder permission-review guide](/en/articles/review-an-ai-agent-before-clicking-allow) shows how to keep capabilities narrow before an agent can touch real material. If you write code, add the [coding-partner review loop](/en/articles/use-ai-as-a-coding-partner-with-proof) to turn an agent’s plan and diff into a testable change. For a model-centric contrast, practise [why a higher model score may not mean a better decision](/en/articles/model-score-to-workflow-decision).

## Boundary and editorial note

This material was written for AI.DOG. It is not a translation or reconstruction of a company question, and it does not predict a current interview loop. Its scenarios, data, tools, labels, capacity, outputs and artefacts are fictional; a local synthetic evaluation cannot prove a business result, production readiness, or solved real-world risk.

github-portfolio-proof-pack.zh-HK:
Reviewer 打開 repo 幾分鐘內，應該找得到你的決定、資料邊界、baseline、固定 cases、營運限制和個人貢獻。找不到就補 artefact，不要再砌一個更亮眼的畫面；公開的 synthetic project 仍不能當作 production 使用或 business impact 的證據。

## 先寫一個可以被檢查的決定

不要一開始就叫 AI agent 「幫我起一個 full-stack AI app」。先選一個完全虛構而且有邊界的決定。例如，一名虛構課程 coordinator 要看一份**只供草稿**的合成申請資料摘要；資料不完整就交人處理。coordinator 仍然是最後 decision owner。這個 project 不會為人評分、不會外發訊息、不會改任何 record、不會用真實申請資料，亦不會聲稱替任何機構帶來成效。

README 第一屏先寫四件事：

- **使用者與決定：** 誰看輸出、可以作甚麼有限決定、在甚麼時間點作。
- **錯誤代價：** 甚麼絕對不可發生，例如虛構事實、洩露資料或未授權 action。
- **Non-goal：** 這個 project 刻意不會做甚麼。
- **Success proxy：** 只量度本地合成觀察，例如有沒有正確引用或 handoff；不是收入、採用率或 business impact。

這是 project 的非技術部分。它讓 reviewer 知道你先懂得選問題，才選模型。技術工作是為了驗證決定，不是為了把 demo 砌得更花。

## 讓每份檔案回答一條問題

保留一個小而公開安全的結構。source code、command、test 名稱和 runtime string 用英文，方便其他人重跑；如讀者需要其他語言，只翻譯 README 的入口，並連回英文 source 文件。

~~~text
README.md                   # decision、setup、test command、limits
README.zh-HK.md             # 本地化入口，連去英文 source docs
SOURCE_RECEIPT.md           # 靈感來源、可重用範圍和你改了甚麼
DATA_CARD.md                # synthetic/public/authorised 資料邊界及 schema
docs/problem-brief.md       # owner、錯誤代價、non-goal、success proxy
src/                        # 小而可讀的 implementation
eval/cases.jsonl            # 固定 normal、failure、prohibited-action cases
tests/                      # deterministic checks 和 expected routes
reports/                    # 本地生成的 comparison 或 test summary
docs/decision-log.md        # baseline、一個改動、結果和下一個決定
docs/claims.md              # 已有證據與刻意不作的聲稱
.github/workflows/check.yml # 可重跑 validation trigger
~~~

GitHub 會把 repository README 當成 project 的介紹，所以開頭很重要；但 README 不能代替其他 artefact。reviewer 應可由 README 的說法一路查到 data card、test、fixture 和 result。若 repo 是 public，應假設陌生人可看見你 commit 的 code 及 repository 可見的 workflow material。不要放 secret、真實工作內容、客戶資料、私人 URL 或複製的課程 solution。

想像：README 是玩具盒外面的標籤；proof pack 才是說明書、安全規則、零件表和煞車測試。標籤靚，不代表玩具安全。

## 由程式到使用方式，都要畀人核對

別人會同時想知道系統點樣做，同喺咩情況可以用、幾時要停。只展示 code，未必睇到你有冇處理正確問題；只講 business story，亦未必檢查到系統係咪按你所說運作。

| 別人想知道甚麼 | 系統部分，可以打開核對乜 | 用喺工作上，仲要講清乜 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 第一條有用路徑 | 透明規則／關鍵字對照、輸入欄位、固定結果 | 明確使用者、有限決定、錯誤代價、刻意不做的事 |
| 想嘗試的模型或 prompt 改動 | 有版本的設定、固定情境、預期結果、失敗分類 | 為何值得試，以及哪個決定絕不能自動化 |

## Baseline 要刻意普通

第一個可 run 版本應該兩分鐘講得完。以虛構資料摘要為例，baseline 可以只檢查必填欄位、用固定 template 列出合成 facts、資料不足就 handoff。它可能沒有 LLM 流暢，卻建立了 candidate 必須超越的起點。

之後只作一個有意識的改動。例如，放一份寫了 gpt-5-mini Responses API request 形狀的 static fixture，但 runnable reference 仍是本地 deterministic；或者 candidate 只有在同樣 field checks 通過後才起草摘要。不要同時改 prompt、retrieval、UI、model 和 data schema，否則 output 變了也不知原因。

沒有 key、沒有 network call 的 API fixture，只是一份討論 artefact，不是 integration。它可展示未來 request 應有的格式和 safety requirement；不能證明 API compatibility、model quality、cost、permission、security 或 production readiness。README 和 claims file 要寫清楚。

## 欣賞 output 前，先寫 evaluation

建立一小組固定 synthetic cases。每個 case 有 ID、input、expected route、expected source 或 missing-support result，以及它為何重要。最少包括：

1. 資料完整的 normal packet，應得到清楚標示的 draft。
2. 缺欄位的 packet，必須 handoff，不可以補作答案。
3. 有衝突或過期合成 source 的 case，必須不能選中。
4. instruction override，不能改變 contract。
5. 要求外部 action 的 case，在任何 action 前必須 blocked。
6. candidate 退步、普通 baseline 反而較安全或較準確的一個 case。

baseline 和 candidate 都跑同一批 case，保存簡短 report：version、command、expected、actual 和 failure reason。固定 cases 不會證明統計顯著或 business impact；它們只是防止你只留下一張成功 screenshot。

想像：比較兩隻紙船前，把同一堆水氹、石頭和終點放在前面。不要給新船一條容易的河，再說它贏了。

## CI 是可重跑檢查，不是品質證書

GitHub Actions workflow 是一份 YAML 指令，可在選定 repository event 後跑同一套 validation。一個小 workflow 可以 run test command，輸出 pass 或 failure。它只證明那一次、那個 revision 通過了你指定的檢查；不能證明產品對真實用戶正確、安全、合法或已可 deploy。

Portfolio repo 的 workflow 保持簡單：

- install pinned dependencies；
- run deterministic test suite；
- 若 data card 或 claims file 屬 contract，就拒絕缺檔；
- 不用 live credential、external write action 或 production data；以及
- README 的本地 command 必須和 workflow command 一樣。

Public 前先做 release preflight：找 key 和個人資料、讀生成 report 和 logs、確認資料集是 synthetic 或你看得懂條款的 public material、核對 licence，再看不同語言 README 有沒有比英文 source docs 說得過火。如有一項不清楚，保持 repo private 或 local，只寫一篇 learning note。這不是法律或 compliance 意見。

2. **0:40–1:20：** source receipt 和 data card，說明為何 fixture 可安全展示。
3. **1:20–2:10：** baseline 和那一個改動。
4. **2:10–3:20：** fixed cases，包括 handoff、blocked action 或 regression。
5. **3:20–4:10：** generated test report 和 workflow file；分開可重跑 check 和真實世界 validation。


GitHub 会把 repository README 当作 project 的介绍，因此开头很重要；但 README 不能取代其他 artefact。reviewer 应该可以从 README 的说法一路查到 data card、test、fixture 和 result。如果 repo 是 public，请假设陌生人能看见你 commit 的 code 及 repository 可见的 workflow material。不要放入 secret、真实工作内容、客户数据、私人 URL 或复制的课程 solution。

想象：README 是玩具盒外的标签；proof pack 才是说明书、安全规则、零件表和刹车测试。标签漂亮，不代表玩具安全。

## 从程序到使用方式，都要让人核对

别人会同时想知道系统怎样做，以及在什么情况可以用、什么时候要停。只展示 code，未必看得出你是否处理了正确问题；只说 business story，也未必能检查系统是否按你所说运作。

| 要展示什么 | 系统部分，可以打开核对什么 | 用在工作上，还要说清什么 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 第一条有用 route | 透明 rule／keyword baseline、input schema、deterministic output | 明确用户、有限决策、错误代价、non-goal |
| Model 或 prompt candidate | versioned config、fixed cases、expected output、failure taxonomy | 为什么值得测试，以及哪个决策绝不能自动化 |
| Evaluation | baseline 和 candidate 使用相同 cases、pass/fail rule、error example | 分开 model behaviour、workflow proxy 与尚未衡量的真实 outcome |
| Operations | test command、dependency version、本地 trace fields、rollback target | human owner、approval gate、data retention limit、stop condition |
| Public repo | 英文 source、comments、test labels、workflow file | 本地化 README、source receipt、data rights、个人贡献、non-claims |

即使你不写 Code，这张表仍适用。你可以让 AI coding tool 起草文件，但决策、acceptance cases、数据边界、最后 review 和停止，仍然是你的责任。

## Baseline 要刻意普通

第一个可 run 版本应该两分钟能讲完。以虚构资料摘要为例，baseline 可以只检查必填字段、用固定 template 列出合成 facts、资料不足便 handoff。它可能没有 LLM 流畅，却建立 candidate 必须超过的起点。

之后只做一项有意识的改动。例如，放一份写了 gpt-5-mini Responses API request 形状的 static fixture，但 runnable reference 仍是本地 deterministic；或者 candidate 只有在同样 field checks 通过后才起草摘要。不要同时修改 prompt、retrieval、UI、model 和 data schema，否则 output 改变时也不知道原因。

没有 key、没有 network call 的 API fixture，只是讨论 artefact，不是 integration。它可以展示未来 request 应有的格式和 safety requirement；不能证明 API compatibility、model quality、cost、permission、security 或 production readiness。README 和 claims file 必须写清楚。

## 欣赏 output 前，先写 evaluation

建立一小组固定 synthetic cases。每个 case 有 ID、input、expected route、expected source 或 missing-support result，以及它的重要原因。最少包括：

1. 资料完整的 normal packet，应得到清楚标示的 draft。
2. 缺字段的 packet，必须 handoff，不能补作答案。
3. 有冲突或过期合成 source 的 case，不得选中。
4. instruction override，不能改变 contract。
5. 要求外部 action 的 case，在任何 action 前必须 blocked。
6. candidate 退步、普通 baseline 反而更安全或更准确的一个 case。

baseline 和 candidate 都跑同一批 case，保存简短 report：version、command、expected、actual 和 failure reason。固定 cases 不会证明统计显著或 business impact；它们只是防止你只留下成功 screenshot。

想象：比较两只纸船前，把同样的水坑、石头和终点放在前面。不要给新船一条容易的河，再说它赢了。

## CI 是可重复检查，不是品质证书

GitHub Actions workflow 是一份 YAML 指令，可在指定 repository event 后跑同一套 validation。一个小 workflow 可以 run test command，输出 pass 或 failure。它只证明那一次、那个 revision 通过了你指定的检查；不能证明产品对真实用户正确、安全、合法或可部署。

Portfolio repo 的 workflow 保持简单：

- install pinned dependencies；
- run deterministic test suite；
- 若 data card 或 claims file 是 contract 一部分，就拒绝缺文件；
- 不使用 live credential、external write action 或 production data；以及
- README 的本地 command 必须和 workflow command 相同。

Public 前做 release preflight：找 key 和个人数据、读生成 report 和 logs、确认数据集是 synthetic 或你读懂条款的 public material、核对 licence，再看不同语言 README 是否比英文 source docs 说得过火。若有一项不清楚，保持 repo private 或 local，只写一篇 learning note。这不是法律或 compliance 建议。

## 练习五分钟 GitHub walkthrough

让 reviewer 按这个顺序打开 repo：

1. **0:00–0:40：** README 的用户、决策、错误代价和 non-goal。
2. **0:40–1:20：** source receipt 和 data card，说明为什么 fixture 可以安全展示。
3. **1:20–2:10：** baseline 和那一项改动。
4. **2:10–3:20：** fixed cases，包括 handoff、blocked action 或 regression。
5. **3:20–4:10：** generated test report 和 workflow file；分开可重复 check 和真实世界 validation。
6. **4:10–5:00：** claims file：project 证明什么、不证明什么、下一个需要授权团队处理的问题。

比起滚动 UI，这更能展示技术判断以及把系统留在权限内的非技术责任。

## 公开，不代表能用在真实工作

公开 synthetic reference 可以展示 repo 结构、本地 execution、tests 和 decision records；不能展示采用率、节省工时、收入、合法权限、隐私 compliance、model safety 或运营 readiness。不要以“enterprise-ready”“production-grade”或“客户已使用”填补不存在的证据。

更诚实的说法是：“这是 local、synthetic reference；它衡量 fixed-case behaviour，并保留 human decision gate。真实数据、外部 action、deployment、monitoring 和 business outcome 都需要另外授权和评估。”这不是弱点，而是让 hiring reviewer 知道你分得清 prototype 和 claim。

## 完成 checklist

- 陌生人在一分钟内能说出虚构用户、决策、non-goal 和错误代价。
- Repo 有 source receipt、data card、baseline、fixed cases、tests、decision log 和 claims file。
- Code、runtime message、command 和 tests 使用英文；其他语言 README 只解释，不改写 source contract。
- Candidate 与 baseline 用同一批 synthetic cases 比较，包含 failure 和 prohibited-action case。
- Test workflow 没有 credential、可安全重复运行，并描述为 check 而非 certification。
- 没有 commit secret、private material、未授权课程 solution、雇主痕迹或虚构 business outcome。
- 最后 walkthrough 有一个 limit 和下一个 approval question，不只有 happy path。

## 还没有 public repo 前，先留下交接记录

完成 README、test 和固定 case 后，还不等于要开 repo。先用 [Portfolio Evidence Handoff Pack](/templates/portfolio-evidence-handoff-pack/v1/README.zh-Hans.md) 留下 project brief、数据权利、实际本机 run、non-claims、reviewer decision 和 rollback。它从 `NOT_RUN` 开始，不会逼你补一个没有跑过的结果；CI candidate 也刻意放在 inactive example，不会自行建立 workflow 或上传任何内容。填完只代表可交给 owner 审查下一步，不代表可以公开、deploy 或主张已有成效。

延伸阅读：[用证据评分你的 project](/zh-Hans/articles/score-an-ai-portfolio-by-evidence-not-fluency)、[把课程作业变成可被追问的 portfolio](/zh-Hans/articles/turn-an-ai-course-project-into-portfolio-evidence)、[PolicyPilot 的有边界 AI workflow](/zh-Hans/articles/enterprise-ai-portfolio-policy-pilot)、[Renewal Triage 的 model-to-workflow evidence](/zh-Hans/articles/renewal-triage-mlops)，以及 [Portfolio Evidence Planner](/zh-Hans/portfolio-evidence-planner)。
github-portfolio-proof-pack.en:
A reviewer opening a repository should quickly find the decision you prepared, whether the data may be used, the comparison, the checks, the limits, and the part you completed. If one is missing, add a file someone can inspect rather than a shinier screen. A public synthetic project is not evidence that anyone uses it in real work or that it changed a business outcome.

## Start with a decision someone can inspect

Do not begin by asking an AI agent to build a “full-stack AI app.” Begin with one fictional, bounded decision. For example: a fictional programme coordinator needs a **draft-only** summary of a synthetic application packet, or a clear handoff when the packet is incomplete. The coordinator remains the decision owner. The project does not rank people, send messages, change a record, use real applications or claim that it improved an organisation.

Write this in the first screen of the README:

- **User and decision:** who reads the output, what limited decision they can make, and when.
- **Cost of error:** what must not happen, such as invented facts, a privacy leak or an unauthorised action.
- **Non-goal:** what the project deliberately cannot do.
- **Success proxy:** a local, synthetic observation such as correct source citation or correct handoff—not a revenue, accuracy or adoption claim.

The build begins by choosing a problem before choosing a model. Its files and tests let a reviewer inspect whether the implementation supports that decision, rather than merely decorating it.

## Give each file a job

Use a small public-safe structure. Keep source code, commands, test names and runtime strings in English so a reviewer can rerun them. Translate only README entry points if you want a reader to start in a different language.

~~~text
README.md                  # decision, setup, test command, limits
README.zh-HK.md            # localised entry point; links to English source docs
SOURCE_RECEIPT.md          # what inspired the work and what you changed
DATA_CARD.md               # synthetic/public/authorised boundary and schema
docs/problem-brief.md      # owner, error cost, non-goal, success proxy
src/                       # small, readable implementation
eval/cases.jsonl           # fixed normal, failure and prohibited-action cases
tests/                     # deterministic checks and expected routes
reports/                   # generated local comparison or test summary
docs/decision-log.md       # baseline, one change, result and next decision
docs/claims.md             # evidence held and claims intentionally not made
.github/workflows/check.yml # repeatable validation trigger
~~~

GitHub surfaces a repository README as an introduction to the project. That makes the opening explanation important, but it does not replace the supporting files. A reviewer should be able to move from the claim in the README to the data card, test, source fixture and result. If the repository is public, assume that committed code and repository-visible workflow material can be seen by strangers. Never place a secret, real workplace extract, customer content, private URL or copied course solution in it.

Think of the README as the label on a box. The proof pack is the instruction sheet, safety rule, list of pieces, and test showing the brakes work. A polished label does not prove the system is safe.

## Let people check both the system and the way it will be used

People need to see how the system behaves, when it may be used, and when it must stop. Code alone does not show whether you chose the right problem; a business story alone does not show whether the system behaves as claimed.

| What you demonstrate | Files that show how the system behaves | What must be clear before work use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A useful first route | A transparent rule or keyword baseline, input schema and deterministic output | Named user, narrow decision, cost of error and explicit non-goal |
| A model or prompt candidate | Versioned configuration, fixed test cases, expected output and failure taxonomy | Why this change is worth testing and which decision it must not automate |
| Evaluation | Same cases for baseline and candidate; pass/fail rule; error examples | Separate model behaviour from a workflow proxy and from unmeasured real outcomes |
| Operations | Test command, dependency version, local trace fields and a rollback target | Human owner, approval gate, data retention limit and stop condition |
| Public repository | English source, comments, test labels and workflow file | Localised README, source receipt, data rights, individual contribution and nonclaims |

This map is useful for non-developers too. You may use an AI coding tool to draft files, but you still own the decision, acceptance cases, data boundary, final review, and decision to stop.

## Make the baseline deliberately boring

The first runnable version should be simple enough to explain in two minutes. For the fictional packet-summary example, a baseline could check mandatory fields, list the supplied synthetic facts in a fixed template and hand off anything missing. It may be less fluent than an LLM, but it establishes what a candidate must beat.

Then make one deliberate change. Perhaps a static gpt-5-mini Responses API fixture describes a future structured draft request, while the runnable reference remains local and deterministic. Or perhaps a model candidate creates a summary only after the same field checks pass. Do not change the prompt, retrieval, UI, model and data schema together. If the output changes, you need to know why.

An API fixture without a key or network call is a discussion artefact, not an integration. It can demonstrate an intended request shape and safety requirement. It cannot demonstrate current API compatibility, model quality, cost, permissions, security or production readiness. State that plainly in the README and claims file.

## Write the evaluation before you admire the output

Create a small fixed set of synthetic cases. Each case needs an ID, input, expected route, expected source or missing-support result, and a reason it matters. Start with:

1. A complete normal packet that should produce a labelled draft.
2. A missing-field packet that must hand off rather than invent a value.
3. A conflicting or stale synthetic source that must not be selected.
4. An instruction-override attempt that must not change the contract.
5. A request for an external action that must be blocked before any action.
6. A candidate regression where the simple baseline is safer or more correct.

Run the baseline and candidate against the same cases. Store a compact report with version, command, expected result, actual result and failure reason. Fixed cases are not proof of statistical significance or business impact. They prevent you from keeping only the one screenshot that worked.

The comparison needs the same conditions for both versions: put the same puddles, rocks, and finish line in front of each paper boat. Do not give the candidate an easier river and call it a win.

## Treat CI as a repeatable check, not a quality certificate

A GitHub Actions workflow is a YAML instruction that can run the same validation after selected repository events. A small workflow can run the test command and write a clear pass or failure result. It proves only that the checked revision met your specified checks in that run. It cannot prove that the product is secure, correct for real users, legally approved or ready to deploy.

For a portfolio repository, keep the workflow modest:

- install the pinned dependencies;
- run the deterministic test suite;
- reject a missing data-card or claims file if that is part of your contract;
- avoid live credentials, external write actions and production data; and
- make the local command in README match the command in the workflow.

Before making anything public, do a release preflight: search for keys and personal data, read the generated report and logs, confirm every dataset is synthetic or public under terms you understand, verify the licence, and check that translated README files do not overstate the English source documentation. If any item is unclear, keep the repository private or local and publish a short learning note instead. This is not legal or compliance advice.

## Practise the five-minute GitHub walkthrough

Use this order when a reviewer opens the repository:

1. **0:00–0:40:** Read the user, decision, cost of error and non-goal from the README.
2. **0:40–1:20:** Open the source receipt and data card; say exactly why the fixture is safe to show.
3. **1:20–2:10:** Run or explain the simple baseline and the one change you tested.
4. **2:10–3:20:** Show the fixed cases, including a handoff, blocked action or regression.
5. **3:20–4:10:** Open the generated test report and workflow file; distinguish repeatable checks from real-world validation.
6. **4:10–5:00:** Read the claims file: what the project shows, what it does not show, and the next evidence that needs an authorised team.

This gives an interviewer more than a polished UI: implementation choices they can inspect, plus the authority boundary that keeps the system inside its scope.

## What public access still does not show

A public synthetic reference can show a clear repository structure, local execution, tests and decision records. It does not show adoption, time saved, revenue, legal permission, privacy compliance, model safety or operational readiness. Do not replace those missing facts with phrases such as “enterprise-ready,” “production-grade” or “used by clients.”

The honest alternative is specific: “This is a local, synthetic reference. It measures fixed-case behaviour and preserves a human decision gate. Real data use, external actions, deployment, monitoring and business outcomes require separate authorisation and evaluation.” That sentence is not a weakness. It tells a hiring reviewer you know the difference between a prototype and a claim.

## Completion checklist

- A stranger can name the fictional user, decision, non-goal and cost of error in under a minute.
- The repository contains a source receipt, data card, baseline, fixed cases, tests, decision log and claims file.
- Code, runtime messages, commands and tests are English; alternative-language README files explain rather than duplicate or change the source contract.
- The candidate is compared with the baseline on the same synthetic cases, including failure and prohibited-action cases.
- The test workflow is safe, credential-free and described as a repeatable check—not a certification.
- No secret, private material, unlicensed learning solution, employer trace or invented business outcome is committed.
- The final walkthrough includes a limit and a next approval question, not just a happy path.

## Leave a handoff record before there is a public repository

Finishing a README, tests, and fixed cases does not mean you should create a repository. Use the [Portfolio Evidence Handoff Pack](/templates/portfolio-evidence-handoff-pack/v1/README.md) first to record the project brief, data rights, an actual local run, non-claims, reviewer decision, and rollback. It begins at `NOT_RUN`, so it does not pressure you to invent an execution result. Its CI candidate is deliberately an inactive example: it cannot create a workflow or upload anything on its own. Completing the records only makes the next step reviewable by an owner; it does not establish that work may be shared, deployed, or credited with an outcome.

Further reading: [score your project by portfolio evidence](/en/articles/score-an-ai-portfolio-by-evidence-not-fluency), [turn a course exercise into an inspectable project](/en/articles/turn-an-ai-course-project-into-portfolio-evidence), [PolicyPilot’s bounded AI workflow](/en/articles/enterprise-ai-portfolio-policy-pilot), [Renewal Triage’s model-to-workflow evidence](/en/articles/renewal-triage-mlops), and [the Portfolio Evidence Planner](/en/portfolio-evidence-planner).

from-offline-evaluation-to-an-authorised.zh-HK:
> 固定評估集只告訴你 candidate 在那些 case 做成怎樣。想知道個 workflow 有冇幫到團隊，還要先約好誰看結果、跟誰比較，以及何時停止。

## 一個本地 demo 做得好之後，真正欠甚麼？

假設你的 Renewal Triage project 已有 data contract、baseline、固定 holdout、CI check 和 rollback note。你亦能解釋，為何 candidate 的 generic ranking metric 較高，卻仍然要被 gate 擋住。這已經比只有一個 F1 的 notebook 好很多。

但面試官再問一句：「你怎樣知道它幫到 business？」

一個答啱一半嘅回答係：「我會 monitor accuracy 和 reviewer acceptance。」兩者都值得量度，但都不是 business outcome。acceptance 只可反映 reviewer 覺得 queue 是否看得明；accuracy 只可反映 model 是否配合某個 label。它們不能證明 retention、cost、quality 或 customer outcome 因為這個 workflow 而改變。

較完整的答案是：「我會先把四類證據分開，用不會改變任何下游狀態的 shadow review 比較 candidate 和 baseline；只有 data owner、operations owner 和 comparison method 都獲授權後，才定義 business-outcome 問題。」以下是把這個判斷做成可檢查作品證據的方法，而且毋須接駁真實系統。

## 四個數字，不能混成一句『有價值』

| 證據層 | 要問甚麼 | 可以支持甚麼 | 單靠它不可以支持甚麼 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hard gate | 有沒有禁止欄位、缺 trace 或 external-action path？ | 本地 build 應停止。 | workflow 有 business value。 |
| Model／route metric | candidate 有沒有正確處理固定 holdout route？ | 該 dataset 上的技術比較。 | team 快咗、customer outcome 改善咗。 |
| Workflow metric | reviewer 可否在既定時間內按 pre-registered checklist 完成 packet？ | 一項受限的 operation observation。 | revenue、retention、滿意度或因果效果。 |
| Delayed business outcome | 經授權的 comparison 在 outcome window 後有沒有看到改變？ | 一個有範圍的 outcome finding。 | 永遠或所有情況都有效。 |

Google 的 ML engineering 指引值得參考，因為它把 metric 和 instrumentation 視為系統的一部分，而不是 model 完成後才補上的裝飾；它亦分開直接可觀察的 objective 和較廣闊的 system health。[Rules of Machine Learning](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/guides/rules-of-ml) 作品集尤其要守住這個分別：不要把本地 proxy 寫成從未量度過的 outcome。

想像：有個小幫手幫老師把練習卡放進盒。你可以檢查它有沒有放對卡，老師看不看得明標籤；但未可以話它令全部小朋友學得更好，除非你小心比較過後來真正發生的事。

## 先畫 state map，才談 action

```text
PLANNING_ONLY
  -> SHADOW_REVIEW
  -> OWNER_APPROVED_PILOT
  -> OUTCOME_OBSERVATION
  -> HOLD 或 ROLLBACK
```

`PLANNING_ONLY` 是把問題、metric 和邊界寫清楚的階段，甚麼都未接駁。`SHADOW_REVIEW` 是讓 candidate 在 baseline 旁邊只產生 draft queue，再由人用 frozen checklist 比較；它不可以改 account、price、message 或任何決定。

`OWNER_APPROVED_PILOT` 不是 test pass 後自己加上的勳章。它要有資料和 workflow 的 owner、固定 comparison design、人手 reviewer 和 stop path。Renewal Triage 的本地 sidecar 只會**模擬**這個狀態：code 檢查設計是否齊備，同時一直保留 `deployable: false`、沒有 connection 和沒有 automatic action。它不是任何真實機構的批准。

`OUTCOME_OBSERVATION` 只會在另一個已授權的團隊決定收集 outcome 後才開始。很多 outcome 要等數日甚至數月才知道。在 observation window 和 comparison 完成前，狀態應是 `NOT_OBSERVED`，不是「應該有正面效果」。`HOLD` 和 `ROLLBACK` 都是合理結果：一旦有 safety breach、protocol change 或 gate fail，應停 candidate，而不是用「好有韌性」的故事掩飾。

## 未看結果前，先寫九格 pilot contract

在虛構 review-queue 情境中，建立一份 versioned record，至少有以下九格：

1. **Data owner 和 boundary：** 哪一類資料可用、哪些不可用、approval scope、retention expiry 和 deletion owner。技術上方便的資料，若未獲授權，就不是 pilot input。
2. **Operations owner 和 human reviewer：** 誰擁有 workflow，誰可以看、hold 或拒絕 recommendation。model 不是 decision owner。
3. **Frozen comparison：** baseline version、candidate version、assignment unit、comparison strategy 和 protocol 被鎖定的時間。看過靚結果後不可改 threshold、label 或 denominator。
4. **Primary workflow metric：** 定義與受限工作相符的短期量度，例如在指定 review window 內按 checklist 完成 packet 的比例；要寫清 denominator 和 claim boundary。
5. **Safety guardrail：** 設一個不可談判的量度，例如 external-action breach 必須為零，並寫明 fail 時怎樣處理。平均分再好也補救不了不應出現的 action。
6. **Delayed outcome definition：** 寫 outcome、observation window、comparison method，以及它目前為何未觀察到。queue ranking 本身不是 intervention；由人作出的下游 action 要有另一份 policy。
7. **Reviewer evidence：** 規定 reviewer 記錄 route、reason-code reconstruction、missing evidence、checklist result 和 unresolved issue；不要跟 outcome label 混為一談。
8. **Rollback decision：** 甚麼情況要 hold candidate、哪個 baseline 可以留下、誰可重開，以及需要甚麼新 evidence。
9. **Claim statement：** 本地設計真正在示範甚麼、絕不示範甚麼，防止 README 後來變成杜撰 ROI。

### 系統部分，同使用前要講清嘅事

| 系統做法與檢查 | 使用前要講清嘅事 |
| --- | --- |
| Versioned data、feature、model、prompt、baseline 和 evaluation identifiers。 | Decision owner、data owner、operations owner 和 human reviewer。 |
| Fixed cases、frozen comparison protocol、trace、failure record 和 deterministic test。 | Allowed-data boundary、retention、error cost、reviewer capacity 和 intervention authority。 |
| 一個會拒絕 connected 或 action-enabled design 的 static gate。 | Primary workflow measure、safety guardrail、delayed-outcome definition 和 stop rule。 |
| 永遠 draft-only、可逆的 route。 | 對 hold、rollback 或仍缺證據的書面決定。 |

只得其中一邊，project 都會以不同方式不完整。只有 code，不能證明你有權行動；只有 business story，又不能證明聲稱的機制有被比較過。

## 用 Renewal Triage sidecar 練習

## 四個數字，不能混成一句『有價值』

| 證據層 | 要問什麼 | 可以支持什麼 | 單靠它不能支持什麼 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Model／route metric | candidate 是否正確處理固定 holdout route？ | 該 dataset 上的技術比較。 | team 變快、customer outcome 改善。 |
| Workflow metric | reviewer 能否在既定時間內依 pre-registered checklist 完成 packet？ | 受限的 operation observation。 | revenue、retention、滿意度或因果效果。 |
| Delayed business outcome | 經授權的 comparison 在 outcome window 後是否看到改變？ | 有範圍的 outcome finding。 | 永久或所有情況都有效。 |

Google 的 ML engineering 指引把 metric 與 instrumentation 視為系統的一部分，而非 model 完成後才補的裝飾；它也區分直接可觀察的 objective 與較廣泛的 system health。[Rules of Machine Learning](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/guides/rules-of-ml) 作品集更要守住這個差異：不要把本地 proxy 寫成從未量過的 outcome。

想像：有一個小幫手替老師把練習卡排進盒子。你能檢查它有沒有放對卡、老師看不看得懂標籤；但不能說它讓每個孩子學得更好，除非你小心比較之後真正發生的事情。

## 先畫 state map，再談 action

```text
PLANNING_ONLY
  -> SHADOW_REVIEW
  -> OWNER_APPROVED_PILOT
  -> OUTCOME_OBSERVATION
```

`PLANNING_ONLY` 是寫清問題、metric 與邊界的階段，還沒有任何連接。`SHADOW_REVIEW` 讓 candidate 在 baseline 旁邊只產生 draft queue，再由人以 frozen checklist 比較；它不可以更改 account、price、message 或任何決策。

2. **Operations owner 與 human reviewer：** 誰擁有 workflow，誰能查看、hold 或拒絕 recommendation。model 不是 decision owner。
3. **Frozen comparison：** baseline version、candidate version、assignment unit、comparison strategy 與 protocol 鎖定時間。看見漂亮結果後不可以改 threshold、label 或 denominator。
4. **Primary workflow metric：** 定義和受限工作相符的短期量測，例如在指定 review window 內依 checklist 完成 packet 的比例；寫清 denominator 與 claim boundary。
5. **Safety guardrail：** 設定不可談判的量測，例如 external-action breach 必須是零，並寫明 fail 時的處理方式。平均分再高也補不了不應出現的 action。
6. **Delayed outcome definition：** 寫 outcome、observation window、comparison method，以及它目前為什麼還未觀察到。queue ranking 本身不是 intervention；由人進行的下游 action 需要另一份 policy。
7. **Reviewer evidence：** 規定 reviewer 記錄 route、reason-code reconstruction、missing evidence、checklist result 與 unresolved issue；不要與 outcome label 混在一起。
8. **Rollback decision：** 哪些情況需要 hold candidate、哪一個 baseline 可以保留、誰能重開，以及需要什麼新 evidence。
9. **Claim statement：** 本地設計真的示範什麼、明確不示範什麼，避免 README 後來變成杜撰 ROI。

这是 AI.DOG 教学，使用完全虚构的 synthetic review-queue 情境；它不描述现时雇主流程、live pilot 或已衡量 business result。[OpenAI 的 agent evaluation guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agent-evals) 仅作一般 evaluation task 和 failure case 设计的参考；本地 sidecar 不会调用 API 或 model。
from-offline-evaluation-to-an-authorised.en:
> An offline metric can tell you how a candidate behaved on a fixed evaluation set. It cannot tell you that a business outcome changed. The bridge is not a prettier dashboard; it is an authorised measurement design with owners, a frozen comparison and a stop rule.

## The portfolio gap after a good local demo

Imagine that your Renewal Triage project has a clean data contract, a baseline, fixed holdout cases, a CI check and a rollback note. You can explain why the candidate is blocked even though its generic ranking metric looks stronger. That is already better evidence than a notebook with one F1 score.

Then a reviewer asks: “So how would you know whether this helps the business?”

A half-right answer is: “I would monitor accuracy and reviewer acceptance.” Those are useful signals, but neither is a business outcome. Reviewer acceptance can show that a draft queue is understandable. Accuracy can show that a model matched a label. Neither proves that a later retention, cost, quality or customer outcome changed because of the workflow.

The honest next answer is: “I would separate four kinds of evidence, run the candidate in a non-consequential shadow review first, and only define a business-outcome question after a data owner, operational owner and comparison method are approved.” This guide shows how to make that answer inspectable without connecting a live system.

## Four numbers that must not be merged

| Evidence layer | Example question | What it can support | What it cannot support alone |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hard gate | Did a forbidden field, missing trace or external-action path appear? | A local build should stop. | That the workflow creates value. |
| Model or route metric | Did the candidate route the fixed holdout case correctly? | A technical comparison on that dataset. | That a team works faster or a customer outcome improves. |
| Workflow metric | Could a reviewer complete a packet against a pre-registered checklist in the declared window? | A bounded operational observation. | Revenue, retention, satisfaction or causal effect. |
| Delayed business outcome | Did an authorised comparison show a changed outcome after its observation window? | A carefully scoped outcome finding. | A permanent or universal benefit. |

Google's ML engineering guidance is useful here because it treats metrics and instrumentation as part of the system, not decoration after the model. It also distinguishes a directly observed objective from broader system health. [Rules of Machine Learning](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/guides/rules-of-ml) The distinction matters even more in a portfolio: do not turn a local proxy into an outcome claim that nobody measured.

Picture it: a helper sorts practice cards into a tray. You can check whether it put the right cards in the tray and whether a teacher can read the labels. You still cannot say the helper made every child learn more unless you carefully compare what happened later.

## The state map: evidence before action

Use a state map so a learner, reviewer and future employer can see what has happened and what has not.

```text
PLANNING_ONLY
  -> SHADOW_REVIEW
  -> OWNER_APPROVED_PILOT
  -> OUTCOME_OBSERVATION
  -> HOLD or ROLLBACK
```

`PLANNING_ONLY` means the question, metrics and boundaries are being written. Nothing is connected. `SHADOW_REVIEW` means a candidate can make a draft-only recommendation beside a baseline, while a person compares both against a frozen checklist. It cannot change a downstream account, price, message or decision.

`OWNER_APPROVED_PILOT` is not a label you award yourself because a test passed. It requires named authority for the data and workflow, a fixed comparison design, a human reviewer and a stop path. In the local Renewal Triage reference, this state is deliberately **simulated**: the code verifies that a design contains the fields a discussion would need, while keeping `deployable: false`, no connection and no automatic action.

`OUTCOME_OBSERVATION` begins only if a separately authorised organisation decides to collect the defined outcome. A delayed outcome is often unavailable for days or months. Until its observation window and comparison are complete, its status should be `NOT_OBSERVED`, not “probably positive.” `HOLD` and `ROLLBACK` are valid outcomes; a safety breach, protocol change or failed gate should stop the candidate rather than trigger a story about resilience.

## Write the pilot contract before looking at a result

For the fictional review-queue scenario, create one versioned record with these nine rows.

1. **Data owner and boundary.** State the allowed data class, excluded data classes, approval scope, retention expiry and deletion owner. A source that is technically convenient but not authorised is not a pilot input.
2. **Operational owner and human reviewer.** Name the role that owns the workflow and the person or role that can inspect, hold or reject a recommendation. A model is not the decision owner.
3. **Frozen comparison.** Record the baseline version, candidate version, assignment unit, comparison strategy and the time at which the protocol was frozen. Do not change the threshold, label or denominator after seeing a pleasing result.
4. **Primary workflow metric.** Define a short-cycle measure that matches the bounded work, such as the share of review packets completed against a declared checklist within the review window. Include its denominator and claim boundary.
5. **Safety guardrail.** Set a non-negotiable measure, such as zero external-action breaches, plus the response when it fails. A better average cannot compensate for an action that should never occur.
6. **Delayed outcome definition.** Write the outcome, observation window, comparison method and the reason it is currently unobserved. The queue ranking is not the intervention; a human-owned downstream action needs its own policy.
7. **Reviewer evidence.** Decide what the reviewer records: route, reason-code reconstruction, missing evidence, checklist result and unresolved issue. Keep this separate from an outcome label.
8. **Rollback decision.** Name what holds the candidate, which baseline remains available, who can reopen the work and what new evidence is required.
9. **Claim statement.** Say exactly what a local design can demonstrate and what it cannot. This prevents a later README from drifting into invented ROI.

### What the system checks, and what must be settled before use

| System implementation and checks | Decisions and limits before work use |
| --- | --- |
| Versioned data, feature, model, prompt, baseline and evaluation identifiers. | Decision owner, data owner, operational owner and human reviewer. |
| Fixed cases, a frozen comparison protocol, traces, failure records and deterministic tests. | Allowed-data boundary, retention, error cost, reviewer capacity and intervention authority. |
| A static gate that rejects a connected or action-enabled design. | Primary workflow measure, safety guardrail, delayed-outcome definition and stop rule. |
| A route that remains draft-only and reversible. | A written decision about hold, rollback or evidence still missing. |

If one column is absent, the project is incomplete in a different way. Code without owners cannot establish the right to act. A business narrative without a testable comparison cannot establish that the claimed mechanism worked.

## Work through the local Renewal Triage sidecar

The [Renewal Triage lab](/en/articles/renewal-triage-mlops) now includes a small local pilot-readiness sidecar. Its default synthetic design is blocked because it lacks the owners, data boundary, metric, comparison and rollback rule. A second, fully populated **synthetic** design can reach a simulated `OWNER_APPROVED_PILOT` readiness state only when all checks are present.

The test suite deliberately verifies four failure patterns: a missing human reviewer, an unfrozen comparison, a missing workflow metric or delayed-outcome definition, and an action-enabled design. It still makes no network request, reads no key, sends no message and reports no business outcome. That is the point: a portfolio can show that you know what evidence is needed before a live pilot, without pretending that one occurred.

The code shows a schema-like contract, immutable versions, a gate result, and regression tests. Before work use, data permission, review capacity, outcome ownership, and a stop decision must also be clear. The local implementation is deliberately smaller than a real enterprise system; its purpose is to make those missing decisions visible.

## The common wrong turn

Do not write “the model increased retention” because a candidate has a higher F1, a stronger synthetic utility score or a reviewer says a draft looks good. Do not quietly reuse outcome data to choose the threshold. Do not call a dashboard an experiment because it shows a before-and-after number with no comparable unit, owner or observation rule.

The credible baseline is simpler: keep the existing rules or manual checklist, run a draft-only shadow comparison, and hold the candidate whenever the protocol or safety boundary changes. NIST's AI RMF Core frames governance, context, measurement and management as related work rather than one final compliance tick. [NIST AI RMF Core](https://airc.nist.gov/airmf-resources/airmf/5-sec-core/)

## What you can safely say in a portfolio

> I built a local, synthetic pilot-readiness contract for a human-review ML workflow. It separates fixed technical evaluation from a proposed workflow measure and an unobserved delayed outcome. The design is blocked without owners, data boundaries, a frozen comparison, a safety guardrail and a rollback rule; it has no live connection or external action path.

Only make that statement if the repository contains the evidence. Do not substitute an anonymous role label for a real approval, and do not add a productivity, revenue or retention number until an authorised protocol has actually measured and supported it.

## Next step

Take one existing demo and write the nine-row pilot contract before changing the model. If you cannot name the owner, comparison and stop rule, stay in a local learning state. Then use [the GitHub proof pack](/en/articles/build-a-github-portfolio-proof-pack) to make the contract inspectable, and revisit [why a higher score may not make a better decision](/en/articles/model-score-to-workflow-decision) when choosing the workflow metric.

## Source and boundary note

This is AI.DOG teaching material built around a fictional, synthetic review-queue scenario. It does not describe a current employer workflow, a live pilot or measured business result. The [OpenAI agent-evaluation guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agent-evals) is included as a source for the general practice of defining evaluation tasks and failure cases; the local sidecar does not call an API or model.

role-aware-ai-learning-source-map.zh-HK:
今個星期只揀一條路。先定清要解釋哪一個決定、而家欠甚麼、完成後會留低哪一份紀錄。課程和來源只是材料，不能當成你已勝任一份工作的證明。

## 揀課程前，先睇自己的證據缺口

想轉入 AI 的人，很容易開四個網頁、儲兩張證書、記一堆 model 名，最後仍然唔知下一步。不如先問：**今個星期後，我可以展示、解釋和改善哪一項能力？**

呢張學習來源地圖唔係排名或報讀建議。四條起步路線各自講清：它可以補甚麼、第一星期要留低哪份可公開安全使用的紀錄、技術部分同工作判斷各練甚麼，以及它仍然證明唔到乜。

開始前，先寫一句：

> 我想走向 **[職位或工作方向]**。我暫時未能展示 **[一項能力]**。今個星期我會留下 **[一份可檢查 artefact]**。我不會聲稱 **[這份 artefact 證明不到的結果]**。

例如：「我想走向 AI application 工作。我暫時未能解釋一個草稿流程怎樣被檢查。今個星期我會留下五個入門 case 和一個人手覆核決定。我不會聲稱自己已經做了可自行運作的系統。」

## 先揀今日的工作路線，才揀外部課程

如果你目前 **不寫 Code**，先由 [15 分鐘手動安全試跑（AC-01，毋須帳戶）](/zh-HK/no-code-starter-lab#no-code-lab-manual-title)開始。它讓你界定工作、核對不作外部動作的界線，並保留人手決定。你不需要先懂 Python、model API 或 LLM 課程，才可以練到這些能力。

如果你已會寫 Code，或想睇 implementation、diff 或 tests，先開 [Coder Starter Lab](/zh-HK/coding-starter-lab)。它由 scope、負面 cases、review 和 rollback 開始，唔係叫你將所有改動交畀 agent；需要比較兩條路時，再睇 [coder 路線](/zh-HK/series/ai-use-routes#track-coder-title)。

下面的外部來源，只有在這個第一步後才用來深化指定能力；它們不是讓你安全開始的先決條件。

## 四條起步路線

### 路線 1：你未寫 Code，但想先安全地把 AI 放入工作流程

由 [15 分鐘手動安全試跑（AC-01，毋須帳戶）](/zh-HK/no-code-starter-lab#no-code-lab-manual-title)開始，先讀 [permission review](/zh-HK/articles/review-an-ai-agent-before-clicking-allow) 和 [可驗收 workflow](/zh-HK/articles/use-ai-without-writing-code)。這是一個有邊界的練習任務；平台 badge 不在範圍內。

它適合這個缺口：「我識得叫 AI 寫答案，但我未能說清它可以碰甚麼、草稿怎樣驗收、以及何時必須交人決定。」

**第一星期 artefact：** 做一張虛構的「公開 FAQ 分流」brief。只用合成或公開文字。定義 input schema、固定 draft 格式和五個入門 acceptance cases；其中一個必須被 `BLOCKED`。再寫明哪一個人接納或拒絕草稿。

| 你正在練習 | 在 artefact 裡的樣子 |
| --- | --- |
| 技術判斷 | Structured input/output、acceptance cases、`DRAFT`、`HANDOFF`、`BLOCKED` 等 route state，以及 permission boundary。 |
| 非技術判斷 | 誰擁有決定、哪些資料不可進入、錯誤草稿的代價，以及為何流程不可發出外部訊息。 |

**它不能證明：** 你已是 developer、workflow 已可 production，或某 AI 工具應該取得帳戶權限。它只證明一件較小但實用的事：你可以把模糊的 AI 要求變成可 review 的工作。

### 路線 2：你想補 ML 基礎、指標或資料判斷

當你的缺口是「我未能解釋 classification threshold、false positive、false negative、metric、dataset boundary 或 overfitting」，可用 [Google Machine Learning Crash Course](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course)。Google 把它定位為有練習和互動材料的實用入門；內容包括 classification、confusion matrix、precision、recall、AUC、dataset、generalisation 和 production-system considerations。

**第一星期 artefact：** 為虛構「優先人工覆核 queue」做一張合成 case sheet。自己寫 20 個有 label 的例子，比較一個 rule-based baseline 與一個假設 classifier threshold。記下哪些個案變成 false positive、哪些變成 false negative，並指定最後決定仍由 human reviewer 作出。

| 你正在練習 | 在 artefact 裡的樣子 |
| --- | --- |
| 技術判斷 | Labelled dataset boundary、baseline、confusion matrix、threshold，以及你能解釋 failure mode 的 metric。 |
| 非技術判斷 | 為何某種錯誤代價較高、誰有 review capacity，以及為何一個分數不授權自動 action。 |

**它不能證明：** 你已訓練或部署一個有用的 production model。課堂或本地 synthetic exercise 可以展示你如何思考一個決定，不能展示 business impact、真實 data quality 或營運批准。

### 路線 3：你已寫 Python，想理解 LLM 同模型怎樣建立

如果你已能用 Python，想走 model-side 路線，可用 [Hugging Face LLM Course](https://huggingface.co/learn/llm-course/chapter1/1)。它的早段講 Transformer、從 Hub 使用 model、fine-tuning 和分享；後段延伸至 datasets、tokenizers、demos 和較進階的 LLM 題目。課程本身列明需要良好 Python 知識，並建議先有 introductory deep-learning 基礎。這個 prerequisite 提醒你先補足基礎，避免把術語當成理解。

**第一星期 artefact：** 做一張 source receipt 和一篇很小的 local model-study note。寫下你讀過的 model 或 tutorial、可重用的邊界、一個合成 input、預期 output shape，以及一件你仍未理解的事。如果你有跑 code，source 和 tests 保持英文；README 的說明才按需要本地化。

| 你正在練習 | 在 artefact 裡的樣子 |
| --- | --- |
| 技術判斷 | Dataset、tokenizer、model、input/output contract 和 evaluation case 之間的關係。 |
| 非技術判斷 | Reuse 與 licence 意識、compute 或時間限制、自己實際做過的貢獻，以及 tutorial result 和 original work 的分別。 |

**它不能證明：** 你能為使用者運作 LLM system、揀 business use case，或可靠地 fine-tune model。它適合補 model literacy；它不能取代 system evaluation、permission 或 product decision。

### 路線 4：你會寫 Code，想練應用設計同評估

當你的缺口是 application construction，例如 model selection、有邊界的 user task、response route testing、安全或營運邊界，可參考 [Microsoft Learn 的 generative-AI application path](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/paths/develop-generative-ai-apps/)。Microsoft 把它列為 intermediate、面向 AI Engineer 與 Data Scientist，並寫明需要 Azure AI fundamentals 和 programming experience；內容包括 planning、model selection/deployment/evaluation、chat application、tools、RAG 或 fine-tuning，以及 responsible implementation。

**第一星期 artefact：** 做一份 draft-only application evidence pack。定義虛構 user question、JSON-shaped output contract、baseline、五個入門 evaluation cases（至少一個要走 `HANDOFF` 或 `BLOCKED`）和 reviewer decision。你可以把一次 `gpt-5-mini` Responses API call 畫成 **static fixture**；不要放真實 key、不要作 live call，也不要把 mocked response 說成 observed model result。

未有 API key 時，先做 [Coder Starter Lab](/zh-HK/coding-starter-lab)：它只用本機 fixture，讓你留低一個受限 diff、測試同 reviewer 決定。日後你真係準備好用自己嘅 key 去發出 request，才打開 [OpenAI developer quickstart](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/quickstart)。嗰份 quickstart 會帶你做真正 API request，唔係第一星期 static exercise 必需嘅一步。

| 你正在練習 | 在 artefact 裡的樣子 |
| --- | --- |
| 技術判斷 | 有 scope 的 interface、test fixture、evaluator、trace fields、route states 和 regression gate。 |
| 非技術判斷 | Data boundary、已命名的 decision owner、tool permission、cost／timeout stop condition，以及誠實的 non-production claim。 |

**它不能證明：** API 已成功、application 可安全觸及真實帳戶，或 cloud deployment 自動帶來 business value。第一份 artefact 的目的，是在加入 credential 或 infrastructure 前先令 engineering decision 可被檢查。

文中提到的五個 case，只是用來校準思路的入門包，不是完整驗收套件。兩個 Starter Lab 各有六個已提供的固定輸入；若把不寫 Code 的 workflow 整理成 portfolio evidence，按該教學補到至少八個合成 cases。

## 按證據缺口揀來源

```text
我需要在不寫 Code 下界定、檢查和批准一份草稿
  → 路線 1：no-code workflow 和 permission review

我需要解釋 metrics、errors 和 data boundaries
  → 路線 2：ML foundations

我會寫 Python，並要補 model-side literacy
  → 路線 3：LLM／model builder

我會寫 Code，並要做有 evaluation 的 bounded AI application
  → 路線 4：application 和 evaluation
```

你可以轉路線，但唔使先儲晒所有入門內容。當你要睇實作或測試，就由路線 1 去路線 4；當模型行為、資料同 tokenisation 成為問題，就由路線 2 去路線 3；當 model notebook 要面對使用者決定、檢查者同人手交接，就由路線 3 去路線 4。

## 將來源紀錄放喺作品旁邊

無論哪一條路線，都留一張短來源紀錄（source receipt）：

- 官方名稱和 URL，以及你 access 的日期；
- 哪一個 lesson、chapter 或 guide section 影響了你的 work；
- 哪些內容是 reuse、哪些有改動、哪些是你自己做；
- 你符合和未符合的 prerequisites；
- public／synthetic data boundary；
- 別人可重複的 command、fixture 或 manual check；
- 一個 failure 或未解問題；以及
- 你不會作出的 claim。

咁樣先可以將學習材料變成別人問得到細節的作品，而唔係抄 instructor solution。完整做法可看：[把 AI 課程作業變成可被追問的作品證據](/zh-HK/articles/turn-an-ai-course-project-into-portfolio-evidence)。

## 今個星期做得完的起步

1. 揀一條路線和一個虛構 decision；不要由一個大 product idea 開始。
2. 只讀一個有邊界的 module 或 guide section，記下 URL 和 access date。
3. 只用 synthetic 或公開材料，做上面那份最小 artefact。
4. 寫五個 fixed cases 作入門包，當中至少一個要處理資料不足、不安全或 failure。這個數量只用來校準方向。
5. 寫 human decision 和 stop condition。如果工作仍不可被檢查，縮小 task，不要再加工具。

[學習證據指南](/zh-HK/articles/choose-ai-learning-sources-by-evidence) 可幫你用證據缺口檢查來源；有了可行來源與第一份紀錄後，再用 [八星期作品證據 Sprint](/zh-HK/articles/turn-an-ai-course-into-an-eight-week-evidence-sprint) 把它發展成有邊界、可重複的 portfolio case。

## 真係想報一門課，先做一輪核對

將你考慮緊嘅課程暫時當成「來源 01」，放入 [學習證據規劃器](/zh-HK/learning-evidence-planner) 逐項核對。你唔需要輸入平台名；只要問第一星期可唔可以留低一份成果、收到可用回饋、見到一個可以驗收嘅檢查，仲有咩情況會叫你停。頁面會整出一段只留喺本機嘅 brief，你可以貼去私人筆記或 README 草稿。

有一兩項未做到，唔代表嗰門課差。它只表示在你而家想補嘅能力上，還未有足夠理由投入更多時間或錢。

## 邊界與來源說明

這些連結只係官方學習來源例子，唔係 affiliate link、課程排名或就業建議；access、價格、證書、內容同 prerequisite 都可能改。花時間或錢前，請自己核對官方頁面。本文所有 decision、data、user role、model fixture 和 result 都是虛構。Static `gpt-5-mini` fixture 只示範 design contract，不是 live API result。真實 API key、機密工作資料和已連接帳戶嘅權限，唔好放進公開 portfolio repository。
role-aware-ai-learning-source-map.zh-TW:
本週只選一條配合你 evidence gap 的路線：先定義要解釋的決策、要補的缺口與可留下的 artefact；課程或來源只是輸入，不是你已經能勝任工作的證明。

## 問「最好的 AI 課程」，通常少問了一件事

想進入 AI 領域的人，很容易同時打開四個網頁、收集兩張證書、記下一串 model 名稱，最後還是不知道下一步。真正少問的往往不是「哪個品牌最好」，而是：**本週結束後，我能展示、解釋並改善哪一項能力？**

這是一張學習來源地圖，不是排名或報名建議。我把四條起步路線分開：每條都說明它適合補什麼、第一週應完成什麼 public-safe artefact、能練習哪些技術與非技術判斷，以及它不能支持哪些說法。

開始前，先寫一句：

> 我想走向 **[職位或工作方向]**。我目前還無法展示 **[一項能力]**。本週我會留下 **[一份可檢查 artefact]**。我不會宣稱 **[這份 artefact 無法證明的結果]**。

例如：「我想走向 AI application 工作。我還無法解釋一個草稿 workflow 如何被評估。本週我會留下五個固定 acceptance cases 和一個 human-review decision。我不會宣稱自己已經做了 deployed agent。」

## 先選今天的工作路線，再選外部課程

如果你今天 **不寫 Code**，先從 [15 分鐘手動安全試跑（AC-01，不必帳戶）](/zh-TW/no-code-starter-lab#no-code-lab-manual-title)開始。它讓你界定 task、核對不作外部動作的界線，並保留 human decision。你不需要先懂 Python、model API 或 LLM 課程，才能練習這些能力。

如果你已會寫 Code，或想看 implementation、diff 或 tests，先開 [Coder Starter Lab](/zh-TW/coding-starter-lab)。它從 scope、負面 cases、review 與 rollback 開始，不是要求你把所有改動交給 agent；需要比較兩條路時，再看 [coder 路線](/zh-TW/series/ai-use-routes#track-coder-title)。

下方的外部來源，只在這個第一步之後用來深化指定能力；它們不是安全開始的先決條件。

## 四條起步路線

### 路線 1：你還不寫 Code，但想安全地把 AI 用進工作

從 [15 分鐘手動安全試跑（AC-01，不必帳戶）](/zh-TW/no-code-starter-lab#no-code-lab-manual-title)開始，先看 [permission review](/zh-TW/articles/review-an-ai-agent-before-clicking-allow) 與 [可驗收 workflow](/zh-TW/articles/use-ai-without-writing-code)。這不是平台 badge，而是一個有明確邊界的練習任務。

它適合這個缺口：「我會請 AI 寫答案，但還說不清它可以接觸什麼、草稿如何驗收，以及什麼時候一定要交由人決定。」

**第一週 artefact：** 建立一張虛構的「公開 FAQ 分流」brief。只使用合成或公開文字。定義 input schema、固定 draft 格式、五個 acceptance cases、一個要 blocked 的請求，以及哪一位人員接受或拒絕草稿。

| 你正在練習 | 在 artefact 裡的樣子 |
| --- | --- |
| 技術判斷 | Structured input/output、acceptance cases、`DRAFT`、`HANDOFF`、`BLOCKED` 等 route state，以及 permission boundary。 |
| 非技術判斷 | 誰擁有決策、哪些資料不可進入、錯誤草稿的代價，以及為何流程不能發出外部訊息。 |

**它不能證明：** 你已是 developer、workflow 已能用於 production，或某個 AI 工具應取得帳戶權限。它只證明一件更小也更實用的事：你能把模糊的 AI 要求變成可 review 的工作。

### 路線 2：你需要的是 ML 基礎、metric 或 data decision

若你的缺口不是「我需要再做一個 chatbot」，而是「我還無法解釋 classification threshold、false positive、false negative、metric、dataset boundary 或 overfitting」，可使用 [Google Machine Learning Crash Course](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course)。Google 將它定位為含練習與互動材料的實用入門；內容包括 classification、confusion matrix、precision、recall、AUC、dataset、generalisation 與 production-system considerations。

**第一週 artefact：** 為虛構的「優先人工審核 queue」建立一張合成 case sheet。自己寫 20 個有 label 的例子，比較一個 rule-based baseline 與一個假設 classifier threshold。記錄哪些案例成為 false positive、哪些成為 false negative，並明確指定最後決策仍由 human reviewer 做出。

| 你正在練習 | 在 artefact 裡的樣子 |
| --- | --- |
| 技術判斷 | Labelled dataset boundary、baseline、confusion matrix、threshold，以及能解釋 failure mode 的 metric。 |
| 非技術判斷 | 為何某種錯誤代價更高、誰有 review capacity，以及為何一個分數不等於自動 action 的授權。 |

**它不能證明：** 你已經訓練或部署一個有用的 production model。課堂或本機 synthetic exercise 能展示你如何思考決策，不能展示 business impact、真實 data quality 或營運核准。

### 路線 3：你已會寫 Python，想理解 LLM／model building

若你已能使用 Python，並想走 model-side 路線，可參考 [Hugging Face LLM Course](https://huggingface.co/learn/llm-course/chapter1/1)。前段介紹 Transformer、從 Hub 使用 model、fine-tuning 與分享；後段延伸到 datasets、tokenizers、demos 與較進階的 LLM 主題。課程本身寫明需要良好 Python 知識，也建議先有 introductory deep-learning 基礎。這個 prerequisite 不是失敗，而是避免不寫 Code 的人把術語誤認為理解。

**第一週 artefact：** 建立一張 source receipt 和一篇極小的 local model-study note。寫下讀過的 model 或 tutorial、允許 reuse 的邊界、一個合成 input、預期 output shape，以及一件尚未理解的事情。若你有執行 code，source 與 tests 保持英文；README 說明才視需要本地化。

| 你正在練習 | 在 artefact 裡的樣子 |
| --- | --- |
| 技術判斷 | Dataset、tokenizer、model、input/output contract 與 evaluation case 之間的關係。 |
| 非技術判斷 | Reuse 與 licence 意識、compute 或時間限制、自己實際完成的貢獻，以及 tutorial result 與 original work 的差異。 |

**它不能證明：** 你能替使用者運作 LLM system、選擇 business use case，或可靠地 fine-tune model。它適合補 model literacy；不能取代 system evaluation、permission 或 product decision。

### 路線 4：你會寫 Code，想走 application 與 evaluation

當你的缺口是 application construction，例如 model selection、有範圍的 user task、response route testing、安全或營運邊界，可參考 [Microsoft Learn 的 generative-AI application path](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/paths/develop-generative-ai-apps/)。Microsoft 將它列為 intermediate、面向 AI Engineer 與 Data Scientist，並寫明需要 Azure AI fundamentals 與 programming experience；內容包含 planning、model selection/deployment/evaluation、chat application、tools、RAG 或 fine-tuning，以及 responsible implementation。

**第一週 artefact：** 建立一份 draft-only application evidence pack。定義虛構 user question、JSON-shaped output contract、baseline、五個固定 evaluation cases、預期 `DRAFT`／`HANDOFF`／`BLOCKED` 結果及 reviewer decision。你可以將一次 `gpt-5-mini` Responses API call 表示成 **static fixture**；不要放入真實 key、不要作 live call，也不要把 mocked response 寫成 observed model result。

還沒有 API key 時，先完成 [Coder Starter Lab](/zh-TW/coding-starter-lab)：它只用本機 fixture，讓你留下受限 diff、測試與 reviewer decision。日後真的準備好用自己的 key 發出 request，才開啟 [OpenAI developer quickstart](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/quickstart)。那份 quickstart 會帶你作真正的 API request，不是第一週 static exercise 必需的一步。

| 你正在練習 | 在 artefact 裡的樣子 |
| --- | --- |
| 技術判斷 | 有 scope 的 interface、test fixture、evaluator、trace fields、route states 與 regression gate。 |
| 非技術判斷 | Data boundary、已命名的 decision owner、tool permission、cost／timeout stop condition，以及誠實的 non-production claim。 |

**它不能證明：** API 已成功、application 可以安全接觸真實帳戶，或 cloud deployment 自動產生 business value。第一份 artefact 的目的，是在加入 credential 或 infrastructure 前，先讓 engineering decision 可以被檢查。

## 用 evidence gap 選來源，不要只看課程名稱

```text
我需要在不寫 Code 的前提下界定、檢查和核准草稿
  → 路線 1：no-code workflow 與 permission review

我需要解釋 metrics、errors 與 data boundaries
  → 路線 2：ML foundations

我會寫 Python，並要補 model-side literacy
  → 路線 3：LLM／model builder

我會寫 Code，並要完成有 evaluation 的 bounded AI application
  → 路線 4：application 與 evaluation
```

你可以跨路線，但不需要先累積完所有 introductory content。真正的 crossover 由限制觸發：當你需要看 implementation 或 tests，便由路線 1 移到路線 4；當 model behaviour、data 與 tokenisation 成為問題，便由路線 2 移到路線 3；當 model notebook 必須處理 user decision、evaluator 與 human handoff，便由路線 3 移到路線 4。

## 把 source receipt 放在 artefact 旁邊

不論哪一條路線，都請保留一張簡短 source receipt：

- 官方名稱與 URL，以及 access 日期；
- 哪一個 lesson、chapter 或 guide section 影響了你的 work；
- 哪些內容是 reuse、哪些有改動、哪些是自己完成；
- 你符合與尚未符合的 prerequisites；
- public／synthetic data boundary；
- 他人可重複的 command、fixture 或 manual check；
- 一個 failure 或尚未解答的問題；以及
- 你不會做出的 claim。

這樣才能把學習輸入轉為 portfolio evidence，而不是重抄 instructor solution。完整做法見：[把 AI 課程作業變成可被追問的作品證據](/zh-TW/articles/turn-an-ai-course-project-into-portfolio-evidence)。

## 小到本週可完成的起步

1. 選一條路線和一個虛構 decision；不要從大型 product idea 開始。
2. 只讀一個有明確邊界的 module 或 guide section，記下 URL 與 access date。
3. 只使用 synthetic 或公開材料，完成上面那份最小 artefact。
4. 加入五個 fixed cases，至少包括一個資訊不足、不安全或 failure case。

把正在考慮的課暫時當成「來源 01」，放入 [學習證據規劃器](/zh-TW/learning-evidence-planner) 逐項核對。你不需要輸入平台名稱；只要問第一週能否留下成果、收到可用的回饋、看見可以驗收的檢查，以及甚麼情況應該停止。頁面會產生一段只留在本機的 brief，可貼到私人筆記或 README 草稿。

有一兩項尚未做到，不代表那門課不好。這只表示它還未證明值得為你現在想補的能力投入更多時間或金錢。
