[学习证据指南](/zh-Hans/articles/choose-ai-learning-sources-by-evidence) 可协助你用 evidence gap 检查来源；有了可行来源与第一份 artefact 后，再利用 [八周作品证据 Sprint](/zh-Hans/articles/turn-an-ai-course-into-an-eight-week-evidence-sprint) 将它发展成有边界、可重复的 portfolio case。

## 真正想报名一门课时，先核对一次

把正在考虑的课程暂时当作“来源 01”，放进[学习证据规划器](/zh-Hans/learning-evidence-planner)逐项核对。你不需要输入平台名称；只要问第一周能否留下成果、收到有用的反馈、看到可以验收的检查，以及什么情况应该停止。页面会生成一段只留在本机的 brief，可贴到私人笔记或 README 草稿。

有一两项尚未做到，不代表那门课不好。这只表示它还未证明值得为你现在想补的能力投入更多时间或金钱。

## 边界与来源说明

这些链接是官方学习来源的例子，不是 affiliate link、课程排名、就业建议，也不保证 access、价格、证书、品质或求职结果。课程内容与 prerequisite 可能改变；投入时间或金钱前请查看官方页面。本文所有 decision、data、user role、model fixture 与 result 都是虚构。Static `gpt-5-mini` fixture 只示范 design contract，并非 live API result。永远不要把真实 API key、机密工作资料或已连接账户的权限放入公开 portfolio repository。
role-aware-ai-learning-source-map.en:
Choose one route that fits your evidence gap this week: name the decision you need to explain, the gap you need to close and the artefact you can retain. A course or other source is an input, not proof that you can already do the job.

## The problem with asking for the “best AI course”

Someone who wants to move into AI can easily collect four tabs, two certificates and a list of model names without gaining a clearer next step. The missing question is usually not “Which brand is best?” It is: **which capability will I be able to show, explain and improve after this week?**

This is a source map, not a ranking or an enrolment recommendation. It deliberately separates four starting routes. Each route says what it is useful for, the first public-safe artefact to make, what the system work lets you inspect, what must be decided before use, and the claim it cannot support.

Before opening anything, write one sentence in this form:

> I am aiming toward **[role or work direction]**. I cannot yet show **[one capability]**. This week I will leave **[one inspectable artefact]**. I will not claim **[an outcome the artefact cannot prove]**.

For example: “I want to move toward an AI application role. I cannot yet explain how a draft workflow is evaluated. This week I will retain five fixed acceptance cases and a human-review decision. I will not claim that I built a deployed agent.”

## Choose your working route before an external course

If you do **not** write code today, begin with the [15-minute manual safe check (AC-01, no account)](/en/no-code-starter-lab#no-code-lab-manual-title). It lets you frame a task, check the no-external-action boundary, and retain a human decision. You do not need Python, a model API or an LLM course before you can practise those abilities.

If you already write code, or want to inspect implementation, a diff or tests, begin with the [Coder Starter Lab](/en/coding-starter-lab). It starts with scope, negative cases, review and rollback—not a request to let an agent change everything. Use the [coder track](/en/series/ai-use-routes#track-coder-title) later if you want to compare the two routes.

The external sources below are selected only after that first choice. They deepen a named capability; they are not a prerequisite for being allowed to start safely.

## The four starting routes

### Route 1: You do not write code yet, but want to use AI safely in real work

Start with the [15-minute manual safe check (AC-01, no account)](/en/no-code-starter-lab#no-code-lab-manual-title), then use the [permission review](/en/articles/review-an-ai-agent-before-clicking-allow) and [reviewable workflow](/en/articles/use-ai-without-writing-code) guides. This is a learning source made of a bounded practice task, not a platform badge.

Use it when the immediate gap is: “I can ask an AI for an answer, but I cannot define what it may touch, how I check the draft, or when a person must decide.”

**First-week artefact:** a one-page fictional “public FAQ triage” brief. Use only synthetic or public text. Define an input schema, a fixed draft format, five acceptance cases, one blocked request, and the named person who accepts or rejects the draft.

| What you are practising | What it looks like in the artefact |
| --- | --- |
| System work to inspect | Structured input/output, acceptance cases, route states such as `DRAFT`, `HANDOFF` and `BLOCKED`, and a permission boundary. |
| Decisions to make before use | Who owns the decision, what data is excluded, the cost of a wrong draft, and why no external message can be sent. |

**It does not prove:** that you are a developer, that the workflow is production-ready, or that an AI tool should receive access to an account. It proves a smaller and more useful thing: you can make a vague AI request reviewable.

### Route 2: You need ML foundations for a decision, metric or data discussion

Use [Google’s Machine Learning Crash Course](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course) when your gap is not “I need another chatbot,” but “I cannot yet explain a classification threshold, false positive, false negative, metric, dataset boundary or overfitting.” Google describes it as a practical introduction with exercises and interactive material; its modules include classification, confusion matrices, precision, recall, AUC, datasets, generalisation and production-system considerations.

**First-week artefact:** a synthetic case sheet for a fictional “priority-review queue.” Create 20 labelled examples yourself. Compare a simple rule-based baseline with a hypothetical classifier threshold. Record which cases become false positives and false negatives, and specify that a human reviewer makes the actual decision.

| What you are practising | What it looks like in the artefact |
| --- | --- |
| System work to inspect | A labelled dataset boundary, a baseline, a confusion matrix, a threshold and a metric whose failure mode you can explain. |
| Decisions to make before use | Why one error costs more than another, who has review capacity, and why a score does not authorize an automated action. |

**It does not prove:** that you trained or deployed a useful production model. A lesson or a local synthetic exercise can show your reasoning about a decision; it cannot show business impact, real data quality or operational approval.

### Route 3: You already write Python and want to understand LLM/model building

Use the [Hugging Face LLM Course](https://huggingface.co/learn/llm-course/chapter1/1) when you can already work in Python and want a model-side route. Its early chapters cover Transformer concepts, using a model from the Hub, fine-tuning and sharing; later chapters cover datasets, tokenizers, demos and more advanced LLM topics. The course itself says good Python knowledge is required and that an introductory deep-learning course is a better precursor. That prerequisite is a feature, not a failure: it stops a non-coder from mistaking vocabulary for working understanding.

**First-week artefact:** a source receipt and a tiny, local model-study note. State the model or tutorial you studied, the allowed reuse boundary, a synthetic input, the expected output shape, and one thing you did not understand yet. If you run code, keep the source and tests in English; localise only the README explanation as appropriate.

| What you are practising | What it looks like in the artefact |
| --- | --- |
| System work to inspect | The relationship between a dataset, tokenizer, model, input/output contract and an evaluation case. |
| Decisions to make before use | Reuse and licence awareness, compute or time constraints, the contribution you actually made, and the difference between a tutorial result and original work. |

**It does not prove:** that you can operate an LLM system for users, choose a business use case, or reliably fine-tune a model. It is the right route for model literacy; it is not a substitute for system evaluation, permissions or a product decision.

### Route 4: You write code and want an application-and-evaluation route

Use [Microsoft Learn’s generative-AI application path](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/paths/develop-generative-ai-apps/) as source material when your gap is application construction: choosing a model, defining a bounded user task, testing a response route and explaining safety or operational boundaries. Microsoft labels its path intermediate, for AI Engineer and Data Scientist roles, and lists programming experience plus Azure AI fundamentals as prerequisites. Its modules span planning, model selection/deployment/evaluation, chat applications, tools, RAG or fine-tuning, and responsible implementation.

**First-week artefact:** a draft-only application evidence pack. Define a fictional user question, a JSON-shaped output contract, a baseline, five fixed evaluation cases, expected `DRAFT`/`HANDOFF`/`BLOCKED` results and a reviewer decision. You may model a `gpt-5-mini` Responses API call as a **static fixture**; do not add a real key, make a live call, or present a mocked response as an observed model result.

Without an API key, start with the [Coder Starter Lab](/en/coding-starter-lab). It uses local fixtures only and leaves a constrained diff, test result, and reviewer decision. Open the [OpenAI developer quickstart](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/quickstart) later, only when you are ready to use your own key for a real request. That quickstart covers a live API request; it is not required for the first-week static exercise.

| What you are practising | What it looks like in the artefact |
| --- | --- |
| System work to inspect | A scoped interface, test fixture, evaluator, trace fields, route states and a regression gate. |
| Decisions to make before use | Data boundary, named decision owner, tool permissions, cost/timeout stop condition and an honest non-production claim. |

**It does not prove:** that an API call succeeded, that an application is safe for real accounts, or that a cloud deployment creates business value. The point of the first artefact is to make the engineering decision inspectable before adding credentials or infrastructure.

## Choose by the evidence gap, not by the course name

```text
I need to frame, check and approve a draft without code
  → Route 1: no-code workflow and permission review

I need to explain metrics, errors and data boundaries
  → Route 2: ML foundations

I can write Python and need model-side literacy
  → Route 3: LLM/model builder

I can write code and need a bounded AI application with evaluation
  → Route 4: application and evaluation
```

You can move across routes, but not by collecting every introduction first. A useful crossover is triggered by a real limitation: move from Route 1 to Route 4 when you need to inspect implementation or tests; move from Route 2 to Route 3 when model behaviour, data and tokenisation become the question; move from Route 3 to Route 4 when a model notebook needs a user decision, evaluator and human handoff.

## Keep the source receipt beside the artefact

For any route, retain a short source receipt:

- official title and URL, with the date you accessed it;
- the exact lesson, chapter or guide section that informed your work;
- what you reused, what you changed, and what you made yourself;
- prerequisites you met and those you have not met;
- the public/synthetic data boundary;
- the command, fixture or manual check someone else can repeat;
- one failure or unresolved question; and
- the claim you will not make.

This is how a learning input becomes portfolio evidence without copying an instructor’s solution. See [how to turn a course exercise into evidence](/en/articles/turn-an-ai-course-project-into-portfolio-evidence) for the full source-receipt pattern.

## A first week that is small enough to finish

1. Pick one route and one fictional decision. Do not start with a broad product idea.
2. Read one bounded module or guide section. Save its URL and access date.
3. Make the smallest artefact above using synthetic or public material only.
4. Add five fixed cases, including one missing-information, unsafe, or failure case.
5. Write a human decision and a stop condition. If the work cannot yet be checked, reduce the task rather than adding another tool.

The [learning-evidence guide](/en/articles/choose-ai-learning-sources-by-evidence) helps you test a source against an evidence gap. Once you have a viable source and first artefact, the [eight-week evidence sprint](/en/articles/turn-an-ai-course-into-an-eight-week-evidence-sprint) shows how to develop it into a bounded, rerunnable portfolio case.

## Before you enrol, check one course properly

Treat the course you are considering as “Source 01” in the [Learning Evidence Planner](/en/learning-evidence-planner). You do not need to enter a provider name. Check whether Week 1 can leave an artefact, useful feedback, an observable assessment and a stop condition. The page creates a local-only brief that you can paste into a private note or README draft.

One or two missing conditions do not make a course bad. They mean it has not yet earned a larger commitment of your time or money for the capability you are trying to build now.

## Limits and source note

These links are examples of official learning sources, not affiliate links, course rankings, employment advice or an assurance of access, price, certification, quality or job outcomes. Course content and prerequisites can change; check the official page before investing time or money. All example decisions, data, user roles, model fixtures and results in this guide are fictional. A static `gpt-5-mini` fixture demonstrates a design contract only; it is not a live API result. Never put a real API key, confidential work data or connected account access in a public portfolio repository.

ai-engineering-shared-language.zh-HK:
一句 `model.generate()` 可以輸出文字；它本身沒有交代使用者要完成甚麼、錯誤時何時停下，或誰負責處理。面試時，把幾個詞混成「我會加個 agent」通常正正顯示你未分得開能力、資料和權限。

## 用一條小流程建立共同語言

想像一位內部 reviewer 想根據**已批准、完全虛構**的政策文件寫一份回覆草稿。最小流程是：

`問題 → 揀合資格文件 → 取相關段落 → model 生成草稿 → rule check → reviewer 決定`

**LLM** 是根據輸入的 tokens 預測下一段文字的 model。它可以寫得流暢，但不會自動知道哪些文件仍有效，亦不會因此獲得發信或改資料的權限。

**Token** 是 model 讀寫的細小單位；**context** 是今次 request 放入 model 可見範圍的 tokens，包括指示、問題、檢索片段和對話。context 大不代表理解更完整：它增加 cost 和 latency，亦可能令重要資料被雜訊淹沒。

## RAG、MCP 和 agent 各自解決甚麼

**RAG**（retrieval-augmented generation）由文件庫取回候選內容，並把少量可引用片段交給 model。它處理的是「model 今次可以根據哪份資料作答」，不是保證答案正確。metadata filter、文件版本、citation 和無足夠證據時的 handoff 仍要另外設計。

**MCP**（Model Context Protocol）可以令一個 host 以標準方式看見工具或資源的 description 和 input schema。它是連接介面，不是 authorization。就算工具叫做 `send_reply`，仍要由 host policy 決定誰可叫、甚麼資料可傳、何時必須要求人批准。

**Agent** 是一個可選的 loop：model 觀察 state、提出下一步、可能使用受限工具，再檢查結果。若流程其實永遠是「search → draft → reviewer」，固定 workflow 通常較容易測試。只有在任務真的需要根據中途結果選路時，才值得加 loop。

## Quantization 不是免費加速

**Quantization** 用較低精度表示部分 model weights 或 activation，通常為了省 memory、提高可部署性或吞吐量。它不是單靠名字就一定更快或更便宜：要比較硬件、batch、context 長度、quality regression 和 fallback。若高風險 case 的表現下降，較便宜的 serving 不一定是較好決定。

## 面試回答可以怎樣落地

不要由模型名開始。一個清楚的回答會講明 reviewer 要作甚麼決定和 data boundary：只用哪類文件、何時拒答、輸出只是一份 draft。再畫出上面六個節點，為每個節點寫一個可檢查的問題：

- retrieval 是否拿到仍有效而且合資格的文件？
- model output 是否符合 schema、附有 citation，還是應 handoff？
- tool 是否只有 read scope，外發行動是否停在 reviewer 前？
- 每次 request 可否由 version、trace 和 case ID 重現？

這張小圖比背十個定義更有用：它同時展示你知道模型做甚麼、系統補甚麼、以及人不應交出甚麼決定權。

## 邊界

這是學習用的 synthetic flow，不代表真實公司文件、真實 MCP server 或 production authorization。不要把 tool description、model guardrail 或「有 RAG」誤當存取控制；權限和外部行動要在可驗證的 policy 層執行。

延伸閱讀：[將 prompt 變成可驗收介面](/zh-HK/interview-lab/prompt-contracts-need-an-acceptance-test)、[拆開 RAG 的 retrieval、generation 和 permission](/zh-HK/interview-lab/rag-retrieval-generation-or-permission) 和 [按 Allow 前審 agent](/zh-HK/articles/review-an-ai-agent-before-clicking-allow)。

ai-engineering-shared-language.en:
One `model.generate()` call can produce text. It does not explain how an AI system helps a person, when it stops, or who owns an error. In an interview, collapsing every component into “I would add an agent” usually shows that capability, data, and authority have not been separated.

## Build a shared language around one small flow

Imagine an internal reviewer drafting a reply from **approved, entirely fictional** policy documents. The smallest flow is:

`question → eligible documents → relevant passages → model draft → rule check → reviewer decision`

An **LLM** predicts the next tokens from its input. It may write fluent text, but it does not automatically know which documents are current, and it does not gain permission to send an email or change a record.

A **token** is a small unit the model reads or writes. **Context** is the set of tokens visible for this request: instructions, question, retrieved passages, and conversation. More context is not automatically better understanding. It increases cost and latency and can bury decisive material in noise.

## What RAG, MCP, and an agent each solve

**RAG** (retrieval-augmented generation) retrieves candidate material and supplies a small set of citable passages to the model. It answers “what material may this response use?” It does not guarantee a correct answer. Metadata filters, document versions, citations, and an insufficient-evidence handoff still need deliberate design.

**MCP** (Model Context Protocol) gives a host a standard way to discover a tool or resource description and input schema. It is a connection interface, not authorization. A tool named `send_reply` still needs host policy to decide who may call it, which data may leave, and when a human approval is mandatory.

An **agent** is an optional loop: the model observes state, proposes a next step, may use a constrained tool, and checks the result. When the work is always “search → draft → reviewer,” a fixed workflow is usually easier to test. Add a loop only when the task truly needs to choose a route from intermediate results.

## Quantization is not free acceleration

**Quantization** represents some model weights or activations at lower precision, often to reduce memory use or improve deployability and throughput. It is not automatically faster or cheaper. Compare hardware, batch size, context length, quality regression, and fallback. A lower-cost serving path is not a better decision if it degrades high-risk cases.

## Turn the vocabulary into an interview answer

Do not begin with a model name. State the reviewer’s decision and the data boundary: which documents are allowed, when the system must decline, and why the output remains a draft. Then draw the six nodes above and attach one inspectable question to each:

- Did retrieval select current, eligible documents?
- Does the model output meet a schema and carry citations, or require handoff?
- Does the tool have read-only scope, with any external action stopped before the reviewer?
- Can a request be reproduced from its version, trace, and case ID?

This small map is more useful than ten disconnected definitions. It shows what a model does, what the application adds, and which decisions people must not surrender.

## Boundary

This is a learning-only synthetic flow, not a real company corpus, MCP server, or production authorization claim. A tool description, a model guardrail, or “we use RAG” is not access control. Permissions and external actions need enforceable policy outside the model.

Continue with [a prompt contract and acceptance test](/en/interview-lab/prompt-contracts-need-an-acceptance-test), [separating retrieval, generation, and permission](/en/interview-lab/rag-retrieval-generation-or-permission), and [reviewing an agent before Allow](/en/articles/review-an-ai-agent-before-clicking-allow).

transformer-model-choice.zh-HK:
如果你答「Transformer 就係 attention，唔準就 fine-tune」，interviewer 通常會再問兩句：模型實際睇到咩？錯誤究竟係資料、generation，定係任務設計？這兩句決定你係背名詞，還是知道怎樣選工具。

## 一個 token 如何影響下一個 token

文字先被切成 **tokens**，再變成 vectors。每層 **self-attention** 讓目前位置用 query（要找甚麼）、key（我有甚麼線索）和 value（可帶走甚麼內容）去加權其他位置。**Position information** 令 model 分得出次序；decoder 的 **causal mask** 阻止它偷看未來 token。最後 layers 產生下一個 token 的 scores（logits）。

這不是資料庫查詢。attention 只是在目前 context 內調整訊息權重；如果可靠資料根本沒有進 context，它不會自動找回來。這正是 retrieval、metadata filter 和 citation 仍有用的原因。

## Generation 是一組取捨，不是 personality slider

logits 經過 sampling 才變成 token。較低 **temperature** 傾向保守；**top-p** 只在一個累積機率集合選擇。它們可改變多樣性，不能修好錯誤資料、缺少權限或不清楚的 acceptance rule。

互動服務也要分 **prefill** 和 **decode**。prefill 讀完整 prompt；decode 一個個產生 token。長 context 可能令第一個 token 慢，長輸出令總時間慢。streaming 會改善等待感，但不會令答案更正確。

## Architecture 同 adaptation 怎樣揀

Decoder-only model 適合逐 token 生成；encoder-style representations 常用於分類或 retrieval。dense model 每次都用大部分參數；Mixture-of-Experts（MoE）會路由到少量 expert，可能改善 compute efficiency，但增加 routing、capacity 和 serving 複雜度。KV cache 避免每次 decode 重算已見 token，但會吃 memory，直接影響 batch 和 context budget。

面對一個不穩定任務，順序應是：

1. 定義固定 input、可接受 output、拒答條件和 baseline。
2. 檢查資料是否應由 retrieval 補足、metadata 是否錯、prompt contract 是否不完整，或 workflow 是否將不相關內容混入 context。
3. 只有當同一類行為在合法、足夠、版本清楚的資料上反覆失敗，才比較 parameter-efficient fine-tuning（例如 LoRA）或其他 adaptation。

Fine-tuning 可以學到穩定模式；它不會自動令資料更新、citation、權限或後果性 action 變安全。訓練前後都要用同一組 held-out cases，分開量 task quality、拒答、latency、cost 和 high-risk regression。

## 留低的證據

做一張 model-choice record：列出 baseline、12 個 synthetic cases、兩個 failure families、context budget、兩個候選改善、預期代價和 stop condition。若 retrieval 已修好 stale-policy case，這是「不 fine-tune」的有價值結論，不是失敗。

延伸閱讀：[Prompt contract](/zh-HK/interview-lab/prompt-contracts-need-an-acceptance-test)、[similarity 高仍然拎錯文件](/zh-HK/interview-lab/high-similarity-is-not-relevance) 和 [模型分數怎樣變成 workflow 決定](/zh-HK/articles/model-score-to-workflow-decision)。

transformer-model-choice.zh-Hans:
如果你回答“Transformer 就是 attention，不准就 fine-tune”，interviewer 通常会再问两句：模型实际看到什么？错误究竟是数据、generation，还是任务设计？这两句决定你是背名词，还是知道怎样选工具。

## 一个 token 如何影响下一个 token

文字先被切成 **tokens**，再变成 vectors。每层 **self-attention** 让当前位置用 query（要找什么）、key（我有什么线索）和 value（可带走什么内容）去加权其他位置。**Position information** 让 model 分得出顺序；decoder 的 **causal mask** 阻止它偷看未来 token。最后 layers 产生下一个 token 的 scores（logits）。

这不是数据库查询。attention 只是在目前 context 内调整信息权重；若可靠数据根本没有进 context，它不会自动找回来。这就是 retrieval、metadata filter 和 citation 仍有用的原因。

## Generation 是一组取舍，不是 personality slider

logits 经过 sampling 才变成 token。较低 **temperature** 倾向保守；**top-p** 只在一个累积概率集合选择。它们可改变多样性，不能修好错误数据、缺少权限或不清楚的 acceptance rule。

互动服务也要分 **prefill** 和 **decode**。prefill 读完整 prompt；decode 一个个产生 token。长 context 可能让第一个 token 慢，长输出让总时间慢。streaming 会改善等待感，但不会让答案更正确。

## Architecture 与 adaptation 怎样选

Decoder-only model 适合逐 token 生成；encoder-style representations 常用于分类或 retrieval。dense model 每次使用大部分参数；Mixture-of-Experts（MoE）会路由到少量 expert，可能改善 compute efficiency，但增加 routing、capacity 和 serving 复杂度。KV cache 避免每次 decode 重算已见 token，但会占 memory，直接影响 batch 与 context budget。

面对不稳定任务，先定义固定 input、可接受 output、拒答条件与 baseline；检查 retrieval、metadata、prompt contract 与 workflow；只有同类行为在合法、足够、版本清楚的数据上反复失败，才比较 LoRA 等 parameter-efficient fine-tuning。

Fine-tuning 不会自动让数据更新、citation、权限或后果性 action 变安全。训练前后都要用同一组 held-out cases，分开量 task quality、拒答、latency、cost 与 high-risk regression。

## 留下的证据

建立 model-choice record：baseline、12 个 synthetic cases、两个 failure families、context budget、两个候选改善、预期代价与 stop condition。若 retrieval 已修好 stale-policy case，“不 fine-tune”也是有价值结论。

transformer-model-choice.en:
If your answer is “a Transformer is attention, and I would fine-tune it when it is wrong,” an interviewer can ask two useful questions: what did the model actually see, and is the failure data, generation, or task design? The answers distinguish a term list from an engineering choice.

## How one token affects the next

Text becomes **tokens**, then vectors. In each **self-attention** layer, a position uses a query (what it needs), key (what signal it offers), and value (what content can move) to weight other positions. **Position information** preserves order; a decoder’s **causal mask** blocks future tokens. The final layers produce next-token scores, or logits.

This is not a database lookup. Attention reweights information already in the current context. If authoritative material never entered the context, it cannot retrieve it. That is why retrieval, metadata filtering, and citations remain separate work.

## Generation is a trade-off, not a personality slider

Sampling turns logits into a token. Lower **temperature** tends to make selection more conservative; **top-p** restricts selection to a cumulative-probability set. These controls can change variety. They cannot repair bad data, missing permissions, or a vague acceptance rule.

Interactive serving also separates **prefill** from **decode**. Prefill reads the whole prompt; decode produces tokens one at a time. Long context can delay the first token, while long output increases total time. Streaming improves perceived wait time, not correctness.

## Choose architecture and adaptation deliberately

Decoder-only models suit token-by-token generation; encoder-style representations often support classification or retrieval. Dense models activate most parameters each time. Mixture-of-Experts routes work to a small set of experts, which can improve compute efficiency while adding routing, capacity, and serving complexity. A KV cache avoids recomputing seen tokens during decoding but consumes memory and constrains batches and context budgets.

For an unstable task, first define fixed input, acceptable output, decline conditions, and a baseline. Check whether retrieval, metadata, the prompt contract, or workflow assembly is the problem. Compare parameter-efficient fine-tuning such as LoRA only when the same behaviour repeatedly fails on lawful, sufficient, versioned data.

Fine-tuning does not make freshness, citations, permissions, or consequential actions safe. Evaluate before and after on the same held-out cases, separating task quality, correct declines, latency, cost, and high-risk regressions.

## Evidence to keep

Create a model-choice record: baseline, twelve synthetic cases, two failure families, context budget, two candidate changes, their costs, and a stop condition. If retrieval fixes a stale-policy case, “do not fine-tune” is an engineering result—not a failure.

Continue with [a prompt contract](/en/interview-lab/prompt-contracts-need-an-acceptance-test), [why high similarity can still retrieve the wrong document](/en/interview-lab/high-similarity-is-not-relevance), and [turning a model score into a workflow decision](/en/articles/model-score-to-workflow-decision).

neural-learning-loop.zh-HK:
模型訓練唔係「餵資料，等佢變聰明」。佢係不停做四件可檢查的事：把 input 變成 prediction、量度錯幾多、沿住一個能減少錯誤的方向更新參數，然後在未見過的資料再驗證。

## 用一個小分類任務看 learning loop

假設你要把完全合成的 FAQ case 分成 `supported` 或 `handoff`。**Representation** 是 input 變成 model 可計算特徵的方式；**target** 是預先定義的正確 route。model 給出 prediction 後，**loss** 把 prediction 和 target 的差距變成一個訓練訊號。

**Gradient** 告訴每個參數：向哪個細小方向改，loss 會下降。**Backpropagation** 是把這個訊號由 output 倒傳到前面 layers 的計算程序；optimizer 再決定每次改幾多。它不是保證學到正確因果，只是令當前 training objective 變小。

## 為何 loss 下降仍未必可用

若 train loss 不斷下降，但 validation loss 變差，常見是 **overfitting**：model 記得了 training set 的偶然細節，未學到可延伸的 pattern。也可能是資料重複、target 定義有歧義、split 洩漏了未來訊息，或 validation case 根本沒有代表日後決定。

所以排查順序不是先換更大 network：先抽查 input 和 target、確認時間邊界、保留簡單 baseline、按 failure family 分組看 confusion matrix，再調整 representation、model 或 optimisation。若任務其實只要 rule 或 human review，這也是有效結論。

## 留下能被追問的證據

用 synthetic data 做一頁 training note：資料版本和 split rule、baseline、metric、train／validation curve、兩個錯誤 case、下一個假設，以及系統不會自動做甚麼行動。這比只貼一張 loss chart 更能證明你明白模型以外的決定。

延伸閱讀：[模型分數升了，決定為何未必更好](/zh-HK/articles/model-score-to-workflow-decision) 和 [由 Transformer 機制走到選型](/zh-HK/articles/choose-transformer-generation-and-adaptation-tradeoffs)。

neural-learning-loop.en:
Training is not “feed data and wait for intelligence.” It repeats four inspectable actions: turn input into a prediction, measure the error, update parameters in a direction that can reduce it, then validate on data the model did not see during training.

## See the learning loop with a small classification task

Imagine routing completely synthetic FAQ cases as `supported` or `handoff`. A **representation** turns input into features the model can compute with. The **target** is a pre-defined correct route. After a prediction, **loss** turns the difference from that target into a training signal.

A **gradient** indicates the small direction in which each parameter could move to reduce loss. **Backpropagation** calculates that signal from output back through earlier layers; an optimizer decides the size of each update. It does not prove the model learned a real causal relationship. It only reduces the current training objective.

## Why falling loss may still be unusable

When train loss falls while validation loss worsens, **overfitting** is a common explanation: the model remembered accidental details in the training set instead of a pattern that extends. Other causes include duplicate data, ambiguous targets, a split that leaks future information, or validation cases that do not represent the later decision.

Do not start by choosing a larger network. Inspect inputs and targets, confirm time boundaries, preserve a simple baseline, group errors by failure family in a confusion matrix, then adjust representation, model, or optimisation. If a rule or human review is sufficient, that is also a useful result.

## Evidence worth keeping

Build a one-page training note with synthetic data: data version and split rule, baseline, metric, train/validation curve, two error cases, the next hypothesis, and actions the system will not take. It demonstrates judgement beyond a screenshot of a loss curve.

Continue with [why a higher model score may not be a better decision](/en/articles/model-score-to-workflow-decision) and [moving from Transformer mechanics to model choice](/en/articles/choose-transformer-generation-and-adaptation-tradeoffs).

implementation-evidence-loop.zh-HK:
「我用 coding agent 做咗個 app，run 到」唔係一個可以交代的實作答案。interviewer 或 reviewer 下一步會問：佢原本應該做乜？邊啲 input 唔可以接受？改咗邊一部分？測試證明咗咩？如果錯咗點樣停？

## 用一個細小 feature 練 implementation judgment

想像一個完全合成的 policy-draft tool。user 輸入一條問題，系統只可在已批准文件內選 source，然後輸出 JSON draft 或 `HANDOFF`。它不讀真實帳戶、不發訊息、不改記錄。

先寫 **input contract**：問題必須是 text、document scope 要存在、最大長度是多少、哪些欄位不會接受。再寫 **output contract**：`draft` 必須有 citation IDs；找不到足夠支持時必須是 `HANDOFF`；不得有外發 action。contract 把「看似正常」變成可以測的條件。

## 正常 case 不夠

一組 fixed cases 最少包括：有足夠支持的問題、無支持的問題、過期文件、跨區文件、空 input、錯誤 JSON、prompt injection 字樣，以及 model response timeout。每個 case 寫 expected terminal state，不是只寫「應該 work」。

**Unit test** 檢查小函數或 validator；**integration test** 檢查 source selection、model-shaped fixture 和 output parser 是否一起遵守 contract；**acceptance case** 則由使用者決定回看：這份草稿能否給 reviewer 看，還是要 handoff。三者不能互相取代。

## Coding agent 的位置

coding agent 可以提出 plan、diff 和 tests，但不可以偷偷擴大 scope。reviewer 要看：

- diff 是否加入 login、network、database 或寫入權限，而 brief 沒有要求？
- negative cases 有冇真係 fail，還是只測 happy path？
- input/output schema 有冇在邊界檢查，而唔係希望 prompt 自己守規矩？
- 失敗後系統會不會留 trace、停在 handoff，還是靜靜重試到出現另一個結果？

## 交付證據不等於 production claim

保留 `SPEC.md`、一頁 plan、可讀 diff、test matrix、一次失敗例子、decision record 和 README rerun steps。它們可以展示你如何把要求變成可驗收 feature；不代表你已在真實公司部署、處理客戶資料或帶來業務成效。

若改動牽涉帳戶、付款、外發、醫療、法律或個人資料，縮細成 synthetic、draft-only prototype。沒有人能說清誰批准最後行動時，正確的 implementation decision 是停低，不是加更多 agent。

implementation-evidence-loop.en:
“I used a coding agent to build an app, and it runs” is not an implementation answer that survives follow-up. An interviewer or reviewer can ask what it was meant to do, which input it must reject, what actually changed, what the tests prove, and where it stops when wrong.

## Practise implementation judgement with one small feature

Imagine a fully synthetic policy-draft tool. A user asks a question; the system may select sources only from approved documents, then return a JSON draft or `HANDOFF`. It does not read real accounts, send messages, or alter records.

Write an **input contract** first: the question must be text, document scope must exist, maximum length, and rejected fields. Then an **output contract**: a `draft` carries citation IDs; insufficient support becomes `HANDOFF`; no output can contain an external action. The contract turns “looks right” into testable conditions.

## Happy paths are not enough

A fixed case set should include supported and unsupported questions, stale and cross-region documents, empty input, malformed JSON, prompt-injection language, and a model-response timeout. Each case names its expected terminal state, not merely “should work.”

A **unit test** checks a small function or validator. An **integration test** checks whether source selection, a model-shaped fixture, and the output parser jointly obey the contract. An **acceptance case** returns to the user decision: can a reviewer see this draft, or must it hand off?

## The coding agent’s role

A coding agent can propose a plan, diff, and tests. It must not quietly expand scope. A reviewer should ask whether the diff adds login, network, database, or write permissions that the brief never asked for; whether negative cases actually fail; whether schemas are checked at the boundary; and whether a failure leaves a trace and ends in handoff instead of silent retries.

## Delivery evidence is not a production claim

Keep `SPEC.md`, a one-page plan, readable diff, test matrix, one failure example, decision record, and README rerun steps. They demonstrate how you turn a request into an acceptable feature. They do not claim a real-company deployment, customer data handling, or business impact.

When a change involves accounts, payments, outbound communication, medical, legal, or personal data, reduce it to a synthetic, draft-only prototype. If nobody can name who approves the final action, the correct implementation decision is to stop—not add more agents.

Continue with [from vague request to accepted feature](/en/articles/from-vague-request-to-accepted-feature), [review a coding-agent build](/en/articles/review-a-coding-agent-build-without-being-a-developer), and [build a GitHub proof pack](/en/articles/build-a-github-portfolio-proof-pack).

agent-execution-and-serving.zh-HK:
> 快不等於可靠。Agent 不知道幾時停、用過甚麼工具，或一次寫入有沒有成功，速度只會放大錯誤。

## 下午四時四十七分，先見到兩套系統

想像一個完全虛構的 **退貨證據 Desk**。Support reviewer 貼入已去識別的 order summary，要求系統根據已批准 policy 片段，產生一份有引用、建議內部 route 的草稿；它永遠不可聯絡客戶、改動退貨或讀取帳戶。

Demo 很順：agent search 一小組 policy，寫 draft，幾秒後完成。到下午四時四十七分，queue 變長，一次 retrieval timeout，而 timeout 前可能已記錄了一張 review task；同時一段很長的歷史內容令第一個字遲遲未出。這時設計要回答的是：

> 「你會怎樣設計，令 agent 可以安全停下，同時 serving layer 仍然守到 user-facing P99 latency budget？」

這題把兩樣通常分開講的事拉在一起。**Agent execution** 決定下一步能否發生；**model serving** 決定工作怎樣到達 model、要等多久。可靠設計要用同一份 budget、穩定 state 和有名字的人手 authority 把它們接起來。

## 只解決一半的答案

> 「我會加 retry、多開 replicas，再開 streaming。」

這些可以是工具，但不是 recovery plan。

多開 replicas 不會告訴 agent 幾時應該停。Streaming 可以令第一段字早些出現，但不會令不安全的 tool call 變得可逆。若一個 write 的結果不明，retry 可能建兩張相同的 review task。就算 model 較快，queue 在 model 開始前已花光 P99 budget，使用者一樣覺得慢。

Job 的界線要清楚，每個 state transition 亦要可以被檢查。

## 一次 run 是 state machine，不是 model 外面的一個 loop

這個 Desk 沒有 send、modify 或 account access 的 permission；唯一 output 是給 reviewer 的 draft。小型 state machine 已足夠令界線清楚：

```text
received
  -> validated
  -> planned
  -> tool_requested
  -> observed
  -> draft_ready
  -> handoff
  -> blocked
  -> retry_scheduled
  -> budget_stopped
```

不是每條箭咀都合法。找不到 policy source，要由 `observed` 去 `handoff`，不是編一段似樣的文字。time budget 用完，要去 `budget_stopped`，不是重返 `planned`。Tool timeout 不代表甚麼都沒有發生；它要進入一個可以先查 stable action identity，再決定可否 retry 的 state。

這就是「可以停」的實際意思：agent 有明確 terminal state、reason code 和下一位 decision owner。它不會因為不肯定，就不斷產生新 plan。

### Tool contract：model 提議，runtime 決定

Model 可以提議 tool call，但 runtime 才決定提議可不可以執行。一份有用的 **tool contract** 會寫清楚：

- tool 名稱和目的；
- input schema 和可接受值；
- effect 是 read-only、draft-only，還是有後果的 action；
- caller identity 和 permission boundary；
- timeout、retry class、idempotency requirement 和 expected output schema；
- success、failure 或 ambiguity 之後可到哪一個 state。

例如 `find_policy_evidence` 只可收 case category 和 approved document version，回傳 citation，而且是 read-only。`create_review_task` 則要 stable `action_id`、要拒絕 duplicate creation，並且只能回 confirmed task reference 或明確 unknown state。Prompt 不是 permission system；contract 才是。

想像一個肯幫手的 intern 拿著 request form。他可以建議開哪個櫃，但實際可以開哪些櫃，是有標籤的 key cabinet 和 supervisor 決定。

### Trace 是營運收據，不是秘密對話逐字稿

保留足夠資料，讓日後可以回答：「這個 case 為何走這條 route？」最小 trace 可以包括：

```text
run_id、case_version、policy_version、state transitions、
tool name、安全的 input summary、action_id、tool result class、
latency slices、token/cost proxy、terminal reason、reviewer outcome
```

不要預設儲存完整客戶文字、raw secret，或每一句 model 想法。目標是在 data minimisation 下重建 decision 和找 regression。一條 `tool_requested → unknown_after_timeout → handoff` 的 trace，比一大段掩蓋了外部 effect 是否完成的 chat transcript 更有用。

## P99 是對使用者的承諾，不是 benchmark trophy

P50 表示一般 latency；P99 描述 slow tail：那一小撮令 reviewer 等到離開 workflow 或狂按 refresh 的 request。目標應由 user decision 推導，不是由 model leaderboard 決定。

先替這個虛構 Desk 同意一份 synthetic user-facing budget，才調任何 serving knob：

| Budget slice | 包甚麼 | 要收集的證據 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Admission | validation、policy check、queue wait | queue timestamp 和 rejection reason |
| Context | retrieval、prompt assembly | retrieved count、context size、cache decision |
| First visible result | model prefill 加 first decode step | time to first token 或 first structured event |
| Completion | 其餘 decoding 和 output validation | total latency、output size、schema result |
| Recovery | retry lookup、route 或 handoff creation | reason、attempt、terminal state |

Budget 是 design constraint，不是偷偷剪走 safety check 的藉口。如果 case 未能及時產生有 evidence 支持的 draft，清楚的 `HANDOFF` 可以比快速但無引用的答案好。Latency 旁邊要量 handoff rate，否則「更快」可能只是「我們更常放棄」。

## Prefill 和 decode 為何造成不同 bottleneck

Autoregressive language model 先處理已有 prompt，這段叫 **prefill**。它通常受 input context 影響：過長的 history、太多 retrieved passages，或反覆加入的 policy instruction，都會拖慢第一個 output。之後 **decode** 才逐 token 產生文字；一份長 draft 因此可能 first token 可以接受，total completion 卻很慢。

這個分別會改變診斷：

- first response 慢，先看 queueing、context length、retrieval fan-out、prompt reuse 和 prefill capacity；
- first response 快但完得慢，先看 expected output length、structured-output repair loop、decoding capacity 和 streaming；
- 只有 load 高先兩邊都慢，先看 admission control 和 batch scheduling，別急著怪 model。

Streaming 適合在 final validated draft 前，讓 user 看得到安全的進度。它不代表可以 stream 未驗證 policy advice 或未完成的 write action；產品要先決定哪一個 event 可以被看見。

## Serving levers，各有代價

Batching、caching、quantisation、scaling 經常被當成一套「加速按鈕」，其實每樣解的 constraint 不同。

| Lever | 可能改善 | 可能變差 | 留下前要檢查 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dynamic batching | throughput、hardware utilisation | 孤單但緊急 request 的 queue wait 和 P99 | 以 traffic class 比較 P50、P95、P99、queue delay |
| Prefix / prompt cache | 重複的穩定 instruction 和 context prefix | prefix 一變，hit rate 下降；舊 policy 可能被重用 | version policy prefix，記錄 hit/miss |
| Response cache | 重複、安全而 deterministic 的問法 | 錯誤 reuse、privacy leak、stale answer | 只 cache 有界 key，連 source/version validity 一起驗證 |
| KV cache | decode 時不重算已見 token state | memory pressure 限制 batch size 和 context | 記錄 cache memory、output length、eviction behaviour |
| Quantisation | memory footprint，有時也改善 throughput | task quality、numerical compatibility 或罕見 case behaviour | 前後跑同一組 quality 和 safety cases |

這些都不能取代較簡單 baseline：縮短 approved context、回傳精簡 structured draft，或把低證據 case 交 reviewer。Optimization 是有 error budget 的 product decision，不是一堆聰明的 switches。

## Retry 前先有 identity，不是先求快

Failure 要按「知道了甚麼」分類：

- input schema 被拒，通常要修正 input 才可再做；
- rate limit 可以是有上限 delay 的 retryable case；
- read-only search timeout，在 contract 容許下可 retry；
- 有後果 action timeout，屬於 **unknown outcome**，不是自動 retry。

對有後果的 tool，call 前要生成 stable idempotency key。出現 ambiguity 時，先向 tool 或 durable state store 查這個 key 有沒有產生 effect。若安全地仍然無法知道，就 handoff。這比樂觀 retry 慢，但避免 duplicate ticket、message 或 refund。

Execution budget 不只 token：還要有最大 state transition、tool attempt、wall-clock time 和 cost proxy。用完 budget，要留下 reviewer 可行動的 reason；不要把 loop 藏在 progress spinner 後面。

## 人手在架構中的位置

Human handoff 要寫入 contract。這個虛構 Desk 會在以下情況 handoff：

- policy source 矛盾，或不足以支持 proposed answer；
- 一個可能造成 effect 的 tool timeout 後 state 不明；
- case 超出已聲明 category；
- latency、cost 或 retry budget 已花完；
- action 會改外部 record 或 message。

Handoff packet 要有已有的 draft、supporting evidence、terminal reason、安全 trace reference 和一位有名字的 owner。「已升級給人」但無目的地，只是另一種 terminal error。

## 未 claim 改善 serving 前，先建立 evidence

先用 synthetic case 和 deterministic tool fixture。小型 evaluation table 至少有：normal short context、normal long context、cache hit、cache miss、retrieval timeout、rate limit、duplicate action ID、unknown write result、policy conflict 和 budget exhaustion。

每一個 case 都要記錄：

- expected terminal state 和 forbidden state transition；
- allowed tool path 和 action identity；
- time to first event、total latency、queue delay 和 output size；
- cache / batching condition；
- draft quality rule、citation rule 和 reviewer route；
- 這個 test **沒有** 證明甚麼。

把 state diagram、contract schema、trace field、load fixture 和 latency report 放進同一個 review pack，再連同 user decision、data boundary、error cost、handoff owner 和 stop condition。reviewer 就可以同時核對系統點樣跑，同埋應該喺邊度停。

## 一段可以接受追問的回答

> 「我會先以 bounded state machine 和 tool contract 起步，不會做 open-ended loop。每個 tool 都有 input/output schema、permission level、timeout、retry class 和 idempotency rule。我會 trace state transition、安全的 tool evidence、latency slices 和 terminal reason，同時 minimising sensitive data。Serving 方面，我會將 user-facing P99 拆成 queueing、context/prefill、decode、validation 和 recovery 的 budget。我會以同一組固定 quality 和 safety case 檢查 batching、caching、KV-cache memory 和 quantisation，而不是只看 latency。若有後果的 tool timeout，我會查 stable action identity；effect 不明就 handoff。第一版保持 draft-only，並有 named reviewer 負責 conflict、budget stop 和不可逆 action。」

這段答案顯示你知道 model behaviour、runtime control、operations 和真實 owner 如何放在同一個系統。

## Repository 應保留的 artefacts

- `brief.md`：虛構 decision、user、data boundary、non-goal 和 reviewer owner。
- `state-machine.md`：合法 state、transition、terminal reason，以及永遠不可以發生的事。
- `tool-contracts/`：schema、permission、timeout、retry class、action ID 和 output validator。
- `trace-schema.md`：保留和刻意排除的 field，以及 retention rationale。
- `latency-budget.md`：P99 slices、traffic assumption、queue policy 和 miss budget 後的 decision。
- `synthetic-evals/`：normal、slow、ambiguous、duplicate 和 blocked case 的固定 fixture。
- `results.md`：quality、handoff、route、latency、cache 和 cost-proxy result，包括一個 failure。
- `decision-log.md`：為何選這個 cache、batch rule 或 handoff threshold，以及仍未證明甚麼。

延伸閱讀可先看 [workflow-level agent evaluation](/zh-HK/articles/evaluate-an-ai-agent-workflow-not-just-the-final-answer)，再實作更窄的 [可 resume batch worker](/zh-HK/articles/build-a-resumable-ai-batch-worker)。配合 [agent 取得 permission 前的 review](/zh-HK/articles/review-an-ai-agent-before-clicking-allow)，以及 [Transformer、generation 和 serving 的取捨](/zh-HK/articles/choose-transformer-generation-and-adaptation-tradeoffs)。

## 邊界與來源說明

這是 AI.DOG 教學，以 synthetic、draft-only scenario 解釋。它不是 production architecture、benchmark result、provider capacity claim，亦不承諾任何 latency、reliability、business outcome 或 interview result。本文的 tool、data、budget、state label 和 artefact 都是示範。真實系統要有自己的 security review、privacy assessment、provider documentation、workload measurement、incident process 和已授權 owner，才可影響客戶或外部 record。
agent-execution-and-serving.zh-TW:
> 一個看起來反應很快的 agent，不一定可靠。它如果不會停止、不會交代使用了什麼工具、不會在結果不明時避免重複 effect，也沒有留給人決定的位置，低 latency 只會讓它更快做錯事。

## 下午四點四十七分，才看見兩套系統

想像一個完全虛構的 **退貨證據 Desk**。Support reviewer 貼入已去識別的 order summary，要求系統根據已核准的 policy 片段，產生一份有引用、建議內部 route 的草稿；它永遠不能聯絡客戶、修改退貨或讀取帳戶。

Demo 很順：agent search 一小組 policy，寫 draft，幾秒後完成。到了下午四點四十七分，queue 變長，一次 retrieval timeout，而 timeout 前可能已記錄了一張 review task；同時一段很長的歷史內容讓第一個字遲遲沒有出現。這時已不是「model 會不會寫」的問題，而是：

> 「你會怎麼設計，讓 agent 可以安全停止，同時 serving layer 仍守得住 user-facing P99 latency budget？」

這題把兩件通常分開說的事拉在一起。**Agent execution** 決定下一步能不能發生；**model serving** 決定工作怎麼到達 model、要等多久。可靠的設計要用同一份 budget、穩定的 state 和有名字的人員 authority 把它們連起來。

## 只解決一半的答案

> 「我會加 retry、多開 replicas，然後開 streaming。」

這些可以是工具，但不是 recovery plan。

多開 replicas 不會告訴 agent 什麼時候該停止。Streaming 可以讓第一段字早些出現，但不會讓不安全的 tool call 變成可逆。若一個 write 的結果不明，retry 可能建立兩張相同的 review task。就算 model 更快，queue 在 model 開始前已耗盡 P99 budget，使用者一樣會覺得慢。

先界定 job，再讓每個 state transition 都可以被檢查。

## 一次 run 是 state machine，不是 model 外面的一個 loop

這個 Desk 沒有 send、modify 或 account access 的 permission；唯一 output 是交給 reviewer 的 draft。小型 state machine 已經足以讓界線清楚：

```text
received
  -> validated
  -> planned
  -> tool_requested
  -> observed
  -> draft_ready
  -> handoff
  -> blocked
  -> retry_scheduled
  -> budget_stopped
```

不是每條箭頭都合法。找不到 policy source，要從 `observed` 去 `handoff`，不是編一段看似合理的文字。time budget 用完，要去 `budget_stopped`，不是回到 `planned`。Tool timeout 不代表什麼都沒有發生；它應進到一個能先查 stable action identity、再決定是否可 retry 的 state。

這就是「可以停止」的實際意思：agent 有明確的 terminal state、reason code 和下一位 decision owner。它不會因為不確定，就不斷產生新的 plan。

### Tool contract：model 提議，runtime 決定

Model 可以提議 tool call，但 runtime 才決定提議能不能執行。一份有用的 **tool contract** 會寫清楚：

- tool 名稱和目的；
- input schema 和可接受值；
- effect 是 read-only、draft-only，還是有後果的 action；
- caller identity 和 permission boundary；
- timeout、retry class、idempotency requirement 和 expected output schema；
- success、failure 或 ambiguity 之後可到哪一個 state。

例如 `find_policy_evidence` 只能接收 case category 和 approved document version，回傳 citation，而且是 read-only。`create_review_task` 則需要 stable `action_id`、要拒絕 duplicate creation，並且只能回傳 confirmed task reference 或明確的 unknown state。Prompt 不是 permission system；contract 才是。

可以把它想成一位願意幫忙的 intern 拿著 request form。他可以建議打開哪一個抽屜，但實際可以打開哪些抽屜，由有標籤的 key cabinet 和 supervisor 決定。

### Trace 是營運收據，不是秘密對話逐字稿

保留足夠資料，讓日後能回答：「這個 case 為什麼走這條 route？」最小 trace 可以包括：

```text
run_id、case_version、policy_version、state transitions、
tool name、安全的 input summary、action_id、tool result class、
latency slices、token/cost proxy、terminal reason、reviewer outcome
```

不要預設儲存完整客戶文字、raw secret，或每一句 model 想法。目標是在 data minimisation 下重建 decision 和找 regression。一條 `tool_requested → unknown_after_timeout → handoff` 的 trace，比一大段掩蓋了外部 effect 是否完成的 chat transcript 更有用。

## P99 是對使用者的承諾，不是 benchmark trophy

P50 表示一般 latency；P99 描述 slow tail：那一小部分讓 reviewer 等到離開 workflow 或一直按 refresh 的 request。目標應由 user decision 推導，不是由 model leaderboard 決定。

先為這個虛構 Desk 同意一份 synthetic user-facing budget，才調整任何 serving knob：

| Budget slice | 包含什麼 | 要收集的證據 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Admission | validation、policy check、queue wait | queue timestamp 和 rejection reason |
| Context | retrieval、prompt assembly | retrieved count、context size、cache decision |
| First visible result | model prefill 加 first decode step | time to first token 或 first structured event |
| Completion | 其餘 decoding 和 output validation | total latency、output size、schema result |
| Recovery | retry lookup、route 或 handoff creation | reason、attempt、terminal state |

Budget 是 design constraint，不是偷偷刪除 safety check 的藉口。如果 case 無法及時產生有 evidence 支持的 draft，清楚的 `HANDOFF` 可以比快速但沒有引用的答案好。Latency 旁邊要量 handoff rate，否則「更快」可能只是「我們更常放棄」。

## Prefill 和 decode 為什麼造成不同 bottleneck

Autoregressive language model 先處理既有 prompt，這段叫 **prefill**。它通常受 input context 影響：過長的 history、太多 retrieved passages，或重複加入的 policy instruction，都會拖慢第一個 output。之後 **decode** 才逐 token 產生文字；一份長 draft 因此可能 first token 還可以，total completion 卻很慢。

這個差別會改變診斷：

- first response 慢，先看 queueing、context length、retrieval fan-out、prompt reuse 和 prefill capacity；
- first response 快但完成慢，先看 expected output length、structured-output repair loop、decoding capacity 和 streaming；
- 只有 load 高才兩邊都慢，先看 admission control 和 batch scheduling，不要急著怪 model。

Streaming 適合在 final validated draft 前，讓 user 看得到安全的進度。它不代表可以 stream 未驗證 policy advice 或未完成的 write action；產品要先決定哪一個 event 能被看見。

## Serving levers，各有代價

Batching、caching、quantisation、scaling 常被當成一套「加速按鈕」，其實每樣解決的 constraint 不同。

| Lever | 可能改善 | 可能變差 | 留下前要檢查 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dynamic batching | throughput、hardware utilisation | 單一但緊急 request 的 queue wait 和 P99 | 依 traffic class 比較 P50、P95、P99、queue delay |
| Prefix / prompt cache | 重複的穩定 instruction 和 context prefix | prefix 一變，hit rate 下降；舊 policy 可能被重用 | version policy prefix，記錄 hit/miss |
| Response cache | 重複、安全且 deterministic 的問法 | 錯誤 reuse、privacy leak、stale answer | 只 cache 有界 key，連 source/version validity 一起驗證 |
| KV cache | decode 時不重算已見 token state | memory pressure 限制 batch size 和 context | 記錄 cache memory、output length、eviction behaviour |
| Quantisation | memory footprint，有時也改善 throughput | task quality、numerical compatibility 或少見 case behaviour | 前後跑同一組 quality 和 safety cases |

這些都不能取代較簡單的 baseline：縮短 approved context、回傳精簡 structured draft，或把低 evidence case 交給 reviewer。Optimization 是有 error budget 的 product decision，不是一堆聰明的 switches。

## Retry 前先有 identity，不是先求快

Failure 要按「知道了什麼」分類：

- input schema 被拒，通常要修正 input 才能再做；
- rate limit 可以是有上限 delay 的 retryable case；
- read-only search timeout，在 contract 允許下可 retry；
- 有後果 action timeout，屬於 **unknown outcome**，不是自動 retry。

對有後果的 tool，call 前要產生 stable idempotency key。出現 ambiguity 時，先向 tool 或 durable state store 查這個 key 有沒有產生 effect。如果安全地仍然無法知道，就 handoff。這比樂觀 retry 慢，但避免 duplicate ticket、message 或 refund。

Execution budget 不只 token：還要有最大 state transition、tool attempt、wall-clock time 和 cost proxy。用完 budget，要留下 reviewer 能行動的 reason；不要把 loop 藏在 progress spinner 後面。

## 人員在架構中的位置

Human handoff 要寫進 contract。這個虛構 Desk 會在以下情況 handoff：

- policy source 矛盾，或不足以支持 proposed answer；
- 一個可能造成 effect 的 tool timeout 後 state 不明；
- case 超出已聲明 category；
- latency、cost 或 retry budget 已用完；
- action 會改變外部 record 或 message。

Handoff packet 要有已有的 draft、supporting evidence、terminal reason、安全 trace reference 和一位有名字的 owner。「已升級給人」但沒有目的地，只是另一種 terminal error。

## 在 claim 改善 serving 前，先建立 evidence

先用 synthetic case 和 deterministic tool fixture。小型 evaluation table 至少有：normal short context、normal long context、cache hit、cache miss、retrieval timeout、rate limit、duplicate action ID、unknown write result、policy conflict 和 budget exhaustion。

每個 case 都要記錄：

- expected terminal state 和 forbidden state transition；
- allowed tool path 和 action identity；
- time to first event、total latency、queue delay 和 output size；
- cache / batching condition；
- draft quality rule、citation rule 和 reviewer route；
- 這個 test **沒有** 證明什麼。

把 state diagram、contract schema、trace field、load fixture 和 latency report 放進同一個 review pack，再連同 user decision、data boundary、error cost、handoff owner 和 stop condition。reviewer 就可以同時核對系統怎麼跑，以及應該在哪裡停。

## 一段能接受追問的回答

> 「我會先以 bounded state machine 和 tool contract 起步，不會做 open-ended loop。每個 tool 都有 input/output schema、permission level、timeout、retry class 和 idempotency rule。我會 trace state transition、安全的 tool evidence、latency slices 和 terminal reason，同時 minimising sensitive data。Serving 方面，我會把 user-facing P99 拆成 queueing、context/prefill、decode、validation 和 recovery 的 budget。我會用同一組固定 quality 和 safety case 檢查 batching、caching、KV-cache memory 和 quantisation，而不是只看 latency。若有後果的 tool timeout，我會查 stable action identity；effect 不明就 handoff。第一版保持 draft-only，並有 named reviewer 負責 conflict、budget stop 和不可逆 action。」

這段回答顯示你知道 model behaviour、runtime control、operations 和真正 owner 如何放在同一個系統。

## Repository 應保留的 artefacts

- `brief.md`：虛構 decision、user、data boundary、non-goal 和 reviewer owner。
- `state-machine.md`：合法 state、transition、terminal reason，以及永遠不能發生的事。
- `tool-contracts/`：schema、permission、timeout、retry class、action ID 和 output validator。
- `trace-schema.md`：保留和刻意排除的 field，以及 retention rationale。
- `latency-budget.md`：P99 slices、traffic assumption、queue policy 和 miss budget 後的 decision。
- `synthetic-evals/`：normal、slow、ambiguous、duplicate 和 blocked case 的固定 fixture。
- `results.md`：quality、handoff、route、latency、cache 和 cost-proxy result，包括一個 failure。
- `decision-log.md`：為什麼選這個 cache、batch rule 或 handoff threshold，以及仍未證明什麼。

延伸閱讀可先看 [workflow-level agent evaluation](/zh-TW/articles/evaluate-an-ai-agent-workflow-not-just-the-final-answer)，再實作更窄的 [可 resume batch worker](/zh-TW/articles/build-a-resumable-ai-batch-worker)。配合 [agent 取得 permission 前的 review](/zh-TW/articles/review-an-ai-agent-before-clicking-allow)，以及 [Transformer、generation 和 serving 的取捨](/zh-TW/articles/choose-transformer-generation-and-adaptation-tradeoffs)。

## 邊界與來源說明

這是 AI.DOG 教學，以 synthetic、draft-only scenario 解釋。它不是 production architecture、benchmark result、provider capacity claim，也不承諾任何 latency、reliability、business outcome 或 interview result。本文的 tool、data、budget、state label 和 artefact 都是示範。真實系統需要自己的 security review、privacy assessment、provider documentation、workload measurement、incident process 和已授權 owner，才可以影響客戶或外部 record。

> 「我会先用 bounded state machine 和 tool contract 起步，不会做 open-ended loop。每个 tool 都有 input/output schema、permission level、timeout、retry class 和 idempotency rule。我会 trace state transition、安全的 tool evidence、latency slices 和 terminal reason，同时 minimising sensitive data。Serving 方面，我会把 user-facing P99 拆成 queueing、context/prefill、decode、validation 和 recovery 的 budget。我会用同一组固定 quality 和 safety case 检查 batching、caching、KV-cache memory 和 quantisation，而不是只看 latency。若有后果的 tool timeout，我会查 stable action identity；effect 不明就 handoff。第一版保持 draft-only，并有 named reviewer 负责 conflict、budget stop 和不可逆 action。」

这段回答显示你知道 model behaviour、runtime control、operations 和真正 owner 如何放在同一个系统。

## Repository 应保留的 artefacts

- `brief.md`：虚构 decision、user、data boundary、non-goal 和 reviewer owner。
- `state-machine.md`：合法 state、transition、terminal reason，以及永远不能发生的事。
- `tool-contracts/`：schema、permission、timeout、retry class、action ID 和 output validator。
- `trace-schema.md`：保留和刻意排除的 field，以及 retention rationale。
- `latency-budget.md`：P99 slices、traffic assumption、queue policy 和 miss budget 后的 decision。
- `synthetic-evals/`：normal、slow、ambiguous、duplicate 和 blocked case 的固定 fixture。
- `results.md`：quality、handoff、route、latency、cache 和 cost-proxy result，包括一个 failure。
- `decision-log.md`：为什么选这个 cache、batch rule 或 handoff threshold，以及仍未证明什么。

延伸阅读可先看 [workflow-level agent evaluation](/zh-Hans/articles/evaluate-an-ai-agent-workflow-not-just-the-final-answer)，再实现更窄的 [可 resume batch worker](/zh-Hans/articles/build-a-resumable-ai-batch-worker)。配合 [agent 获得 permission 前的 review](/zh-Hans/articles/review-an-ai-agent-before-clicking-allow)，以及 [Transformer、generation 和 serving 的取舍](/zh-Hans/articles/choose-transformer-generation-and-adaptation-tradeoffs)。

## 边界与来源说明

这是 AI.DOG 教学，以 synthetic、draft-only scenario 解释。它不是 production architecture、benchmark result、provider capacity claim，也不承诺任何 latency、reliability、business outcome 或 interview result。本文的 tool、data、budget、state label 和 artefact 都是示范。真实系统需要自己的 security review、privacy assessment、provider documentation、workload measurement、incident process 和已授权 owner，才可以影响客户或外部 record。
agent-execution-and-serving.en:
> A fast-looking agent is not necessarily a dependable one. If it cannot stop, explain the tool it used, recover without repeating an effect, and leave room for a person to decide, lower latency only helps it make the wrong move sooner.

## The 4:47 pm request that exposes two different systems

Imagine a fictional **Returns Evidence Desk**. A support reviewer pastes an already-sanitised order summary and asks for a draft that names the policy evidence, suggests the next internal route, and never contacts the customer. The first demo is pleasant: the agent searches a tiny approved policy set, writes a draft, and returns it in a few seconds.

At 4:47 pm, three things change at once. The queue grows, one retrieval call times out after it may already have recorded a review task, and a long pasted history delays the first visible word. The question is no longer “can the model write?” It is:

> “How would you design this agent so that it can stop safely while its serving layer still meets a user-facing P99 latency budget?”

That question joins two disciplines which are often discussed separately. **Agent execution** decides what may happen next. **Model serving** decides how work reaches the model and how long it takes. A reliable design connects them through a shared budget, stable state, and named human authority.

## The answer that fixes only half the problem

> “I would add retries, more replicas, and streaming.”

Those can be useful tools. They are not a recovery plan.

More replicas do not tell an agent when a request should stop. Streaming makes the first text visible sooner, but does not make an unsafe tool call reversible. Retrying a write whose result is unknown can create the same review task twice. A faster model still gives a bad user experience if queueing consumes the whole P99 budget before the model starts.

Start by defining the bounded job, then make every transition inspectable.

## One run is a state machine, not a loop around a model

The Returns Evidence Desk has no permission to send a message, modify a return, or access an account. Its only possible product is a draft for a reviewer. A small state machine is enough to make that boundary visible:

```text
received
  -> validated
  -> planned
  -> tool_requested
  -> observed
  -> draft_ready
  -> handoff
  -> blocked
  -> retry_scheduled
  -> budget_stopped
```

Only some arrows are legal. A missing policy source goes from `observed` to `handoff`, not to invented prose. An expired time budget goes to `budget_stopped`, not back to `planned`. A tool timeout is not proof that nothing happened; it goes to a state where the system can check a stable action identity before deciding whether a retry is safe.

This is what “stoppable” means in practice. The agent has explicit terminal states, a reason code, and an owner for the next decision. It does not keep generating plans because it feels uncertain.

### A tool contract turns model suggestions into bounded actions

A model may propose a tool call. The runtime decides whether that proposal is admissible. A useful **tool contract** says:

- the tool name and purpose;
- the input schema and allowed values;
- whether the effect is read-only, draft-only, or consequential;
- the caller identity and permission boundary;
- a timeout, retry class, idempotency requirement, and expected output schema;
- which state transition can follow success, failure, or ambiguity.

For example, `find_policy_evidence` can accept a case category and approved document version, return citations, and be read-only. `create_review_task` would require a stable `action_id`, reject duplicate creation, and return either a confirmed task reference or an explicit unknown state. A prompt is not the permission system; the contract is.

Picture a helpful intern holding a request form. They can suggest which drawer to open, but a labelled key cabinet and the supervisor decide which drawers can actually be opened.

### A trace is an operational receipt, not a secret transcript

Keep enough information to answer, later, “why did this case take this route?” A minimal trace might include:

```text
run_id, case_version, policy_version, state transitions,
tool name, safe input summary, action_id, tool result class,
latency slices, token/cost proxy, terminal reason, reviewer outcome
```

Do not default to saving full customer text, raw secrets, or every model thought. The point is to reconstruct decisions and find regressions while respecting data minimisation. A trace that says `tool_requested → unknown_after_timeout → handoff` is more useful than a long chat transcript that hides the uncertain external effect.

## P99 exposes the slow requests that can miss a wait-time target

P50 describes a typical latency. P99 tells you about the slow tail: the requests that may make a reviewer wait long enough to abandon a workflow or click refresh. The target should come from the user decision, not from a model leaderboard.

For this fictional desk, agree a synthetic user-facing budget before tuning anything:

| Budget slice | What it covers | Evidence to collect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Admission | validation, policy check, queue wait | queue timestamp and rejection reason |
| Context | retrieval and prompt assembly | retrieved count, context size, cache decision |
| First visible result | model prefill plus first decode step | time to first token or first structured event |
| Completion | remaining decoding and output validation | total latency, output size, schema result |
| Recovery | retry lookup, route, or handoff creation | reason, attempts, terminal state |

The budget is a design constraint, not an excuse to silently cut safety checks. If a case cannot get a supported draft in time, a clear `HANDOFF` can be better than an uncited fast answer. Measure handoff rate beside latency so that “faster” does not merely mean “we gave up more often.”

## Why prefill and decode create different bottlenecks

An autoregressive language model first processes the existing prompt. That **prefill** work is usually dominated by the input context: a large pasted history, long retrieved passages, or an unnecessarily repeated policy instruction can delay the first output. During **decode**, the model produces new tokens step by step. A long draft can therefore have acceptable time to first token but poor total completion time.

This distinction changes the diagnosis:

- When first response is slow, inspect queueing, context length, retrieval fan-out, prompt reuse, and prefill capacity.
- When the first response is prompt but completion is slow, inspect expected output length, structured-output repair loops, decoding capacity, and streaming behaviour.
- When both are slow only under load, inspect admission control and batch scheduling before claiming the model itself is the cause.

Streaming is useful when a user can safely see progress before the final validated draft. It is not a licence to stream unverified policy advice or an incomplete write action. The product must decide which event is safe to reveal.

## Serving levers have different costs

The same four words—batching, caching, quantisation, scaling—often get repeated as if each automatically improves latency. They solve different constraints.

| Lever | What it can improve | What can get worse | A check before keeping it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dynamic batching | throughput and hardware utilisation | queue wait and P99 for a lonely urgent request | compare P50, P95, P99 and queue delay by traffic class |
| Prefix or prompt cache | repeated stable instructions and repeated context prefixes | hit rate falls when prefixes vary; stale policy can be reused | version the policy prefix and record cache hit/miss |
| Response cache | repeated, safe, deterministic questions | wrong reuse, privacy leakage, stale answer | cache only a bounded key and include source/version validity |
| KV cache | avoids recomputing prior token states during decode | memory pressure limits batch size and context | record cache memory, output length, and eviction behaviour |
| Quantisation | memory footprint and sometimes throughput | task quality, numerical compatibility, or rare-case behaviour | run the same fixed quality and safety cases before/after |

None of these replaces a simpler baseline: shorten the approved context, return a compact structured draft, or route low-confidence cases to a reviewer. Optimisation is a product decision with an error budget, not a collection of clever switches.

## Retries need identity before speed

Treat failures according to what is known.

- A rejected input schema is usually permanent until the input is corrected.
- A rate-limit response may be retryable with a capped delay.
- A timeout after a read-only search may be retried if the contract permits it.
- A timeout after a consequential action is an **unknown outcome**, not an automatic retry.

For a consequential tool, generate a stable idempotency key before the call. On ambiguity, ask the tool or durable state store whether that key has already produced the effect. If the state cannot be determined safely, hand off. This is slower than an optimistic retry, but it avoids duplicate tickets, messages, or refunds.

An execution budget should include more than tokens: maximum state transitions, tool attempts, wall-clock time, and cost proxy. When a budget expires, emit a reason that a reviewer can act on. Do not hide a loop behind a progress spinner.

## Where the human sits in the architecture

Write the human handoff into the system contract. This fictional desk hands off when:

- policy sources conflict or do not support a proposed answer;
- a tool’s state is unknown after a possible effect;
- the case is outside the declared category;
- the latency, cost, or retry budget is spent;
- the action would change an external record or message.

The handoff packet needs the draft if one exists, supporting evidence, terminal reason, safe trace reference, and a named owner. “Escalated to a human” without a destination is only another terminal error.

## Build evidence before claiming you improved serving

Use synthetic cases and deterministic tool fixtures first. A useful small evaluation table includes normal short context, normal long context, cache hit, cache miss, retrieval timeout, rate limit, duplicate action ID, unknown write result, policy conflict, and budget exhaustion.

For every case, record:

- expected terminal state and forbidden state transition;
- allowed tool path and action identity;
- time to first event, total latency, queue delay, and output size;
- cache and batching condition;
- draft quality rule, citation rule, and reviewer route;
- what the test does **not** show.

Put the state diagram, contract schemas, trace fields, load fixture, and latency report in one review pack, alongside the user decision, data boundary, error cost, handoff owner, and stop condition. A reviewer can then check how the system runs and where it must stop.

## A concise answer that invites a useful follow-up

> “I would begin with a bounded state machine and tool contracts, not an open-ended loop. Each tool has an input/output schema, permission level, timeout, retry class, and idempotency rule. I would trace state transitions, safe tool evidence, latency slices, and terminal reasons, while minimising sensitive data. For serving, I would set a user-facing P99 budget split across queueing, context/prefill, decode, validation, and recovery. I would test batching, caching, KV-cache memory, and quantisation against the same fixed quality and safety cases, not latency alone. If a consequential tool times out, I would check a stable action identity and hand off when the effect is unknown. The first release stays draft-only, with a named reviewer for conflicts, budget stops, and irreversible actions.”

That answer shows how model behaviour, runtime control, operations, and a real owner fit together.

## Keep these artefacts in the repository

- `brief.md` — fictional decision, user, data boundary, non-goals, and reviewer owner.
- `state-machine.md` — legal states, transitions, terminal reasons, and what must never happen.
- `tool-contracts/` — schemas, permissions, timeouts, retry classes, action IDs, and output validators.
- `trace-schema.md` — retained fields, deliberately excluded fields, and retention rationale.
- `latency-budget.md` — P99 slices, traffic assumptions, queue policy, and the decision if the budget is missed.
- `synthetic-evals/` — fixed fixtures for normal, slow, ambiguous, duplicate, and blocked cases.
- `results.md` — quality, handoff, route, latency, cache, and cost-proxy results, including one failure.
- `decision-log.md` — why a cache, batch rule, or handoff threshold was chosen and what remains unproven.

For related practice, start with [workflow-level agent evaluation](/en/articles/evaluate-an-ai-agent-workflow-not-just-the-final-answer), then build a narrower [resumable batch worker](/en/articles/build-a-resumable-ai-batch-worker). Pair either one with [permission review before an agent gets access](/en/articles/review-an-ai-agent-before-clicking-allow) and [the Transformer and serving trade-offs behind generation](/en/articles/choose-transformer-generation-and-adaptation-tradeoffs).

## Boundary and source note

This is AI.DOG teaching material built from a synthetic, draft-only scenario. It is not a production architecture, benchmark result, provider-capacity claim, or a promise of a particular latency, reliability, business outcome, or interview result. Tool names, data, budgets, state labels, and artefacts here are illustrative. A real system needs its own security review, privacy assessment, provider documentation, workload measurement, incident process, and authorised owner before it can affect a customer or external record.

multimodal-product-boundaries.zh-HK:
> 一張清晰文件相、一段語音，配上一個看似準確的回答，很容易令人以為「多模態 AI 已經做到」。交付時要回答的是：它究竟可不可以讀、讀到的是甚麼、哪一步要停低，以及誰有權把結果變成行動；model 能描述 input 只是一小部分。

## 把 demo 收窄成一個可審核的工作

用一個**完全虛構**的例子練習：營運同事收到一張預約更改表格的影像、PDF 或語音留言。系統唯一工作，是把可核對的資料整理成草稿，交給職員覆核；它不會自行改預約、發訊息或建立客戶紀錄。

最小流程可以寫成：

`input → 類型與質素檢查 → 擷取候選欄位 → 規則檢查 → DRAFT／REVIEW／BLOCKED → 職員決定`

這條線比「我用了 vision model」重要。每一個 node 都有一個可驗收的責任：input 是否容許處理、欄位是否有來源、結果是否完整、以及甚麼情況必須交人。model 只是其中一個可替換元件。

## 影像、文件和語音不是同一種 input

**影像**可能有光線、反光、裁切、旋轉和手寫字問題。它可以包含文字，亦可以只是現場相片；不要因為看見一個盒子就推論當中資料可讀或可用。保留頁面或區域位置，讓 reviewer 知道某個候選欄位從哪裏來。

**文件**多一層 layout：一份掃描 PDF 可能有多頁、頁眉、表格、版本號和附件。OCR 或 vision extraction 可以把字變成候選資料，卻不會自動知道哪一頁才是最新表格。檔名、檔案類型和文件版本都應是 input metadata，不是事後猜測。

**語音**不是一句已經乾淨的文字。先有音訊品質、語言、說話速度、背景噪音、時間點和 transcription。系統可以把「星期二下午」變成一段有 timestamp 的候選內容；它不應從聲線推論身份、情緒、能力或其他不在任務內的特徵。

三種 input 最終都可以輸出同一個 schema，例如 `requested_date`、`reference_id`、`evidence_pointer` 和 `route`。但取得這些欄位的證據不同，所以不可只用一個「整體準確率」遮蓋所有錯誤。

## 把質素、延遲和 route 分開量

用一組合成 fixtures 開始，不要上傳任何真實文件或錄音。可以有清晰打字表格、旋轉或模糊頁面、缺少關鍵欄位的附件、背景嘈雜的語音，以及根本不屬於任務的 input。每個 fixture 都寫明預期 route 和 reviewer 可以核對的 evidence。

質素至少分三條看：

- **欄位正確性**：日期、參考編號或名稱是否符合 fixture，而不是只看整段摘要像不像；
- **route 正確性**：缺資料、低可讀性或錯誤文件有沒有去 `REVIEW` 或 `BLOCKED`；以及
- **證據完整性**：每個重要欄位能否連回頁碼、區域或語音 timestamp。

延遲也要拆開。upload、影像預處理、轉錄、model request 和 reviewer 畫面各自消耗時間。寫下可接受的等待預算，並量 p50 和 p95；沒有量到的數字就留作假設，不要把 demo 感覺快寫成效能證明。若語音 transcript 未完成，流程可以顯示「仍在處理」或直接交人，毋須逼 model 猜一個答案。

## 私隱不是把 input 交給 model 後才補救

相片、掃描文件和錄音往往比純文字更容易帶出不必要資料：背景的人、地址、簽名、帳戶號碼或說話者的聲音。設計要從最小資料開始：任務需要哪一頁、哪一段聲音、哪些欄位？不需要的就不要收、不要存、不要放入 prompt。

作品集只可用合成或已公開而且可合法重用的素材。README 應寫明 input 不可包含甚麼、誰可看原始檔、保留多久、trace 可以記錄甚麼，以及示範環境沒有連接真實帳戶。redaction 或加密是可加的控制，但不是用來合理化一個本來不應收集的 input。

## fallback 的目標是保留決定，而不是假裝自動化

一個好 fallback 不只是「信心低就重試」。它要講清楚哪個判斷無法成立，以及下一個人會得到甚麼。例子：`reference_id` 被遮住、同一頁出現兩個日期、語音有噪音令關鍵詞不清楚，或文件類型不在允許清單內。系統應輸出 `REVIEW` 或 `BLOCKED`，附上頁碼、crop 或 timestamp、已擷取的候選值和不確定原因。

reviewer 可以確認、改正或拒絕草稿。這個決定要有 case ID、input version、流程版本和 route reason，方便回看問題在 input、extraction rule 還是工作定義。不要把每次人手改正自動當成可拿去訓練的資料；首先要確認同意、用途和資料管治。

## 作品集要展示的不是一段漂亮輸出

一個可信的 multimodal evidence pack 可以包括：

- input taxonomy，列出支援和拒絕的影像、文件及語音種類；
- 一組 versioned synthetic fixtures，以及每個 fixture 的預期欄位、evidence pointer 和 route；
- acceptance matrix，分開欄位正確性、route、證據和 latency budget；
- privacy note，列出資料最小化、保留和 access boundary；以及
- 一張 human-handoff screen 或 trace 範例，顯示人如何理解和完成未完成的 case。

技術上，這證明你能設計 schema、fixtures、checks 和 trace。非技術上，它證明你知道「減少人手重新輸入」不等於取得自動改紀錄的權限。這比用真實私隱 input 做一個華麗 demo 更適合公開作品集。

## 邊界

這是學習用的 synthetic flow，不是醫療、身份驗證、監控、招聘或任何真實公司的處理建議。沒有真實 input、真實 model call、真人聲音或部署結果，就不要聲稱達到某個準確率、延遲、私隱合規或商業成效。把 case 變得可檢查後，才決定是否值得加更多模型能力。
