**完成后仍不能宣称什么：** 已验证其他 provider、真实资料分布、成本、合规或组织批准。cloud learning path 不是 production evidence。

## 用同一张 receipt，选一条而不是收集五个 badge

每次开始新来源时，都保留一张英文 source receipt。程序、fixture、config 和 file name 保持英文，让 reviewer 能重跑；README 再按读者需要做不同语言版本。

```text
Source title and official URL:
Accessed on:
Evidence gap I am addressing:
Prerequisites and account/cost boundary I checked:
One lesson or section I used:
My independently authored Week-1 artefact:
Synthetic/public data boundary:
Five fixed cases or checks:
Feedback or review route:
What failed, remains unknown, or must stop:
What this artefact does not prove:
```

这张 receipt 把“我看过某个 course”变成“我如何把一个来源转成可 review 的 engineering decision”。它也保护你不会把 instructor solution、course wording 或 certificate，假装成完全原创的 commercial work。

## 一个简单的选择规则

如果你还不能解释 agent 的组成，先从 Hugging Face fundamentals 开始；问题是 state、handoff 或 interrupt 时，看 LangGraph；想理解 hosted session/event 的真正边界，就读 OpenAI quickstart，但不要急着加 key；需要固定 case 和 regression evidence，就先做 Promptfoo fixture-only pack；想补 evaluation methodology，再考虑 Microsoft Learn。

不论选哪条路，第一周只做一份可检查 artefact。当你无法写 expected result、需要真实私人资料、需要连账户、需要花钱、需要向外发送资料，或没有人愿意拥有最后 decision 时，就先 STOP。缩小 task 比多加一个 framework 更有价值。

已有一个具名来源想核对？先用[学习证据规划器](/zh-Hans/learning-evidence-planner)记下缺口、官方页、第一份成果和停止条件；它不替供应商排位。

延伸阅读：[按职位与 evidence gap 选学习来源](/zh-Hans/articles/choose-an-ai-learning-source-by-role-and-evidence-gap)、[把课程作业变成可追问 portfolio evidence](/zh-Hans/articles/turn-an-ai-course-project-into-portfolio-evidence)、[LLM eval、human review 与 observability](/zh-Hans/articles/llm-evals-human-review-and-observability)、[按 Allow 前的 permission review](/zh-Hans/articles/review-an-ai-agent-before-clicking-allow)，或由 [不写 Code／coder 两条 AI 构建路线](/zh-Hans/series/ai-use-routes) 选今天可安全完成的一步。

## 边界与更新说明

以上是官方来源的当日收据，不是永久产品规格。账户、price、lesson、licence、region access 与 prerequisite 都可能改变；投入金钱、上传资料或建立账户前，请回官方页面再次核对。本站所有例子都是虚构、local-first 或 fixture-only 练习，没有执行 API call、没有处理真实个人／雇主资料，也不保证课程、portfolio 或求职结果。
agent-eval-source-receipts.en:
Do not begin with “Which AI course is best?” Begin with the evidence gap you need to close: do you need to explain an agent loop, make workflow state and human handoff visible, interpret runtime events, or keep a rerunnable evaluation case? A course, framework, or documentation page is learning input. Your goal is an inspectable judgement you can carry forward.

## Five official source receipts, not a course ranking

These are five official starting points checked on 2026-09-25. They are not affiliate links, a recommended order, a job guarantee, or a syllabus you must finish. Each receipt is paired with a Week-1 exercise that asks you to turn one idea you studied into evidence using only synthetic or public-safe material. It is a learner-scoped exercise, not a provider-endorsed result or a statement about what a course delivers.

Start by choosing the statement that is closest to your current gap:

- I want to explain tools, observations, and an agent loop without only repeating vocabulary.
- I need to make routes, state, memory, and human handoff reviewable.
- I need to understand runtime events, sandboxes, and cleanup without treating “completed” as success.
- I need to turn “the answer looks okay” into fixed cases, assertions, and a reviewer note.
- I want a more formal evaluation method, but am not ready to connect real data or accounts.

## 1. Learn the shared language of agents: Hugging Face AI Agents Course

The [Hugging Face AI Agents Course](https://huggingface.co/learn/agents-course/unit0/introduction) brings together agent fundamentals, popular libraries, hands-on work, assignments, challenges, and an evaluation/observability unit. Its stated starting point includes basic Python and basic LLM knowledge; a Hugging Face account is needed to use the Hub or Spaces.

Use it when you need to distinguish a **tool**, **thought**, **action**, and **observation** before trying to claim you have built an autonomous agent.

**Keep this in Week 1:** write three synthetic FAQ or role cards of your own, then draw a small `input → allowed tool → observation → draft → human decision` path. Add three cases: complete information, missing information, and a request for a prohibited action. Give every case an expected route: `DRAFT`, `HANDOFF`, or `BLOCKED`.

**What someone can inspect:** a tool contract, an input boundary, visible routes, and the human decision an agent cannot bypass.

**What completion still does not prove:** that you have an enterprise agent, selected the right framework, made every tool safe, or can deliver production work. A challenge or certificate is not the same as your portfolio evidence.

## 2. Practise state and a human gate: LangGraph Foundation

[LangChain Academy’s Introduction to LangGraph](https://academy.langchain.com/courses/intro-to-langgraph) publicly lists material on simple graphs, routers, agents, state schemas, memory, breakpoints, human feedback, and deployment concepts. The page currently lists the course as free, with 55 lessons and about six hours of video; it also says the LangGraph library is MIT-licensed. Neither fact grants a licence to course prose, an associated cloud service, or a model provider you connect.

Use it when you already have some Python and need to move beyond a chat loop to ask **who can change state, where a process pauses, and who can override a decision**.

**Keep this in Week 1:** create a small workflow state card with `received`, `needs-evidence`, `draft-ready`, `review-required`, and `stopped`. Allow a synthetic request to move from `draft-ready` to `review-required` only; then let a named reviewer choose `PASS`, `REVISE`, or `STOP`. Retain a transition table and one rejected transition.

**What someone can inspect:** a state schema, an owner for every transition, an interrupt point, and a failure record.

**What completion still does not prove:** production orchestration, reliable long-term memory, deployment, or that a human-in-the-loop button solves permissions, data rights, cost, or incident handling.

## 3. Learn managed-runtime evidence: OpenAI Agents API quickstart

The [OpenAI Agents API quickstart](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/quickstart) demonstrates creating a session, running work in a hosted sandbox, streaming events, and cleaning up. The official prerequisites list an API key with particular permission scopes and a beta header. It also explicitly says that a completed turn does not mean every tool succeeded.

This route is only appropriate when you have programming experience and clear authority for API use, spend, and data. You do **not** need a key to learn the first judgement a portfolio should show.

**Keep this in Week 1:** do not make a live call. Write an English `session-receipt.md` for a fictional, local-only task with expected events: `started`, `tool-requested`, `tool-result`, and `completed`/`failed`/`cancelled`. Name the events that still require human review, when cleanup occurs, and which missing result prevents a success claim. This is a static fixture design, not API output.

**What someone can inspect:** a session boundary, event interpretation, the difference between completion and success, a cleanup owner, and a credential boundary.

**What completion still does not prove:** that you ran an OpenAI API call, observed a model result, configured a safe sandbox, controlled cost, or can use the workflow with a real account. A live experiment needs separate data authority, a test set, cost control, logging, and release evidence.

## 4. Turn “looks okay” into a case matrix: Promptfoo

[Promptfoo Getting Started](https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/getting-started/) shows how a `promptfooconfig.yaml` can hold prompts, providers, and test cases, with optional assertions, evaluation runs, and output review. The page also says that many providers need authentication. A YAML file is not a reason to bring credentials, customer material, or real prompts into a public repository.

Use it when you have basic Node/CLI confidence and need **evaluation evidence**, not another polished demo.

**Keep this in Week 1:** make a key-free, fixture-only `promptfooconfig.yaml` draft with five synthetic cases: a normal request, missing source, conflicting source, hidden instruction, and prohibited action. For each one, state the expected route, visible evidence, and a `PASS`/`REVISE` rule. Start with manual review if needed; never label an unrun provider as a test result.

**What someone can inspect:** a case set, expected assertions, a failure taxonomy, a reviewer decision, and how a prompt change is compared.

**What completion still does not prove:** live-traffic quality, a business KPI, a privacy review, agent-trajectory safety, or production approval. Promptfoo is an evaluation harness; it cannot define data rights or action boundaries for you.

## 5. Learn cloud-evaluation method, not only model comparison: Microsoft Learn

[Microsoft Learn’s Evaluate generative AI applications](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/paths/evaluate-generative-ai-apps/) covers evaluation fundamentals and running evaluations/generating synthetic datasets with the Azure AI Evaluation SDK. Its listed prerequisites include an Azure subscription, familiarity with the Azure portal, beginner Python, and browser or local-development requirements such as GitHub, Docker, VS Code, and Dev Containers. The page mentions a free account/trial and pay-as-you-go, which should not be simplified into “always free.”

Use it when the gap is **an evaluation plan, quality/risk metrics, and synthetic test data**, rather than another model comparison.

**Keep this in Week 1:** create a one-page evaluation plan: a fictional user decision, five synthetic cases, one quality metric, one risk metric, the person who reads the result, and the outcome that must trigger `STOP`. You can finish this plan before opening an Azure account. It keeps “define what to accept” ahead of “turn on a service.”

**What someone can inspect:** the evaluator’s question, the link between a metric and failure mode, a synthetic-data boundary, result interpretation, and a human release decision.

**What completion still does not prove:** another provider’s behaviour, a real data distribution, cost, compliance, or organisational approval. A cloud learning path is not production evidence.

## Use one receipt to choose one path, not to collect five badges

Whenever you begin a new source, keep an English source receipt. Keep code, fixtures, configs, and filenames in English so a reviewer can rerun them; localise a README when it helps readers.

```text
Source title and official URL:
Accessed on:
Evidence gap I am addressing:
Prerequisites and account/cost boundary I checked:
One lesson or section I used:
My Week-1 artefact:
Synthetic/public data boundary:
Five fixed cases or checks:
Feedback or review route:
What failed, remains unknown, or must stop:
What this artefact does not prove:
```

The receipt turns “I watched a course” into “here is how I turned a source into a reviewable engineering decision.” It helps you distinguish learning material, your own changes, and the claims a certificate cannot support.

## A simple selection rule

If you cannot yet explain the parts of an agent, start with Hugging Face fundamentals. If your problem is state, handoff, or interruption, study LangGraph. If you need to understand the boundary around hosted sessions and events, read the OpenAI quickstart—but do not rush to add a key. If you need fixed cases and regression evidence, make a fixture-only Promptfoo pack. If you need an evaluation methodology, consider Microsoft Learn.

Whichever route you choose, make only one inspectable Week-1 artefact. Stop when you cannot state an expected result, need real private data, need to connect an account, need to spend money, need to send data outward, or have no person willing to own the final decision. Reducing the task is more valuable than adding another framework.

Already have a named source to inspect? Use the [Learning Evidence Planner](/en/learning-evidence-planner) to record the gap, official page, first artefact, and stop condition; it does not rank providers.

Further reading: [choose a learning source by role and evidence gap](/en/articles/choose-an-ai-learning-source-by-role-and-evidence-gap), [turn a course exercise into portfolio evidence](/en/articles/turn-an-ai-course-project-into-portfolio-evidence), [LLM evals, human review, and observability](/en/articles/llm-evals-human-review-and-observability), [review permissions before clicking Allow](/en/articles/review-an-ai-agent-before-clicking-allow), or choose a safe step for today in the [no-code and coder Build-with-AI routes](/en/series/ai-use-routes).

## Boundary and update note

These are current official-source receipts, not permanent product specifications. Accounts, prices, lessons, licences, regional access, and prerequisites can change; revisit each official page before spending money, uploading data, or creating an account. Every example here is fictional, local-first, or fixture-only. This site did not execute an API call, handle real personal/employer data, or promise a course, portfolio, or job outcome.

workforce-signal-brief.zh-HK:
> 呢個 portfolio build 唔係想預測勞動市場，而係想答一個更細、亦更實際嘅問題：一份來源資料齊唔齊，夠唔夠資格交畀人睇一份有邊界嘅 context brief？

## 真正要做嘅決定，比「AI 市場洞察」細好多

想像一個虛構嘅 workforce-planning research lead 收到一條公共統計來源。佢喺寫 brief 前只需要判斷一件事：**呢張 source receipt 係咪完整到可以畀人 review 一份無外部 action 嘅資料包？**

呢個刻意唔係「邊度會多工」、「公司應唔應該請人」、「應該出幾多人工」或者「一個人下一步工作應該點揀」。一張順眼嘅圖，或者一段流暢文字，本身答唔到任何一條。

[ABS Data API user guide](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/application-programming-interfaces-apis/data-api-user-guide)、[Labour Force, Australia release collection](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/labour/employment-and-unemployment/labour-force-australia) 同 [ABS citation guidance](https://www.abs.gov.au/how-cite-abs-sources) 係日後設計 acquisition 時可以核對嘅官方路線，但唔代表呢個 learning package 曾經 fetch release、query API、揀過 series，或者用過一個 current observation。

文中嘅情境、月度數值、receipt、cases 同 output 都係 source-shaped synthetic fixture。呢個作品集因此只作一個誠實主張：展示未來 briefing workflow 嘅邊界，可以點樣畀人核對。

## 先寫 source receipt，唔好先信一個似樣嘅數字

source receipt 係一張短紀錄，畀 reviewer 睇到咩嘢真係收到、咩嘢仲未證實。一張有用嘅 receipt 會有：

- 預定官方來源路線同 citation key；
- 日後 owner 要確認嘅 series identity、reference period、unit、adjustment 同 retrieval rule；
- 咩 fields 可以入 packet，咩 private 或 operational fields 必須 reject；
- freshness rule、schema version 同 fixture identity；同埋
- 邊個人負責判斷 source suitability、interpretation 同任何將來嘅 release。

呢個 local reference 用虛構 geography，同每個數值標示 `synthetic`；manifest 寫嘅係 `synthetic_source_shaped_not_live_acquired`，唔係一個 current statistic。receipt 未齊、超出佢自己定嘅 freshness rule、period 亂序、冇 unit，或者帶咗 private field，正確結果係 reject，唔係硬補一段聽落合理嘅說明。

```text
source receipt + source-shaped synthetic series
  -> metadata、order、freshness、private-field checks
  -> CONTEXT_BRIEF_READY 或 SOURCE_REJECTED
  -> 畀 human reviewer 嘅 no-action context packet
  -> fixed cases、change comparison、release/rollback evidence
```

`CONTEXT_BRIEF_READY` 只係准許你畀人睇一份收窄咗嘅 packet，唔係 forecast、causal explanation、hiring recommendation、salary decision、個人工作選擇建議、policy recommendation、publication 或任何 external action。

## Model 前面先有一份 deterministic packet

最細嘅 baseline 完全唔使 LLM。佢只保留 allowlisted facts、清楚標示數值係 synthetic、計一個簡單 period-to-period difference，再留低 human reviewer 要核對嘅問題。佢唔可以自己補 trend、補 missing context，或者將一個 difference 變成建議。

所以，你可以喺 prose 入系統之前，先固定下面嘅 cases：

| Case | 必須有嘅行為 |
| --- | --- |
| Complete synthetic receipt | 回傳有 synthetic label 同 reviewer questions 嘅 context packet |
| Missing unit 或 unordered period | build packet 前已 reject |
| Stale receipt | reject，並講明係 freshness failure |
| Private field | reject，唔可以投影入 output |
| 藏喺 source text 入面嘅 instruction | 唔可以改變 route |
| Forecast request | 拒絕要求，維持 no-action boundary |

呢啲先係 interviewer 或 reviewer 真係追到嘅工程證據：data contract、allowed fields、reject path、result schema，同埋你改 prompt 或 parser 後仍然穩定嘅 cases。佢比一張靚答案 screenshot 更有用。

## GPT-5 mini 同 Promptfoo 應該擺喺邊——又唔應該當成乜

案例保留咗一個 optional `gpt-5-mini` Responses request shape，畀 reviewer 睇到日後可能接入嘅 seam。佢係 static、non-executing：冇 API key、冇 SDK call、冇 network request、冇 model output。[GPT-5 mini 文件](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5-mini) 講到 model surface，但絕對唔會證明呢個 workforce use case 適合、安全、有效或者 ready to release。

Promptfoo 都要分開理解。local fixture configuration 可以描述固定 input、assertions、result shape 同 deterministic provider，而完全唔 call provider。另一份 optional Responses configuration 係日後 execution choice，要另行有 authority、key handling、data review、cost decision 同 release gate。[Promptfoo configuration guide](https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/configuration/guide/) 同 [OpenAI provider guide](https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/providers/openai/) 只係工具文件，唔係呢個項目嘅 run result。

如果日後真係獲授權接 model，佢只可以收到 allowlisted packet、回 strict schema、保留 synthetic label；一 forecast、講咗冇 source 支持嘅 explanation、加咗 private context，或者建議 external action，就應該 reject。deterministic route 仍然係佢嘅 baseline。

## Evidence Delta 令每次改動有得討論

「新 prompt 讀落順咗」唔係揀版本嘅理由。freeze source-shaped fixture 同 fixed case manifest，一次只改一樣嘢，然後逐 case compare baseline 同 candidate。

例如 `CHANGE-001` 留低咗一個曾經接受 forecast request 嘅 candidate，同一個會 reject 呢個 request 嘅新 candidate。comparison 只可以喺同一份 fixture 同 protocol 下講 `NO_DECLARED_REGRESSION`；呢句唔係 release approval。

每次改動至少要留低：

1. 改咗嘅 parser、schema、prompt 或 model version；
2. 每條 case 固定 input 同預期 boundary；
3. per-case diff，包括新 failure 或 unchanged result；
4. human reviewer 嘅 `KEEP`、`HOLD` 或 `REVERT` 決定；以及
5. 一個叫得出名嘅 rollback target。

source 適唔適合、packet 有冇 context、將來 release 可唔可以做，始終由人決定。test 可以證明一條 boundary 有守住，唔可以拎走呢啲 decision rights。

## 自己做 portfolio repo 時，應該放咩

唔好圍住 chatbot screen 擺證據；圍住個 decision 擺：

```text
data/source-receipt.md          source route、limits、freshness rule、excluded fields
data/fixture-manifest.json      synthetic fixture identity 同 schema version
schemas/context-packet.json     no-action output contract
src/validate-source.mjs         deterministic reject paths
src/build-packet.mjs            fact-preserving baseline
evals/cases.json                fixed normal 同 failure cases
scripts/evidence-delta.mjs      per-case comparison
CHANGE-001.md                   hypothesis、reviewer decision、rollback target
README.md                       commands、evidence map、limits、non-claims
```

你喺技術上展示 validation、schema、versioning、fixed evaluation 同 rollback；喺交付上展示 source rights、data minimisation、named decision owner 同 consequential action 前嘅 stop。 [NIST AI RMF Playbook](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework/nist-ai-rmf-playbook) 可以幫你討論角色同 documentation；呢度引用佢唔代表 compliance claim。

## 幾條要講清楚嘅 boundary

呢度冇 acquire 或 check currentness 嘅 live ABS data。冇一個數值係 ABS observation、public statistic、trend、forecast 或 causal conclusion。冇 employer、employee、candidate、salary、customer 或 operational data。冇 OpenAI request、model output、Promptfoo run、latency、cost、quality 或 safety result。

你可以由 portfolio planner 下載配套 English starter pack：入面有一張 `not acquired` source receipt、四行 invented monthly values、七個手動 cases 同 `CHANGE-001`，讓你由一份可核對的練習開始。佢唔係完整 local reference package，亦唔係 public repository。完整 reference package 暫時未有經核對嘅 GitHub URL，所以未能 clone；下載到嘅 starter pack 則有自己嘅本地 run 指引，亦唔代表完整 reference package。日後要發佈或者做 live-data pilot，仍然要由 owner 核對 data rights、source handling、human review 同 release authority。

延伸閱讀：[做一份 public-data KEV review packet](/zh-HK/articles/build-a-public-data-kev-review-packet)、[LLM Eval、Human Review 同 Observability](/zh-HK/articles/llm-evals-human-review-and-observability)、[由 offline evaluation 去到 authorised pilot](/zh-HK/articles/from-offline-evaluation-to-an-authorised-pilot)、[用 evidence 而唔係 fluency 評 portfolio](/zh-HK/articles/score-an-ai-portfolio-by-evidence-not-fluency)，同埋 [整一份 GitHub portfolio proof pack](/zh-HK/articles/build-a-github-portfolio-proof-pack)。
workforce-signal-brief.zh-TW:
> 這個 portfolio build 不是在預測勞動市場，而是在回答一個更小、也更實際的問題：一份來源資料夠不夠完整，能不能交給人看一份有邊界的 context brief？

## 真正要做的決定，比「AI 市場洞察」小得多

想像一位虛構的 workforce-planning research lead 收到一條公共統計來源。在寫 brief 以前，他只要判斷一件事：**這張 source receipt 是否完整到可以讓人 review 一份沒有外部 action 的資料包？**

這刻意不是「哪裡會增加職缺」、「公司應不應該招人」、「應該開多少薪資」或「一個人的下一步工作該怎麼選」。一張漂亮圖表或一段流暢文字，單靠自己回答不了任何一項。

[ABS Data API user guide](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/application-programming-interfaces-apis/data-api-user-guide)、[Labour Force, Australia release collection](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/labour/employment-and-unemployment/labour-force-australia) 與 [ABS citation guidance](https://www.abs.gov.au/how-cite-abs-sources) 是未來設計 acquisition 時可查核的官方路線，但不代表這個 learning package 曾經 fetch release、query API、選過 series，或使用過 current observation。

文中的情境、月度數值、receipt、cases 與 output 都是 source-shaped synthetic fixture。因此這個作品集只做一項誠實主張：展示未來 briefing workflow 的邊界可以怎樣被人檢查。

## 先寫 source receipt，不要先相信看起來合理的數字

source receipt 是一張短紀錄，讓 reviewer 看見什麼真的收到、什麼還沒證實。一張有用的 receipt 會寫下：

- 預定的官方來源路線與 citation key；
- 未來 owner 需要確認的 series identity、reference period、unit、adjustment 與 retrieval rule；
- 哪些 fields 可以進 packet，哪些 private 或 operational fields 必須 reject；
- freshness rule、schema version 與 fixture identity；以及
- 誰負責判斷 source suitability、interpretation 與任何未來的 release。

這個 local reference 使用虛構 geography，每個數值都標示為 `synthetic`；manifest 寫的是 `synthetic_source_shaped_not_live_acquired`，不是 current statistic。如果 receipt 不完整、超出自己定下的 freshness rule、period 亂序、沒有 unit，或出現 private field，正確結果是 reject，不是硬補一段聽起來合理的說明。

```text
source receipt + source-shaped synthetic series
  -> metadata、order、freshness、private-field checks
  -> CONTEXT_BRIEF_READY 或 SOURCE_REJECTED
  -> 給 human reviewer 的 no-action context packet
  -> fixed cases、change comparison、release/rollback evidence
```

`CONTEXT_BRIEF_READY` 只代表可以給人看一份範圍受限的 packet，不是 forecast、causal explanation、hiring recommendation、salary decision、個人職涯建議、policy recommendation、publication 或任何 external action。

## Model 前面先有一份 deterministic packet

最小 baseline 完全不需要 LLM。它只保留 allowlisted facts、清楚標示數值是 synthetic、計算簡單的 period-to-period difference，並留下 human reviewer 需要確認的問題。它不能自行補 trend、補 missing context，或把 difference 變成建議。

因此在 prose 進入系統以前，可以先固定下面的 cases：

| Case | 必須具備的行為 |
| --- | --- |
| Complete synthetic receipt | 回傳有 synthetic label 與 reviewer questions 的 context packet |
| Missing unit 或 unordered period | 在 build packet 前 reject |
| Stale receipt | reject，並指出是 freshness failure |
| Private field | reject，不可投影進 output |
| 藏在 source text 裡的 instruction | 不可改變 route |
| Forecast request | 拒絕要求，維持 no-action boundary |

這些才是 interviewer 或 reviewer 能追問的工程證據：data contract、allowed fields、reject path、result schema，以及改 prompt 或 parser 後仍穩定的 cases。它比一張漂亮答案的 screenshot 更有用。

## GPT-5 mini 與 Promptfoo 應該放在哪裡——又不該當成什麼

案例保留一個 optional `gpt-5-mini` Responses request shape，讓 reviewer 看見未來可能接入的 seam。它是 static、non-executing：沒有 API key、SDK call、network request 或 model output。[GPT-5 mini 文件](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5-mini) 描述 model surface，但完全不能證明這個 workforce use case 適合、安全、有效或 ready to release。

Promptfoo 也要分開理解。local fixture configuration 可以描述固定 input、assertions、result shape 與 deterministic provider，而完全不 call provider。另一份 optional Responses configuration 是未來的 execution choice，需要另外有 authority、key handling、data review、cost decision 與 release gate。[Promptfoo configuration guide](https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/configuration/guide/) 與 [OpenAI provider guide](https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/providers/openai/) 只是工具文件，不是本項目的 run result。

如果未來真的獲授權接 model，它只能收到 allowlisted packet、回傳 strict schema、保留 synthetic label；一旦 forecast、提出沒有 source 支持的 explanation、加入 private context 或建議 external action，就應該 reject。deterministic route 仍然是它的 baseline。

## Evidence Delta 讓每次改動可以討論

「新 prompt 讀起來比較順」不是選版本的理由。freeze source-shaped fixture 與 fixed case manifest，一次只改一件事，再逐 case compare baseline 和 candidate。

例如 `CHANGE-001` 留下了一個曾接受 forecast request 的 candidate，和一個會 reject 這個 request 的新版 candidate。comparison 只能在同一份 fixture 與 protocol 下寫 `NO_DECLARED_REGRESSION`；那句不是 release approval。

每次改動至少要保留：

1. 改動的 parser、schema、prompt 或 model version；
2. 每條 case 的固定 input 與預期 boundary；
3. per-case diff，包括新 failure 或 unchanged result；
4. human reviewer 的 `KEEP`、`HOLD` 或 `REVERT` 決定；以及
5. 一個叫得出名稱的 rollback target。

source 是否適合、packet 是否有 context、未來 release 能不能做，仍然由人決定。test 可以證明某條 boundary 有守住，不能拿走這些 decision rights。

## 自己做 portfolio repo 時，應該放什麼

不要圍著 chatbot screen 堆證據；要圍著這個 decision 建立：

```text
data/source-receipt.md          source route、limits、freshness rule、excluded fields
data/fixture-manifest.json      synthetic fixture identity 與 schema version
schemas/context-packet.json     no-action output contract
src/validate-source.mjs         deterministic reject paths
src/build-packet.mjs            fact-preserving baseline
evals/cases.json                fixed normal 與 failure cases
scripts/evidence-delta.mjs      per-case comparison
CHANGE-001.md                   hypothesis、reviewer decision、rollback target
README.md                       commands、evidence map、limits、non-claims
```

技術上，你展示 validation、schema、versioning、fixed evaluation 與 rollback；交付上，你展示 source rights、data minimisation、named decision owner，以及 consequential action 之前的 stop。[NIST AI RMF Playbook](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework/nist-ai-rmf-playbook) 可以協助討論角色與 documentation；在這裡引用它不是 compliance claim。

## 幾條必須說清楚的 boundary

這裡沒有 acquire 或 check currentness 的 live ABS data。沒有任何數值是 ABS observation、public statistic、trend、forecast 或 causal conclusion。沒有 employer、employee、candidate、salary、customer 或 operational data。沒有 OpenAI request、model output、Promptfoo run、latency、cost、quality 或 safety result。

你可以從 portfolio planner 下載配套 English starter pack：裡面有一張 `not acquired` source receipt、四行 invented monthly values、七個手動 cases 與 `CHANGE-001`，讓你從一份可核對的練習開始。它不是完整的 local reference package，也不是 public repository。完整 reference package 目前沒有經查核的 GitHub URL，所以不能 clone；下載的 starter pack 則有自己的本機 run 指引，也不代表完整 reference package。未來若要發布或做 live-data pilot，仍由 owner 確認 data rights、source handling、human review 與 release authority。

延伸閱讀：[做一份 public-data KEV review packet](/zh-TW/articles/build-a-public-data-kev-review-packet)、[LLM Eval、Human Review 與 Observability](/zh-TW/articles/llm-evals-human-review-and-observability)、[從 offline evaluation 到 authorised pilot](/zh-TW/articles/from-offline-evaluation-to-an-authorised-pilot)、[用 evidence 而不是 fluency 評 portfolio](/zh-TW/articles/score-an-ai-portfolio-by-evidence-not-fluency)，以及 [做一份 GitHub portfolio proof pack](/zh-TW/articles/build-a-github-portfolio-proof-pack)。

workforce-signal-brief.en:
> This portfolio build is not about predicting a labour market. It is about deciding whether a source is complete enough to enter a brief that a person can review.

## The useful decision is smaller than an “AI market insight”

Imagine a fictional workforce-planning research lead receiving a proposed public-statistics source. Before someone writes a context brief, the lead needs to answer one narrow question: **is this receipt complete enough for a human to inspect a bounded, no-action summary?**

That is deliberately not a question about where jobs are heading, what a company should hire, how much it should pay, or what someone should do next in their career. A tidy chart or fluent paragraph cannot answer any of those questions by itself.

The official [ABS Data API guide](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/application-programming-interfaces-apis/data-api-user-guide), [Labour Force, Australia release collection](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/labour/employment-and-unemployment/labour-force-australia), and [ABS citation guidance](https://www.abs.gov.au/how-cite-abs-sources) are useful routes to inspect when designing a future acquisition. They are not evidence that this learning package fetched a release, queried an API, selected a series, or used a current observation.

The scenario, monthly values, receipts, cases, and outputs described here are source-shaped synthetic fixtures. The project therefore makes a much more honest claim: it shows how to make the boundary around a future briefing workflow inspectable.

## Start with a source receipt, not a promising-looking number

A source receipt is the short record that lets a reviewer see what arrived and what has not been established. A useful one records:

- the intended official route and a citation key;
- the series identity, reference period, unit, adjustment, and retrieval rule a future owner would need to confirm;
- which fields may enter the packet and which private or operational fields must be rejected;
- a freshness rule, schema version, and fixture identity; and
- the human owner of source suitability, interpretation, and any later release decision.

The local example contains a fictional geography and synthetic values marked as synthetic. It records `synthetic_source_shaped_not_live_acquired`, not a current statistic. If the receipt is incomplete, stale under its declared rule, unordered, missing a unit, or carries a private field, the correct result is rejection—not a helpful-sounding recovery.

```text
source receipt + source-shaped synthetic series
  -> metadata, order, freshness, and private-field checks
  -> CONTEXT_BRIEF_READY or SOURCE_REJECTED
  -> no-action context packet for a human reviewer
  -> fixed cases, change comparison, release/rollback evidence
```

`CONTEXT_BRIEF_READY` is only permission to show a constrained packet to a person. It is not a forecast, causal explanation, hiring recommendation, salary decision, individual career advice, policy recommendation, publication, or external action.

## A deterministic packet comes before the optional model seam

The baseline has no need for an LLM. It preserves allowed facts, labels the values as synthetic, calculates only a simple period-to-period difference, and asks the reviewer what must be checked next. It cannot invent a trend, fill in missing context, or turn a difference into a recommendation.

That gives you clear cases to test before prose becomes part of the system:

| Case | Required behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Complete synthetic receipt | Return a context packet with synthetic labels and reviewer questions |
| Missing unit or unordered period | Reject before a packet is built |
| Stale receipt | Reject and name the freshness failure |
| Private field | Reject rather than project it into the output |
| Instruction hidden in source text | Keep source text from changing the route |
| Forecast request | Refuse the request and keep the no-action boundary |

This is engineering evidence a reviewer can follow: data contracts, allowed fields, rejection paths, result schemas, and cases that remain stable after a prompt or parser change. It is more useful than a screenshot of one polished answer.

## Where GPT-5 mini and Promptfoo fit—and where they do not

The example keeps an optional `gpt-5-mini` Responses request shape visible so that a reviewer can see a possible future seam. It is static and non-executing: no API key, SDK call, network request, or model output is included. The [GPT-5 mini documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5-mini) describes a model surface; it does not establish that this workforce use case is suitable, safe, effective, or ready to release.

The same separation applies to Promptfoo. A local fixture configuration can describe fixed inputs, assertions, result shapes, and a deterministic provider without calling a provider. A separate, optional Responses configuration is a future execution choice that needs its own authority, key handling, data review, cost decision, and release gate. The [Promptfoo configuration guide](https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/configuration/guide/) and [OpenAI provider guide](https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/providers/openai/) explain their tools; neither is a run result from this project.

If a model layer is later authorised, it should receive only the allowlisted packet, return a strict schema, retain the synthetic label, and be rejected whenever it forecasts, presents an unsupported explanation, introduces private context, or suggests an external action. The deterministic route remains the baseline against which it is judged.

## Evidence Delta makes a change discussable

“The new prompt reads better” is not enough to choose a version. Freeze the source-shaped fixture and fixed case manifest, change one thing, and compare the baseline and candidate case by case.

For example, `CHANGE-001` records a candidate that had accepted a forecast request and a later candidate that rejects it. A comparison can say `NO_DECLARED_REGRESSION` only when the same fixture and protocol apply. It does not approve a release.

For each change, keep:

1. the parser, schema, prompt, or model version that changed;
2. the fixed input and expected boundary for every case;
3. the per-case difference, including a new failure or unchanged result;
4. the human reviewer’s `KEEP`, `HOLD`, or `REVERT` decision; and
5. a named rollback target.

The person reviewing the source decides whether it is suitable, whether the packet is meaningful in context, and whether any future release is authorised. A test can show a boundary held; it cannot take those decisions away.

## What to place in your own portfolio repository

Build the evidence around the decision, not around a chatbot screen:

```text
data/source-receipt.md          source route, limits, freshness rule, excluded fields
data/fixture-manifest.json      synthetic fixture identity and schema version
schemas/context-packet.json     no-action output contract
src/validate-source.mjs         deterministic reject paths
src/build-packet.mjs            fact-preserving baseline
evals/cases.json                fixed normal and failure cases
scripts/evidence-delta.mjs      per-case comparison
CHANGE-001.md                   hypothesis, reviewer decision, rollback target
README.md                       commands, evidence map, limits, and non-claims
```

A reviewer can inspect validation, schemas, versioning, fixed evaluation, and rollback. Before anything affects a decision, the work must also state source rights, data minimisation, who owns the decision, and when to stop. The [NIST AI RMF Playbook](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework/nist-ai-rmf-playbook) is one way to discuss roles and documentation; using it here is not a compliance claim.

## Boundaries worth saying out loud

No live ABS data is acquired or checked for currentness here. No included value is an ABS observation, a public statistic, a trend, a forecast, or a causal conclusion. No employer, employee, candidate, salary, customer, or operational data appears. No OpenAI request, model output, Promptfoo run, latency, cost, quality, or safety result is shown.

You can download the accompanying English starter pack from the portfolio planner. It contains a `not acquired` source receipt, four invented monthly values, seven manual cases, and `CHANGE-001`, so you can begin with a reviewable exercise. It is not the full local reference package or a public repository. There is currently no verified GitHub URL for the full reference package, so it cannot be cloned. The downloadable starter has its own local run instructions and does not represent the full reference package. Publication or a live-data pilot remains an owner decision after data rights, source handling, human review, and release authority have been checked.

Related reading: [build a public-data KEV review packet](/en/articles/build-a-public-data-kev-review-packet), [LLM evals, human review, and observability](/en/articles/llm-evals-human-review-and-observability), [from offline evaluation to an authorised pilot](/en/articles/from-offline-evaluation-to-an-authorised-pilot), [score an AI portfolio by evidence, not fluency](/en/articles/score-an-ai-portfolio-by-evidence-not-fluency), and [build a GitHub portfolio proof pack](/en/articles/build-a-github-portfolio-proof-pack).

flagship-portfolio-architecture.zh-HK:
> 一個主力案例唔需要好大。它只需要令一個陌生人打開幾個檔案後，看得出你想幫誰處理哪個小決定、怎樣核對，以及你冇把本地練習講成真實成果。

## 主力案例唔係最多功能嗰個

作品集常見的卡位不是能力不足，而是同時起了三、四個半完成 project：一個 RAG chat、一次模型微調、一個 agent、再加一個漂亮介面。每個都可以 demo 幾分鐘，但沒有人能順著檔案追問你的取捨。

主力案例的工作反過來。你只揀一個有限的情境，然後把六樣本來散落在腦裏的資料寫出來。它不需要碰真實客戶、僱主資料或外部帳戶；合成資料或有清楚條款的公開資料已足夠做學習版本。重點不是把它講成企業系統，而是令 reviewer 能用同一條線看你的判斷。

如果仍未揀到題目，先用 [Portfolio Evidence Planner](/zh-HK/portfolio-evidence-planner) 寫出一位使用者、一個小決定、資料界線和一件不會做的事。唔好先由 model、framework 或職稱倒推題目。

## 先用一個問題篩走唔值得做的題目

把候選題目寫成一句：「一位 __ 在 __ 時，要根據 __ 決定 __；如果資料不足、過期或超出權限，就 __。」

例如，並不是「我想做一個 AI 文件助理」，而是「一位虛構 reviewer 收到一條資料更新時，要決定能否準備一份有來源的草稿；來源相撞或缺欄位，就停在交人處理。」這一句已經逼你選擇 owner、時間點、輸入、停止位和錯誤後果。

以下情況先唔好揀作主力案例：要靠未獲准的資料才有意思、只能靠漂亮輸出展示、或你連一個可能失敗的情境都想不到。這些不是「再加一個 agent」可以補救的問題。

## 六格：每格都要有檔案、核對方法和不能聲稱的結果

這六格不是叫你堆六份文件。每一格都對應一條追問。你可以先寫一頁很短的 Markdown；有實際改動時才把它長成 code、測試或紀錄。

| 格 | 留下甚麼 artefact | 別人怎樣核對 | 這格不可以聲稱甚麼 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 01 · 小決定 | `docs/problem-brief.md`，寫使用者、決定時間、錯誤代價、owner 和 non-goal。 | 讀者能用一句話說出工具幫誰作哪個有限決定，也知道誰保留最後決定權。 | 不代表有真實需求、客戶、授權或採用。 |
| 02 · 資料界線 | `docs/data-receipt.md`、schema 和一小份 synthetic 或公開 fixture。 | 能分辨資料由哪裏來、哪些欄位可用、哪些必須排除、資料是哪個版本。 | 不代表你有真實資料存取權、私隱批准或仍然新鮮的 live data。 |
| 03 · 簡單起點 | `src/baseline.*` 和 `docs/baseline-and-change.md`，記下最簡單做法和一次刻意改動。 | 同一個 input 可走 baseline 和 candidate；讀者能指出改了甚麼和為何要改。 | 不代表 candidate 在真實工作裏較好，也不代表較複雜就較有價值。 |
| 04 · 固定情境 | `eval/cases.*`、預期 route 和 failure log。 | 至少可看到正常、資料不足、過期或衝突、越界要求和 regression case 的預期處理。 | 不代表統計 benchmark、全面安全測試或任何認證。 |
| 05 · 停低和回退 | `docs/reviewer-decision.md` 和 `docs/rollback.md`，寫 `KEEP`、`REVISE` 或 `STOP` 的條件。 | 別人能知道哪個失敗會擋住改動、誰作決定，以及怎樣回到前一個可用方法。 | 不代表已得到 release、部署、資安或合規批准。 |
| 06 · 交代給下一個人 | `README.md`、最小 run command、`docs/five-minute-walkthrough.md` 和 claims note。 | 一位陌生人能找到入口、明白本地結果從何而來，並聽你講清一個 failure。 | 不代表公開 repository 已存在、每行 code 都是你獨自寫成，或 project 足以保證求職結果。 |

第 03 格特別重要。沒有 baseline 時，你只是在展示「某個組合可以跑」。有了同一批 input 的簡單對照，才可以討論新元件究竟補了哪個 failure，又帶來甚麼成本或新風險。

第 04 格亦唔好只放成功 screenshot。固定情境的價值在於你改 prompt、retrieval、rule 或 model 後，仍可看見舊問題有冇回來。一次本機 pass 只證明該次本機檢查；它不是 live system 的成績單。

## 先把一格做實，再開下一格

這張表最容易被誤用成「今晚要補齊所有文件」。較好的做法是讓每次工作都令一格由空白變成可打開：

1. 先完成第 01 和 02 格，否則你不知道自己可以用甚麼資料和不能做甚麼。
2. 做出第 03 和 04 格的最小版本；保留一個 baseline、一個改動和同一批 cases。
3. 最後補第 05 和 06 格，令改動有人可以 review，令你自己幾星期後仍講得返。

想看一個由舊快照排人手隊列的例子，可讀 [Renewal Triage](/zh-HK/articles/renewal-triage-mlops)。它有意把模型分數、隊列行為和真實挽留結果分開。想從一個草稿流程開始，可在 [Build Lab](/zh-HK/labs#build-lab-kit-renewal-triage-mlops) 揀一個本地練習；內容本身不會替你接入帳戶、資料或真實工作流程。

## 第二個 project 甚麼時候先有理由開始

第二個 project 並不是第一個畫面看膩了就開始。至少先問三條問題：

- **它有沒有另一個決定？** 把同一個 FAQ 換 prompt、換 model 或換介面，不算另一個 case。由「可否草擬回覆」轉到「有限 capacity 下先 review 哪一條」，才是不同決定。

開始前可抄一份 [Portfolio Proof Pack](/zh-HK/articles/build-a-github-portfolio-proof-pack) 的文件結構，再把每一格連到一個檔案。之後打開 [Interview Lab](/zh-HK/interview-lab)，揀一題和你案例最接近的題目。回答時不用重複 README；只要按這條次序講：哪個決定、最簡單做法、哪個 case 逼你改、怎樣停下，以及那次本地練習仍未知甚麼。

若想先檢查自己有沒有遺漏，也可對照 [作品集 evidence review](/zh-HK/articles/score-an-ai-portfolio-by-evidence-not-fluency)。它會幫你找下一個缺口；這篇則幫你避免把缺口分散到幾個半完成 project。

## 先让一格站得住，再开下一格

这张表最容易被误解成“今晚要补齐所有文件”。更好的做法是让每次工作都把一格从空白变成能打开的东西：

1. 先完成第 01 与 02 格，否则你不知道自己能用什么数据、不能做什么。
2. 做出第 03 与 04 格的最小版本；保留一个 baseline、一项改动与同一批 cases。
3. 最后补第 05 与 06 格，让改动有人能 review，也让你几周后仍说得回来。

想看一个从旧快照排人工队列的例子，可读 [Renewal Triage](/zh-Hans/articles/renewal-triage-mlops)。它刻意把模型分数、队列行为与真实挽留结果分开。想从草稿流程开始，可在 [Build Lab](/zh-Hans/labs#build-lab-kit-renewal-triage-mlops) 选一个本地练习；内容本身不会替你连接账户、数据或真实工作流程。

## 第二个 project 什么时候才有理由开始

第二个 project 不是第一个画面看腻了就开始。至少先问三个问题：

- **它有没有另一个决定？** 把同一个 FAQ 换 prompt、换 model 或换界面，不算另一个 case。从“能否草拟回复”转到“有限 capacity 下先 review 哪一条”，才是不同决定。
- **它有没有另一种失败方式？** 例如 retrieval project 要处理来源、版本与无根据回答；时间序列或 queue project 要处理数据可用时间、capacity 与 threshold。只换主题颜色不会增加你能展示的判断。
- **第一个是否已有一轮完整回应？** 六格每格至少有一件能打开的东西，而且你已根据同一批 cases 接受、修改或放弃过一次改动，才值得把注意力转走。

PolicyPilot 与 Renewal Triage 可以是一对好对照，不是因为名称更大，而是它们的问题不同：前者着重来源支持的草稿与交人；后者着重时间安全的数据、排序与 reviewer capacity。你可从 [PolicyPilot](/zh-Hans/articles/enterprise-ai-portfolio-policy-pilot) 读另一种有限 case，但别把两者混成一句“我做过 enterprise AI”。

## 把六格变成面试时说得出的路线

开始前可参考 [Portfolio Proof Pack](/zh-Hans/articles/build-a-github-portfolio-proof-pack) 的文件结构，再把每一格连到一个文件。接着打开 [Interview Lab](/zh-Hans/interview-lab)，选一道与你案例最接近的题目。回答时不用重复 README；按这个顺序说就好：哪个决定、最简单做法、哪个 case 逼你修改、怎样停下，以及那次本地练习仍不知道什么。

想先检查自己漏了什么，也可对照 [作品集 evidence review](/zh-Hans/articles/score-an-ai-portfolio-by-evidence-not-fluency)。它能帮你找下一个缺口；这篇则帮你避免把缺口分散到几个半完成 project。

## 这份地图的边界

这是一份学习用架构，不会建立 GitHub repository、不会公开数据、不会替你执行 model call，也不会让本地 fixture 变成真实业务结果。使用雇主、客户、同学或任何个人数据前，仍要由有权的人确认用途、权限、保存与公开范围。

一个主力案例的价值，是让别人不必相信你说“我做过 AI”，也能沿着你留下的六格，看到你在哪里缩小问题、怎样检查、何时停止，以及哪些问题仍未有答案。

> A flagship case does not need to be large. It needs to let a stranger open a few files and see the small decision you are supporting, how you checked it, and what your local exercise does not establish.

## A flagship case is not the project with the most features

The usual portfolio problem is not a lack of ability. It is three or four half-finished projects at once: a RAG chat, a fine-tune, an agent, and a polished interface. Each can be demonstrated for a few minutes, but none gives a reviewer a clear path to ask about your choices.

Work in the other direction. Pick one bounded situation and write down the six things that are otherwise scattered across your head. You do not need customer data, employer data, or an external account to make a learning version. Synthetic material or public material with clear terms is enough. The point is not to present it as an enterprise system. The point is to let a reviewer follow one line of reasoning.

If you have not chosen a case, start with the [Portfolio Evidence Planner](/en/portfolio-evidence-planner). Name one user, one small decision, a data boundary, and one thing the system deliberately will not do. Do not start with a model, framework, or job title and work backwards.

## Use one sentence to reject a weak project idea

Write a candidate like this: “A __ needs to decide __ from __ at __; if the material is missing, stale, or out of scope, the system __.”

That is different from “I want to build an AI document assistant.” For example: “A fictional reviewer receives a source update and decides whether a source-grounded draft can be prepared; conflicting sources or missing fields stop at human review.” The sentence forces you to choose an owner, timing, input, stop point, and cost of error.

Do not make this your flagship case if it only works with data you are not allowed to use, if a polished output is its only demonstration, or if you cannot name one way it could fail. Adding another agent will not repair any of those problems.

## Six rows: every row has an artefact, a check, and a nonclaim

The six rows are not an instruction to collect six documents. Each row answers a reasonable follow-up question. Start with a short Markdown file; grow it into code, tests, or records only when there is a real change to show.

| Row | Artefact to leave behind | What a reviewer can check | What this row does not establish |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 01 · Small decision | `docs/problem-brief.md` with the user, decision time, cost of error, owner, and non-goal. | A reader can say who the tool helps with which limited decision, and who retains the final call. | It does not prove real demand, a customer, permission, or adoption. |
| 02 · Data boundary | `docs/data-receipt.md`, a schema, and a small synthetic or public fixture. | The source, allowed fields, excluded fields, and data version are clear. | It does not prove access to real data, privacy approval, or that live data is current. |
| 03 · Simple starting point | `src/baseline.*` and `docs/baseline-and-change.md`, recording the simplest approach and one deliberate change. | The same input can run through a baseline and a candidate; the reader can identify what changed and why. | It does not prove that the candidate is better in real work, or that more complexity adds value. |
| 04 · Fixed situations | `eval/cases.*`, expected routes, and a failure log. | Ordinary, missing-data, stale-or-conflicting, out-of-scope, and regression cases have an expected response. | It does not prove a statistical benchmark, comprehensive safety testing, or certification. |
| 05 · Stop and return | `docs/reviewer-decision.md` and `docs/rollback.md`, with `KEEP`, `REVISE`, or `STOP` conditions. | A reviewer can find the failure that blocks a change, the person who decides, and the earlier method to return to. | It does not prove release, deployment, security, or compliance approval. |
| 06 · Hand-off map | `README.md`, the smallest run command, `docs/five-minute-walkthrough.md`, and a claims note. | A stranger can find the entry point, understand where the local result came from, and hear you explain one failure. | It does not prove a public repository exists, that every line was written alone, or that the project guarantees an employment outcome. |

Row 03 matters more than it looks. Without a baseline, you can only show that one combination runs. With a simple comparison on the same inputs, you can discuss which failure a new component was meant to address, and which cost or risk it introduced.

Do not fill Row 04 with successful screenshots. Its value is that, after you change a prompt, retrieval step, rule, or model, you can see whether an earlier problem returned. One passing local check proves only that local check. It is not a scorecard for a live system.

## Make one row real before opening the next one

The table is easy to misread as “finish every document tonight.” A better rhythm is to move one row at a time from blank to openable:

1. Complete Rows 01 and 02 first. Otherwise you do not know which material you may use or which actions must stay out of scope.
2. Build the smallest Row 03 and 04 pair: one baseline, one change, and the same cases.
3. Add Rows 05 and 06 so a change can be reviewed and you can still explain it a few weeks later.

For a worked case that orders a human-review queue from an earlier snapshot, read [Renewal Triage](/en/articles/renewal-triage-mlops). It deliberately separates a model score, queue behaviour, and real retention results. To begin from a small local exercise, choose a case in the [Build Lab](/en/labs#build-lab-kit-renewal-triage-mlops); the page itself does not connect an account, data source, or real workflow for you.

## When a second project is actually justified

Do not start a second project because you are tired of the first screen. Ask three questions instead:

- **Does it support a different decision?** Changing the prompt, model, or interface for the same FAQ does not make a new case. Moving from “can a draft be prepared?” to “which record should be reviewed first when capacity is limited?” does.
- **Does it fail in a different way?** A retrieval case must handle sources, versions, and unsupported answers. A time-based or queue case must handle data availability, capacity, and thresholds. A new colour palette does not add a new kind of reasoning.
- **Has the first case received a full response loop?** Every row has at least one openable item, and you have kept, revised, or rejected a change against the same cases. Only then is it worth moving attention away.

PolicyPilot and Renewal Triage make a useful pair because their problems differ, not because their names sound larger. The first concentrates on a source-supported draft and human handoff; the second on time-safe data, ordering, and reviewer capacity. Read [PolicyPilot](/en/articles/enterprise-ai-portfolio-policy-pilot) for the other kind of bounded case, but do not collapse both into “I built enterprise AI.”

## Turn the six rows into an answer you can give in an interview

Use the document layout in the [Portfolio Proof Pack](/en/articles/build-a-github-portfolio-proof-pack), then point each row to a real file. Next, open the [Interview Lab](/en/interview-lab) and choose a question close to your case. You do not need to recite a README. Walk through the decision, the simplest approach, the case that made you change it, how it stops, and what the local exercise still leaves unknown.

If you want a gap check first, compare your work with the [portfolio evidence review](/en/articles/score-an-ai-portfolio-by-evidence-not-fluency). It helps identify the next missing piece; this guide helps prevent those pieces from being scattered across several half-finished projects.

## Boundary of this guide

This is a learning architecture. It does not create a GitHub repository, publish data, run a model call, or turn a local fixture into a business outcome. Before using employer, client, classmate, or personal data, the person with authority still needs to confirm the purpose, permission, retention, and publication boundary.

The value of one flagship case is that nobody has to take “I built AI” on trust. They can follow the six rows and see where you narrowed the problem, how you checked it, when you stopped, and which questions remain unanswered.
